### Локальный CPUID-профиль `DiagnosticV1` (S2-26a)

`DiagnosticV1` — узкий диагностический profile для одной bare-инструкции
`0F A2` (`CPUID`) в режиме Long64. Его явное назначение в profile обязательно;
неявный/default profile и вызов через legacy API отвергаются fail closed.
Для vendor/identity, topology и ширин физических/линейных адресов профиль
сохраняет выбранные значения neutral Ubuntu target ниже. Feature masks и boot
guarantees от него не наследуются: все feature masks `DiagnosticV1` равны
нулю. Профиль не представляет x86-64-v1 CPU и не является Ubuntu/Linux boot
contract.

| Input EAX | EAX | EBX | ECX | EDX | Разрешённое значение |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `0` | `0x00000001` | ASCII `Open` | ASCII `top ` | ASCII `Desk` | Максимальный basic leaf и vendor identity; vendor bytes в порядке EBX/EDX/ECX дают `OpenDesktop `. |
| `1` | `0x00000600` | `0x00000100` | `0` | `0` | Версия/type и один логический процессор, APIC ID 0; все feature masks равны нулю. |
| `0x80000000` | `0x80000008` | `0` | `0` | `0` | Максимальный extended leaf. |
| `0x80000001` | `0` | `0` | `0` | `0` | Feature masks остаются нулевыми. |
| `0x80000002..0x80000007` | `0` | `0` | `0` | `0` | Нулевые ответы. |
| `0x80000008` | `0x00003024` | `0` | `0` | `0` | Физическая ширина адреса 36 бит, линейная ширина 48 бит. |
| Любой другой leaf | `0` | `0` | `0` | `0` | Нулевой ответ. |

Input ECX/subleaf игнорируется. Для leaf 1 EBX содержит только топологические
поля выше; ECX и EDX, а также feature-bearing поля всех остальных ответов,
нулевые. Ни один CPUID feature bit не объявляется. Любой префикс запрещён:
точная форма `F0 0F A2` (`LOCK CPUID`) даёт `#UD`, а остальные prefix-bearing
формы возвращают `Unsupported`. JIT/native/physical execution для профиля не
допускается. Это нормативная граница S2-26a. Реализация и local interpreter
checks внесены в [отчёт этапа 2](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-26a--локальный-diagnosticv1-cpuid);
независимое review завершено. Это не подтверждает physical execution
или требования загрузки ОС.

### Локальный probe-профиль `SysenterProbeV1` (S2-26b)

`MsrProfile::SysenterProbeV1` — immutable CPU-side policy для выбранного
synthetic target `od-x86-64-v1-neutral-v0.1`. Он исполняет только точные bare
Long64 формы `0F 32` (`RDMSR`) и `0F 30` (`WRMSR`) и только при явно выбранном
профиле. Индекс берётся из `ECX[31:0]`; `RCX[63:32]` игнорируется. Для ровно
`0x174`, `0x175` и `0x176` обе формы синтетически возвращают `#GP(0)` при CPL0
и CPL1–3. Это CPU-side fault decision из уже выбранной политики target, а не
общая реализация x86 MSR или утверждение о поведении всех x86 CPU. Любой другой
индекс имеет результат `Unsupported` и не делает заявления о его архитектурном
поведении.

Точные `F0 0F 32` и `F0 0F 30` дают `#UD` только после успешного fetch всех
трёх байтов; усечённый fetch имеет приоритет и сохраняет fetch fault.
Остальные prefix-bearing формы возвращают `Unsupported`, также после
необходимого fetch для классификации. Legacy API paths отвергают профиль
fail closed. В этом срезе нет успешного чтения/записи MSR: fault не возвращает
значение `RDMSR`, не записывает значение `WRMSR`, не моделирует `-EIO` или
Linux exception-table fixup, не доставляет guest `#GP`, не меняет CPU state,
не вызывает data-memory callbacks и не retire-ит инструкцию. Он не подтверждает
наблюдение Linux safe-write fixup или загрузку Linux. JIT/native/physical
admission остаётся закрытым; Mac mini проверки отложены до общего финального
substage. Реализация, local evidence и повторное независимое review S2-26b
зафиксированы в
[отчёте этапа 2](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-26b--локальный-sysenterprobev1-msr-probe).

### Локальный профиль `GsBaseV1` (S2-26c)

`MsrProfile::GsBaseV1` — отдельный immutable profile для одного MSR
`IA32_GS_BASE` (`0xC0000101`). Он не расширяет `SysenterProbeV1`: каждый
профиль принимает только собственный набор индексов, а legacy API и неизвестные
индексы остаются fail closed. Допускаются только bare Long64 `0F 32`
(`RDMSR`) и `0F 30` (`WRMSR`) с индексом `ECX[31:0] == 0xC0000101`.

При CPL0 `RDMSR` возвращает текущее 64-битное значение `gs_base` в `EDX:EAX`;
`WRMSR` берёт значение из `EDX:EAX` и успешно записывает его только если оно
48-bit canonical (биты 63:48 совпадают с битом 47). Неканоническая запись даёт
`#GP(0)` и не меняет состояние. При CPL1–3 обе операции дают `#GP(0)` без
изменения состояния. Успешный `WRMSR` меняет только `gs_base`; он не изменяет
GS selector или hidden GS descriptor cache и не изменяет `fs_base`, FS selector
или hidden FS descriptor cache. `RDMSR` не изменяет эти поля и `gs_base`.
Другие индексы не получают MSR semantics от этого профиля.

Выбор canonical48 — фиксированная политика этого профиля, согласованная с
выбранным 48-bit linear target; это не обобщение на процессоры с другой
шириной linear address. В Intel SDM Vol. 3A §§2.8.10 и 4.5.3 описаны 32-bit
индекс RDMSR/WRMSR в 64-bit mode и проверки canonicality при WRMSR к
IA32_GS_BASE: [официальный Intel SDM Vol. 3A](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/technical/intel-sdm.html).

Профиль не меняет нулевые feature masks CPUID `DiagnosticV1` и не заявляет
Linux boot, Linux fixup или guest `#GP` delivery. JIT/native/physical admission
не допускается. Local evidence и независимое Sol medium review S2-26c
завершены; Mac mini проверки отложены до общего финального substage. Матрица
реализации и проверки указана в
[плане](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-26c--локальный-gsbasev1-msr) и будет отражена в
[отчёте этапа 2](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-26c--локальный-gsbasev1-msr).

### Локальный профиль `FsBaseV1` (S2-26f)

`MsrProfile::FsBaseV1` независимо покрывает только `IA32_FS_BASE`
(`0xC0000100`), не расширяя `GsBaseV1` или `SysenterProbeV1`. Допущены только
bare Long64 `0F 32` и `0F 30`; индекс берётся из `ECX[31:0]`. Профиль фиксирует
linear-address width 48 и не включает LA57, LAM или VMX. CPL0 `RDMSR` возвращает
`fs_base` в `EDX:EAX` с zero-extension 32-bit результатов; CPL0 `WRMSR`
собирает только низкие 32-bit половины `EDX:EAX` и принимает только
canonical48 значение. CPL1–3 и noncanonical48 запись дают CPU-side `#GP(0)` без
state mutation, retirement или data-memory callback. Успешная запись меняет
только `fs_base`; FS selector/cache attributes и flags сохраняются. Успешная
инструкция продвигает RIP на 2 и считается завершённой один раз.

Неизвестный индекс, legacy API и отсутствие выбранного профиля остаются
`Unsupported`. Профиль самостоятельный и не включает GS/SYSENTER policy. По
Rev. 093 правила MSR описаны в инструкциях `RDMSR`/`WRMSR` Vol. 2, а проверки
`IA32_FS_BASE` canonicality — Vol. 3A §2.8.10 и §4.5.3:
[официальный Intel SDM](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/technical/intel-sdm.html).
Указанный scope не утверждает Linux boot/runtime, exception delivery,
JIT/native execution или физическую проверку.

### Локальный профиль `KernelGsBaseV1` (S2-26g)

`MsrProfile::KernelGsBaseV1` независимо принимает только `IA32_KERNEL_GS_BASE`
(`ECX[31:0] == 0xC0000102`) и bare Long64 `0F 32`/`0F 30`. CPL0 `RDMSR`
возвращает явное `kernel_gs_base` в `EDX:EAX` с zero-extension 32-bit частей;
CPL0 `WRMSR` собирает значение только из низких EAX/EDX и изменяет только
`kernel_gs_base`, если результат canonical48. Начальное состояние обязано
содержать `Some(base)`, включая допустимое `Some(0)`; отсутствующее значение
не подменяется нулём. CPL1–3 и noncanonical48 WRMSR дают CPU-side `#GP(0)` без
изменения состояния, retirement или data-memory callbacks. Успешная операция
продвигает RIP на 2 и retire-ится один раз. Неизвестный индекс и legacy API
остаются Unsupported; этот профиль не расширяет другие MSR profiles.

Fixture-профиль `s2-long-msr-kernel-gs-base-v1` отдельно выбирает MSR policy и
SWAPGS policy только для четырёх точных программ: `0F 32`, `0F 30`,
`0F 30 0F 01 F8 0F 32`, и `0F 30 0F 01 F8 65 48 8B 00`. Последние две
проверяют, что SWAPGS видит значение, записанное в kernel GS base, а следующий
RDMSR/GS-load использует бывшую активную GS base/новую активную GS base.
Обычный `run_with_msr_profile` сам по себе не включает SWAPGS.

Нормативные правила MSR и canonical checks основаны на Intel SDM Rev. 093,
Vol. 2 `RDMSR`/`WRMSR` и Vol. 3A §§2.8.10, 4.5.3; обмен активного GS base с
IA32_KERNEL_GS_BASE — на Vol. 2B `SWAPGS` pp. 4-697–4-698 и Vol. 3A FRED
ограничении. Источники: [официальный Intel SDM](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/technical/intel-sdm.html),
[Vol. 2B Rev. 093 PDF](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/929354/253667-093-sdm-vol-2b.pdf).
Профиль предполагает CS.L=1, FRED disabled, canonical48, no VMX/SMM и не
утверждает JIT/native/C ABI, Linux runtime или физическую проверку.

### Локальная политика `SepDisabledV1` (S2-26d)

`SepProfile::SepDisabledV1` — отдельная immutable CPU-side policy для выбранной
синтетической цели с `SEP=0`. Только точные bare Long64 `0F 34` (`SYSENTER`) и
`0F 35` (`SYSEXIT`) распознаются как эти операции; после полного fetch оба дают
`#UD` (vector 6, no error code) при CPL0–3. Решение не зависит от CPL и не
исполняет переход: оно не retire-ит инструкцию и не меняет RIP, регистры,
RFLAGS/definedness, RAM или другую state. Вызовов data-memory API нет.

Без явного профиля legacy `step`/`run` оставляют точные формы `Unsupported`.
Префиксы, иные режимы и соседние формы не расширяются этим slice; неизвестные
или не точные варианты остаются `Unsupported` после успешного fetch, если
отдельный существующий decoder contract не определяет их иначе. Ошибка fetch
сохраняет исходный класс и payload и имеет приоритет над `#UD`. Проверки stop и
zero budget остаются до fetch. JIT, native runner и C adapter не допускаются;
никаких SEP/CPUID bits не объявляется, `DiagnosticV1` identity/leaves и нулевые
feature masks не меняются. Это не задаёт `#UD` delivery, Linux fixup или
наблюдение на физическом процессоре.

Нормативный источник — Intel SDM revision 093, Vol. 2B, записи SYSENTER и
SYSEXIT: opcode forms `0F 34`/`0F 35`, availability indicated by the SEP
feature flag. Для выбранной цели SEP явно равен нулю, поэтому узкая local
policy принимает решение `#UD`; проект не заявляет всеобщую x86 семантику
для произвольных профилей. Нормативный текст находится в
[Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2B PDF](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/929354/253667-093-sdm-vol-2b.pdf).
Implementation evidence и
границы проверок: [план S2-26d](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-26d--local-sepdisabledv1-sysentersysexit-policy),
[отчёт](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-26d--local-sepdisabledv1-sysentersysexit-policy).

### Локальный профиль `RdtscSourceV1` (S2-26e)

`RDTSC` исполняется только для точной bare Long64 кодировки `0F 31` в
явном профиле `s2-long-rdtsc-v1`. Ни prefixes, ни соседние инструкции,
режимы или implicit/default API этим профилем не принимаются. `CR4.TSD` —
неизменяемый явный вход профиля; CPL берётся из существующего
`AccessContext`. При `CR4.TSD=1` и CPL1–3 операция даёт CPU-side `#GP(0)` после
полного fetch без retirement, изменения CPU state или вызова источника. В
остальных разрешённых случаях injected TSC source вызывается ровно один раз;
его младшие 32 бита zero-extend в EAX, старшие 32 — в EDX. RIP продвигается на
два байта; остальные архитектурные регистры, flags и память сохраняются.

Host clock не читается и не выбирается автоматически: caller обязан передать
источник. Fixture profile фиксирует исходное 64-bit значение и ожидаемое число
вызовов; результат отражает фактическое число вызовов. Legacy APIs без
одновременно явных controls/source остаются fail-closed (`Unsupported`).
JIT, native runner, C adapter и physical execution остаются закрытыми.
Generic amd64 target и существующие CPUID masks этим локальным контрактом не
меняются. Это CPU-side decision, не доставка `#GP`, не claim о синхронизации
или физическом измерении TSC.

Нормативный источник — Intel SDM revision 093, Vol. 2B, RDTSC,
pp. 4-559–560 ([официальный Intel PDF](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/929354/253667-093-sdm-vol-2b.pdf)).
Реализация, fixtures и local checks описаны в
[плане S2-26e](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-26e--точный-rdtsc-с-явным-tsc-источником) и
[отчёте этапа](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-26e--точный-rdtsc-с-явным-tsc-источником).

### Ubuntu Generic `amd64`: `od-x86-64-v1-neutral-v0.1`

Связь принятого target и таблицы A–D с local slices, tests/oracles и оставшейся приёмкой сверена в существующей [матрице S2-00/S2-40a](../reports/STAGE_2_LINUX_PROFILE.md#s2-40a--матрица-требований-ubuntu-generic-amd64). Это документационный inventory, который не расширяет capabilities и не объявляет полный C/D inventory или Stage 2 завершёнными.

Это выбранная синтетическая reference-цель для последующего CPU контракта и diagnostic Linux boot analysis. Она задаёт x86-64-v1 ABI/ISA floor и перечисленные дополнительные machine capabilities; она не является обещанием, что движок уже реализует эти функции, и не подтверждает совместимость или загрузку Ubuntu. Общий ABI floor остаётся x86-64-v1; v2/v3/v4 исключены. `PSE`, `TSC`, `MSR`, `PAE`, `CX8`, `APIC`, `PGE`, `PAT`, `NX` и `SYSCALL` ниже выбраны для этой project target отдельно и не выводятся все из одного psABI floor.

| CPUID input | EAX | EBX | ECX | EDX |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `CPUID(0)` | `0x00000001` | ASCII `Open` | ASCII `top ` | ASCII `Desk` |
| `CPUID(1)` | `0x00000600` | `0x00000100` (one logical CPU, APIC ID 0, brand index and CLFLUSH size 0) | `0x00000000` | `0x0781A379` |
| `CPUID(0x80000000)` | `0x80000008` | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `CPUID(0x80000001)` | 0 | 0 | 0 | `0x20100800` |
| `CPUID(0x80000002..0x80000007)` | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `CPUID(0x80000008)` | `0x00003024` | 0 | 0 | 0 |

The Generic amd64 CPUID target advertises TSC as selected above; that target
capability is separate from local execution support. S2-26e implements only
the exact interpreter profile and caller-injected source described above; it
does not provide a machine-wide clock or alter CPUID advertisement.

The CPUID.0 vendor bytes in architectural EBX/EDX/ECX order form `OpenDesktop ` (12 ASCII bytes). CPUID.1 EDX advertises FPU, PSE, TSC, MSR, PAE, CX8, APIC, PGE, CMOV, PAT, MMX, FXSR, SSE and SSE2; SEP is clear. CPUID.1 ECX is zero (including no XSAVE, OSXSAVE, AVX, or hypervisor-present bit). CPUID.80000001 EDX advertises SYSCALL, NX and long mode. CPUID.80000008 reports physical-address width 36 and linear-address width 48. Any unlisted EAX function returns four zero registers. This table is the selected project target, not a claim that these values came from an existing physical CPU.

For CPUID, the input ECX is ignored for every listed function in this profile; unlisted EAX function numbers return four zero registers irrespective of ECX. XSAVE/XRSTOR and XGETBV/XSETBV are outside this target; CR4.OSXSAVE must remain clear. Legacy x87/MMX/XMM state and FXSAVE/FXRSTOR remain in scope as required by the selected Linux startup path. SEP=0; the explicit S2-26d `SepDisabledV1` local policy raises CPU-side `#UD` for exact bare SYSENTER/SYSEXIT after complete fetch. It does not model exception delivery or settle Linux behavior. Linux 7.0's `idt_syscall_init` calls `wrmsrq_safe` for IA32_SYSENTER_CS/ESP/EIP (`0x174..0x176`) in both `ia32_enabled()` branches, without guarding those writes on SEP; the calls are listed in authenticated Ubuntu `arch/x86/kernel/cpu/common.c:2265–2285` ([upstream v7.0 source](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v7.0/arch/x86/kernel/cpu/common.c#L2121-L2141)). The exact Ubuntu config has `CONFIG_PARAVIRT_XXL=y`: `arch/x86/include/asm/paravirt.h:159–161,186–188` routes the safe write through its MSR operation, and the default `pv_ops` table in `arch/x86/kernel/paravirt.c:116` binds that operation to `native_write_msr_safe` ([paravirt.h](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v7.0/arch/x86/include/asm/paravirt.h#L149-L176), [paravirt.c](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v7.0/arch/x86/kernel/paravirt.c#L98-L108)). The native wrapper installs `EX_TYPE_WRMSR_SAFE` in the exception table (`arch/x86/include/asm/msr.h:144–156`); `EX_TYPE_WRMSR_SAFE` identifies the `-EIO` failure result, and `arch/x86/mm/extable.c:188–191,346–347` sets that result and resumes at the fixup IP ([msr.h](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v7.0/arch/x86/include/asm/msr.h#L134-L146), [extable_fixup_types.h](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v7.0/arch/x86/include/asm/extable_fixup_types.h#L40), [extable.c](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v7.0/arch/x86/mm/extable.c#L154-L178)). For this synthetic target, the selected CPU-side policy for RDMSR/WRMSR to those indices is a `#GP(0)` decision without state change, as specified by the `SysenterProbeV1` profile above. This is not a statement about all x86 CPUs, guest `#GP` delivery, or execution of Linux safe-write fixup. Static source reachability does not show that the call or fixup was observed at runtime. The bounded S2-26c `GsBaseV1` and S2-26f `FsBaseV1` local profiles cover individual FS/GS-base operations only. The broader MSR set (including EFER, STAR/LSTAR/SFMASK, CSTAR and conditional startup probes), initial control/segment/table/FPU state, alternatives, initramfs and boot success milestone still require a versioned execution manifest and implementation checks.

The choice uses the exact Ubuntu 7.0.0-38.38 source/binary mapping in [S2-00 Linux profile evidence](../reports/STAGE_2_LINUX_PROFILE.md#exact-source-to-binary-mapping--28-октября-2026); static evidence does not prove any runtime branch or guest boot. Windows CPU profile remains unselected. The x86-64-v1 baseline decision and its evidence are described in [GUEST_REQUIREMENTS.md](GUEST_REQUIREMENTS.md).

### S6-14a — bounded AP startup trampoline profile

This is the CPU profile for one statically selected AP startup path of Ubuntu
Generic `amd64` package `7.0.0-38.38`. It is an AP-only extension to
`od-x86-64-v1-neutral-v0.1`; it does not change the firmware entry contract.
The evidence is the linked `real_mode_blob` extracted from the staged image,
re-decoded on a physical x86 host, and recorded in the
[S6-02 inventory](../reports/data/stage6/ap-start-inventory.json) and
[physical decode report](../reports/data/stage6/s6-02-x86-reverification.md).
The byte-level decode rows that define the closed instruction-form allowlist
are preserved in the report's [real-16](../reports/data/stage6/s6-02-x86/16bit-objdump.txt),
[protected-32](../reports/data/stage6/s6-02-x86/32bit-objdump.txt),
[long-mode trampoline](../reports/data/stage6/s6-02-x86/64bit-objdump.txt),
and the [common verify](../reports/data/stage6/s6-02-x86/common-verify-objdump.txt)
and [common no-verify](../reports/data/stage6/s6-02-x86/common-no-verify-objdump.txt)
outputs. The table below selects the instruction rows by the stated control-flow
and target predicates; the raw outputs also contain unselected branches and
alignment bytes, which are not thereby admitted to this profile.
The static inventory establishes instruction bytes and control-flow targets,
not a signed upstream source-to-binary chain, runtime AP execution, or the
runtime-selected Linux callback. `setup_real_mode()` copies the linked blob to
low memory and applies segment and linear relocations; the runtime copy's
absolute operands therefore depend on its allocation base.

The selected entry is native physical xAPIC INIT/SIPI. The first SIPI enters
`pa_trampoline_start` at blob offset `0x1000` in real mode. The architectural
AP state and SIPI vector address are defined by
[`SMP_CONTRACT.md` §§3–4](SMP_CONTRACT.md#3-состояния-vcpu-и-переходы). For
this profile, vector `v` is represented by the canonical real-mode entry
`CS.selector = v << 8`, `CS.base = v << 12`, `IP = 0`, yielding physical
address `v << 12` as specified for AP startup by Intel SDM Vol. 3A
§11.4.3 step 6 and §11.4.4.1 step 10; the canonical selector/base pair
follows the real-address segment-base rule in §12.1.4. See the
[official Intel SDM](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/technical/intel-sdm.html).
The `0x1000` here is an offset in the extracted blob, not a claim about its
runtime physical copy base. The bounded path is:

| Order | Blob location | Execution mode / decode defaults | Profile path |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `0x1000`–`0x1024` | real-address, 16-bit defaults | `CLI`, `WBINVD`, real-mode far jump, CS-to-AX and AX-to-DS/ES/SS moves, `LOCK BTS` startup lock with its `JAE`/`PAUSE`/back-edge loop, 32-bit stack-pointer load, then `CALL verify_cpu` at `0x1024`. |
| 2 | `0x1080`–`0x11a8` | real-address, 16-bit defaults | `verify_cpu` checks RFLAGS.ID/CPUID; probes leaves 0, 1, `0x80000000`, and `0x80000001`; validates feature masks. The `OpenDesktop ` vendor selects neither AMD nor Intel vendor-specific branches, and target features satisfy long-mode and SSE/SSE2 checks. The selected success path returns zero at `0x11a4`–`0x11a8`; the alternate failure return is at `0x119b`–`0x11a2`. AMD/Intel-specific MSR paths are not selected. |
| 3 | `0x1027`–`0x102b` | real-address, 16-bit defaults | After return, `TEST EAX,EAX` at `0x1027` and `JNE 0x104c` at `0x102a` select the success continuation for this target. A nonzero failure result branches to the terminal `HLT`/back-edge loop at `0x104c`–`0x104d`; that conditional failure path is not taken by the selected target. The `NOP` at `0x104f` is unreachable padding. |
| 4 | `0x102c`–`0x1041` | real-address, 16-bit defaults through the CR0 write | On successful verification, `LIDT` and `LGDT` read the real-mode tables through DS; DX is loaded with the flat data selector; `MOV CR0,EAX` at `0x1041` sets PE while paging remains clear. |
| 5 | `0x1044` | protected mode, 16-bit transition state | The single required 16-bit protected-mode instruction is the far jump to selector `0x08`, offset `0x2000`; it enters the flat 32-bit code segment. No general 16-bit protected-mode execution is included. |
| 6 | `0x2000`–`0x2062` | protected mode, 32-bit defaults through the CR0 write | The flat data selector is loaded into SS/DS/ES/FS/GS. The target's non-encrypted branch skips the optional AMD SME MSR sequence. CR4 is loaded from the trampoline header, CR3 receives the trampoline page-table root, EFER is read and conditionally updated from the header, then `MOV CR0,EAX` at `0x2062` enables paging and IA-32e mode. |
| 7 | `0x2065` | IA-32e compatibility mode, 32-bit decode | The single transition-state far jump targets selector `0x10`, offset `0x20f0`, entering 64-bit code. No general compatibility-mode execution is included. |
| 8 | `0x20f0` | 64-bit mode | One RIP-relative indirect `JMP` reads the target at blob offset `0x5000` and transfers to `secondary_startup_64`. The separately inventoried common-entry bytes are `CALL verify_cpu` at `0xffffffff8139c090` and the aliased no-verify entry `XOR R15D,R15D` at `0xffffffff8139c095`; they are evidence for the handoff boundary, not an extension to general Long64 support. |

The real-mode decode has 16-bit default operand and address sizes. An observed
`0x66` selects a 32-bit operand for forms such as `PUSHFD`/`POPFD` and the
32-bit register forms that encode it; it does not change the 16-bit address
size. Fixed-width system forms retain their architectural operands: for
example, the unprefixed `0F 22 C0` is `MOV CR0,EAX`, and `CPUID`/`RDMSR` use
their defined EAX/EDX register operands. `LOCK` is admitted only on the
inventoried `BTS m32, imm8`; `F3` only on the inventoried `PAUSE`. There is no
address-size override in the selected real-mode rows. Real-mode addresses use
`segment.base = selector << 4`; a 16-bit effective offset wraps at 16 bits
before adding that base. Instruction fetch uses CS, implicit stack accesses use
SS, and the inventoried explicit data references use DS. SS's 16-bit stack
address size means the path uses SP even when `0x66` makes a PUSH/POP operand
32-bit; the 32-bit load of ESP at `0x101e` leaves its upper half zero. The
real-mode IDT/GDT pseudo-descriptor loads use their recorded operand-size
override with a 16-bit effective address. No general-purpose real-mode
segmentation API is implied.

The protected-mode transition uses a GDT loaded by the real-mode path. Selector
`0x08` names the flat 32-bit code segment; selector `0x18` names the flat data
segment used by the startup code. The far jump to selector `0x10` enters the
64-bit code segment after CR4.PAE, the trampoline CR3, EFER.LME and CR0.PG are
configured from the selected header. The target profile excludes memory
encryption and SNP/Hyper-V/UV overrides, so the optional AMD encrypted-memory
branch is outside the executed path.

The inventory also contains the separate real-mode entry at blob offset
`0x1050` (`sev_es_trampoline_start`). It is not selected for this target because
the accepted profile excludes SEV-ES/SNP; its segment/lock setup is therefore
not an admitted alternative SIPI entry. The profile similarly excludes the
conditional AMD SME branch and vendor-specific AMD/Intel checks that are not
selected by the `OpenDesktop ` CPUID vendor string.

This allowlist is closed over the linked instruction rows and the stated branch
conditions; it does not admit arbitrary code in real or protected mode. An
instruction not present in these rows, a different prefix/addressing form, or
an unselected optional path is outside this profile and must return an explicit
unsupported result in later implementation slices. It does not add BIOS,
reset-vector, v8086, general 16-bit protected mode, general IA-32e compatibility
mode, interrupt-delivery, or general real-mode support. Windows CPU-06 remains
a separate unverified hypothesis.

S6-02's x86 repeat matched 119 real-mode rows (excluding three alignment-byte
decodes), 29 protected-mode rows, one long-mode trampoline row, and two common
entry instructions. It did not execute the guest. The profile and its limits
are recorded in the [S6-14a report](../reports/STAGE_6_REPORT.md#s6-14a--ap-startup-trampoline-profile).

### S2-39a — Legacy FXSAVE/FXRSTOR contract (evidence-only)

This section records the selected target's normative legacy FP/SIMD memory
image. It does not claim implementation, guest boot, C/D acceptance, or
physical execution. Sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 (September 2026), Vol. 2A
pp. 3-409–3-419, especially Tables 3-45–3-49, and Vol. 1 §§10.5.1–10.5.3
and 11.6.5–11.6.6 ([Vol. 2A](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199),
[Vol. 1](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671436)). Exact Linux forms
and source/binary mapping are in the [S2-39a profile evidence](../reports/STAGE_2_LINUX_PROFILE.md#s2-39a--fxsave-evidence-only).

The legacy save area is 512 bytes; its base must be 16-byte aligned. The
architectural defined fields are:

| Offset | Bytes | Field and rule |
|---:|---:|---|
| `0` | 2 | FCW |
| `2` | 2 | FSW, including TOP in bits 13:11 |
| `4` | 1 | Abridged FTW: one bit per physical register R0–R7, 1 means nonempty; 0 means empty. It does not preserve Valid/Zero/Special distinctions. |
| `5` | 1 | Reserved |
| `6` | 2 | FOP in low 11 bits; upper five bits reserved |
| `8..23` | 16 | Mode-specific FIP/FDP and, only for REX.W=0 with CPUID.07H.00H:EBX[13]=0, FCS/FDS selectors; see below. |
| `24` | 4 | MXCSR |
| `28` | 4 | MXCSR_MASK; FXRSTOR ignores this field |
| `32..159` | 128 | ST0–ST7 (MM0–MM7 aliases), 16 bytes each; low 80 bits are raw payload and upper 48 bits are unused/reserved. |
| `160..415` | 256 | XMM0–XMM15, 16 bytes each in 64-bit mode. |
| `416..463` | 48 | Reserved; not architecturally meaningful state. No write behavior is asserted here. |
| `464..511` | 48 | Software-available; FXSAVE does not write these bytes, and FXRSTOR does not use them. FXSAVE therefore preserves their prior memory contents. They are not architectural CPU state. |

The image is not the `FSAVE` image or the project's schema-v2 state snapshot.
The eight data slots are ST0–ST7 order; FTW is abridged and in physical R0–R7
order, so the relation between a slot and its FTW bit depends on TOP rotation.
FXRSTOR reconstructs each nonempty full tag
from the corresponding raw 80-bit payload; this can only preserve distinctions
that payload encoding and the architectural reconstruction permit. Compare
and round-trip tests must use architecturally defined fields, not reserved or
unused bytes. In particular, reserved/unused image bytes are not, by that
label alone, a restore-time validation rule; only explicit SDM checks such as
reserved MXCSR bits are asserted here. Bytes 464–511 are software-available;
FXSAVE does not write them and preserves their prior contents, while FXRSTOR
does not use them. Bytes 416–463 are reserved and not meaningful state. Vol. 1
states that the instructions do not use bytes 416–511, but this contract does
not infer write semantics for reserved bytes 416–463. Saving does not
initialize or otherwise clear the live FP/SIMD registers.

In Long64, ordinary `FXSAVE/FXRSTOR` with REX.W=0 stores FIP at bytes 8–11 and
FDP at bytes 16–19 as 32-bit offsets. Because this selected target's unlisted
CPUID leaf 7 returns zero, bytes 12–13 and 20–21 hold FCS and FDS; bytes 14–15
and 22–23 are unused. `FXSAVE64/FXRSTOR64` with REX.W=1 instead stores complete
64-bit FIP and FDP at bytes 8–15 and 16–23, with no selectors in those ranges.
The remaining fields and XMM offsets are shared. S2-39b adds independently
optional FCS/FDS representation to `X87State` and schema-v2 snapshots, but
those component snapshots are still not interchangeable with this 512-byte
wire image or sufficient to implement its memory effects.

The selected target advertises FXSR separately from SSE/SSE2; Vol. 1 notes that
FXSAVE/FXRSTOR have their own CPUID feature bit. Execution preconditions for a
defined SSE save/restore include CPUID.01H:EDX.FXSR[24]=1, CR0.EM=0,
CR0.TS=0 and CR4.OSFXSR=1. With OSFXSR clear, SSE state handling is
implementation-dependent. This target keeps CR4.OSXSAVE clear and does not
advertise XSAVE/OSXSAVE/AVX. The exact FXSAVE 64-bit mode exceptions include
misalignment #GP(0) (with specified #AC variability where enabled), noncanonical
address #GP(0)/#SS(0), #PF, #NM for CR0.EM/TS, and #UD if FXSR is absent or
LOCK is used. This evidence slice does not implement their guest delivery.

MXCSR is an architectural 32-bit value and FXRSTOR faults if reserved MXCSR
bits are set. Intel describes the saved MXCSR_MASK field and its zero-field
fallback. The selected synthetic target's immutable supported mask is
`0x0000ffbf`; the bounded S2-39e restore profile validates MXCSR against this
target policy and ignores the incoming image's MXCSR_MASK field. This is
distinct from testkit's `diagnostic_mxcsr_mask` snapshot metadata: numerical
equality does not make that local diagnostic metadata the target capability
source.

Each instruction operates on a 512-byte memory area and can encounter
alignment, address, or page faults. This describes the area, not a promise that
every byte is written or read. Intel's cited description does not establish an
all-area atomic write or a general rollback guarantee for external memory
backends; the interpreter must not claim either. The Linux exact forms and
recommended order are recorded in [S2-39a plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-39a-нормативное-evidence-legacy-fxsavefxrstor-evidence-only).
S2-39a is evidence-only. Its first implementation candidate was the plain
Long64 RIP-relative FXSAVE mask-init probe, which is now implemented under
[S2-39c](#s2-39c--plain-long64-rip-relative-fxsave). It stores architectural
state beyond MXCSR_MASK while preserving bytes 464–511; it is not a mask-only
store. Selector representation was resolved by
[S2-39b](#s2-39b--selector-state-representation-only). FXRSTOR and other
forms remain unsupported.

### S2-39b — Selector state representation only

`X87State` carries independently optional 16-bit `instruction_selector` and
`data_selector` values, and schema-v2 `X87Snapshot` carries matching optional
hex values. `None` means the selector is unavailable or unrepresented;
`Some(0)` is a known zero value. FIP and FDP remain full-width `u64` offsets.
The older x87 and x87/SSE profiles serialize these fields absent and reject
present selector fields. Fixture seed data also leaves them absent; selectors
are not inferred from current CS or DS.

The isolated `s2-long-x87-selectors-state-v1` profile requires x87, SSE, and
both selectors. It admits only one NOP byte (`90`), budget 1, with stop RIP
immediately following it. A handwritten fixture uses distinct nonzero
selectors and 64-bit pointer sentinels. NOP preserves full raw x87 and SSE
state; result comparison includes both selector presence and value. The C
fragment adapter rejects the containing x87 state, and JIT/native admission
remain explicitly unsupported.

Because existing x87 instruction semantics update FIP/FDP but do not model FCS
or FDS transitions, the interpreter fails closed before state mutation or data
memory access for any supported x87 primary-opcode instruction whenever either
selector is present. STOP-address and zero-budget checks retain their existing
ordering. No selector is fabricated from CS/DS.

At the S2-39b substage, this closed [ISSUE-026](../KNOWN_ISSUES.md#issue-026--plain-long64-fxsavefxrstor-target-lacks-selector-state)
for state representation only. It did not add FNINIT execution or an
FXSAVE/FXRSTOR memory image, instruction, alignment/fault behavior, or native
observation. S2-39c later implements one exact plain FXSAVE save form and S2-39d
one exact FXSAVE64 save form. At the S2-39b status point, FXRSTOR and broader
forms remained unsupported; the narrow S2-39e FXRSTOR64 profile is documented
below. Broader S2-39 remains open. Hardware/Mac mini checks are deferred to the combined final
hardware substage. See the [S2-39b plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-39b-lossless-selector-state-representation-no-fxsave-execution)
and [implementation report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-39b--selector-state-representation-only).

### S2-39c — Plain Long64 RIP-relative FXSAVE

The local profile `s2-long-fxsave-rip-v1` accepts exactly one unprefixed
Long64 instruction, `0F AE 05 disp32` (`/0`, ModRM.mod=00, r/m=101,
RIP-relative). REX.W is zero. The decoder rejects prefixes/REX, other ModRM
forms, FXSAVE64 and FXRSTOR within this S2-39c profile, and neighboring `0F AE`
operations except the existing independent MFENCE encoding. The shared decoder
separately admits only the exact S2-39d FXSAVE64 form described below. Execution requires x87/SSE state and
both known FCS/FDS selectors; `Some(0)` is known zero. CPUID FXSR=1,
CR0.EM=0, CR0.TS=0 and CR4.OSFXSR=1 are profile preconditions, not runtime
gates in the current state model. CPUID dispatch, JIT and native execution do
not admit this operation.

For the 512-byte destination, the interpreter preflights 16-byte alignment
and the complete non-overflowing canonical48 area before any write callback.
This full-range geometry check is bounded local profile policy; it does not
claim hardware probes the unused tail. It performs exactly 13 ascending,
write-only `GuestMemory::write` calls over `[0,5)`, `[6,14)`, `[16,22)`,
`[24,32)`, eight 10-byte slots at `[32+16*i,42+16*i)`, and `[160,416)`.
There are no data reads and no read/modify/write callbacks.

The image stores FCW/FSW raw little-endian; FTW is abridged with one bit per
physical register and 1 for every nonempty full tag; FOP is low 11 bits with
upper five bits zero; FIP/FDP are low 32-bit offsets with independent FCS/FDS
selectors. MXCSR is copied raw and `state.mxcsr` is never masked. The immutable
`od-isa::TARGET_FXSAVE_MXCSR_MASK` is `0x0000_ffbf`, a conservative DAZ-clear
capability policy for the synthetic Generic amd64 target. It is intentionally
separate from the testkit diagnostic mask constant, even though their current
numeric values match. x87 slots i contain `registers[(TOP+i)&7]` low 10 raw
bytes; XMM0–15 are copied raw.

All holes/reserved/software bytes remain unchanged. Intel explicitly preserves
bytes 464–511; preservation of reserved bytes 5, 14–15, 22–23,
`[42+16*i,48+16*i)` for `i=0..7`, and 416–463 is a local policy, not a claim
about their hardware write behavior.
The writes are not an all-area transaction: if callback k fails, successful
earlier slices remain written, callback k itself is unchanged under the
GuestMemory contract, and later callbacks are skipped. CPU state, RIP and
retirement do not commit. This is restricted to the current private synchronous
RAM model and makes no MMIO, shared-DMA, SMP, or global rollback claim.

The fixture preserves the observed Linux bytes `0F AE 05 6B F9 17 00`; a
separate direct execution uses another disp32. Tests cover all TOP values,
tag routing, selectors, raw pointers/MXCSR, all XMM registers, sentinel holes,
write order/count, callback fault matrix, preflight gates, strict decode and
fetch truncation. They establish local interpreter/profile behavior only;
they do not establish hardware behavior, guest exception delivery, boot, or
physical execution. At the S2-39c status point FXRSTOR and other FXSAVE
addressing forms remained open; S2-39e later implements one exact restore form.
Other forms and complete S2-39 remain open. Physical validation is deferred to the combined final Mac mini
substage. See the [S2-39c plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-39c-exact-plain-long64-rip-relative-fxsave)
and [implementation report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-39c--plain-long64-rip-relative-fxsave).

### S2-39d — Exact Long64 FXSAVE64 `[RAX+0x40]`

The local `s2-long-fxsave64-rax-disp8-v1` profile admits only the exact five
bytes `48 0F AE 40 40`. This is REX.W=1 FXSAVE64 with base RAX and disp8
`0x40`; other REX values, prefixes, registers, displacements, address forms,
and FXRSTOR64 are unsupported within this S2-39d save profile. S2-39e adds a
separate exact FXRSTOR64 profile. The profile requires x87 and SSE state but
accepts each optional FCS/FDS selector independently as present or absent,
because the 64-bit image stores full FIP/FDP and no selector fields.

The shared serializer keeps S2-39c's 13 ascending write-only callbacks. For
this layout, the environment slices are `[6,16)` (FOP and full 64-bit FIP) and
`[16,24)` (full 64-bit FDP); the bytes formerly used for selectors in the plain
layout are pointer bytes here. All other field layouts, MXCSR mask policy,
preflight geometry, callback-failure behavior, and preserved ranges match the
plain profile. This local save profile does not admit JIT/native execution and does not
implement FXRSTOR within its own exact profile; S2-39e separately adds a
narrow restore profile and representable-state round-trip. Physical checks
remain in the combined final Mac mini substage. See the [S2-39d plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-39d-exact-long64-fxsave64-rax0x40) and
[implementation report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-39d--exact-long64-fxsave64-rax0x40).

### S2-39e — Exact Long64 FXRSTOR64 `[RBX+0x40]`

The local `s2-long-fxrstor64-rbx-disp8-v1` profile admits exactly the five
bytes `48 0F AE 4B 40`: REX.W=1 FXRSTOR64 with base RBX and disp8 `0x40`.
It requires x87/SSE state, but accepts `instruction_selector` and
`data_selector` independently absent or present and preserves their prior
options. No general base-plus-displacement form, other address form, JIT, or
native execution is admitted.

The effective base is architectural wrapping `RBX+0x40`. Before memory access,
the complete 512-byte image must be 16-byte aligned, canonical48 and
non-overflowing. Execution performs exactly 13 ascending read-only callbacks:
`[0,5)`, `[6,16)`, `[16,24)`, `[24,28)`, eight 10-byte slices at
`[32+16*i,42+16*i)`, and `[160,416)`. Reserved, padding, MXCSR_MASK and tail
bytes are not read. The loaded state is staged in temporary buffers. The image
MXCSR_MASK is ignored; MXCSR must satisfy
`loaded_mxcsr & !TARGET_FXSAVE_MXCSR_MASK == 0`, otherwise the interpreter
returns #GP(0). Reads and validation complete before replacing x87/SSE state
or advancing RIP/retirement. On a read or validation failure CPU state,
definedness, RIP and retirement remain unchanged; callbacks stop at the first
read failure. Backend error categories are preserved. No generic backend
rollback is claimed for completed reads.

The restore copies raw FCW/FSW, full 64-bit FIP/FDP, low 11 FOP bits and every
80-bit payload without normalization or quieting. FTW bits are physical R0–R7;
slots are logical ST0–ST7, so the restore applies TOP rotation. Empty FTW bits
produce Empty; nonempty raw values classify as Zero only for exponent zero and
zero full significand, Valid only for exponent 1..0x7ffe and J=1, and Special
otherwise. XMM0–15 are copied byte-for-byte. Restoring does not deliver pending
x87 arithmetic exceptions. Since abridged FTW cannot encode the original
nonempty tag class, arbitrary tag-word round-trip is not asserted.

The handwritten literal fixture and local tests document all TOP values,
selector option preservation, raw pointer and XMM state, ignored mask/padding,
reserved-MXCSR rejection, per-callback failure, wrapped base arithmetic and
range preflight. This is local interpreter evidence only; hardware, physical
x86, SSH/Mac mini, exception delivery and broader S2-39 acceptance remain open.
See the [S2-39e plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-39e-exact-long64-fxrstor64-rbx0x40),
[implementation report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-39e--exact-long64-fxrstor64-rbx0x40),
and [fixture](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-39e-long64-fxrstor64-rbx0x40).

### S2-39f — Bounded FXSAVE64 CR0 EM and TS `#NM` gates

The local-only `s2-long-fxsave64-cr0-gates-v1` profile accepts exactly
`48 0F AE 40 40` (`FXSAVE64 [RAX+0x40]`) and explicit immutable `cr0_em` and
`cr0_ts` booleans. `FXSR=1` and `CR4.OSFXSR=1` remain fixed prerequisites;
their absent cases are outside this profile. After complete instruction fetch
and decode, `CR0.EM=1` or `CR0.TS=1` produces CPU fault vector 7 (`#NM`), no
error code, zero retirement, no CPU/RAM mutation, and no data-memory callback,
for CPL0–3. If both bits are clear, the existing S2-39d serializer executes.
Pending x87 exception state and MXCSR sticky flags remain saved state; FXSAVE
does not deliver `#MF` or `#XM`.

The fixture is restricted to an aligned canonical48 writable private 512-byte
data mapping. Incoming stop and zero budget precede fetch; the complete
encoding is fetched before the CR0 gate. Combined data-address/page-fault gate
priority is not claimed. The profile does not establish `FXSR=0`,
`CR4.OSFXSR=0`, another FXSAVE layout, hardware-image equivalence, CPUID or CR
writes, general CR state, FXRSTOR, JIT/native/C-adapter support or other forms.
The handwritten success fixture compares against an independent literal
512-byte image; the fault matrix covers all CR0 bit pairs at CPL0–3 and checks
full snapshot/no-commit behavior. Intel SDM Rev. 093, Vol. 2A FXSAVE 64-Bit
Mode Exceptions, pp. 3-418–3-419, lists `#NM` for either CR0 bit. Vol. 3A,
Event 7, pp. 7-33–7-34, identifies `#NM` as a fault with no error code and no
program-state change because the instruction is not executed:
[Vol. 2A](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199),
[Vol. 3A](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/technical/intel-sdm.html). Parent S2-39 and
the Generic amd64 target remain open; hardware checks stay in the combined
final Mac mini batch. See the [S2-39f plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-39f-bounded-fxsave64-cr0-em-and-ts-nm-gates),
[report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-39f--bounded-fxsave64-cr0-em-and-ts-nm-gates),
and [fixture](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-39f-long64-fxsave64-cr0-em-and-ts-gates).

### S2-39g — Bounded FXRSTOR64 CR0 EM and TS `#NM` gates

The interpreter-only profile `s2-long-fxrstor64-cr0-gates-v1` admits exactly
`48 0F AE 4B 40` (`FXRSTOR64 [RBX+0x40]`) with immutable `cr0_em` and `cr0_ts`
inputs. FXSR=1 and CR4.OSFXSR=1 remain fixed prerequisites. Once the complete
instruction has been fetched and decoded, either bit set returns CPU fault
vector 7 (`#NM`), no error code, zero retirement, no CPU/RAM/RIP change, and no
data-memory reads at CPL0–3. With both bits clear, the existing S2-39e restore
path performs its 13 staged reads and commits only after MXCSR validation.

To keep the fixture oracle bounded, it admits only an aligned canonical48
readable private 512-byte image with MXCSR valid under the immutable target
mask. This profile does not claim `#NM` priority against invalid-image,
address, or page faults. STOP and zero budget are checked before fetch; all
instruction bytes are fetched before the gate. Restored pending x87/SSE status
and MXCSR sticky flags remain state data; FXRSTOR does not deliver `#MF` or
`#XM`. Existing S2-39e invalid-image/address/fault coverage remains in that
separate profile. No JIT/native/C-adapter path, alternate image layout,
FXSR=0, or CR4.OSFXSR=0 behavior is admitted.

Handwritten success and `#NM` fixtures use a literal 512-byte image with valid
MXCSR and nonzero ignored/padding bytes. Coverage checks TOP/tag reconstruction,
full FIP/FDP, XMM0–15, optional selector preservation, ignored MXCSR_MASK and
padding, pending status, full no-commit snapshots, and the four CR0 combinations
at CPL0–3 with zero callbacks on `#NM`. Intel SDM Rev. 093, Vol. 2A, FXRSTOR
64-Bit Mode Exceptions, pp. 3-409–3-411 lists `#NM` for CR0.EM or CR0.TS. Vol.
3A Event 7, pp. 7-33–7-34 specifies no error code and no program-state change
because the faulting instruction is not executed:
[Vol. 2A](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199),
[Vol. 3A](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/technical/intel-sdm.html). Local software
checks do not establish physical execution or broader S2-39 acceptance. See the
[S2-39g plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-39g-bounded-fxrstor64-cr0-em-and-ts-nm-gates),
[report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-39g--bounded-fxrstor64-cr0-em-and-ts-nm-gates),
and [fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-39g-long64-fxrstor64-cr0-em-and-ts-gates).

### S2-39h — Exact FP-init plus FXSAVE64 composition

The local-only `s2-long-cr0-cr4-fp-init-fxsave64-v1` schema-v2 profile admits
exactly the S2-25c 28-byte sequence followed by `48 0F AE 40 40`
(`FXSAVE64 [RAX+0x40]`), for 33 bytes and nine retirements. Initial CR0.EM/TS
and CR4.OSFXSR/OSXMMEXCPT may independently take all 16 combinations. The
existing sequence clears CR0.EM/TS and sets both CR4 bits before the save, so
an initially clear OSFXSR does not cause a synthetic fault; no OSFXSR-clear
behavior at the FXSAVE instruction is admitted or inferred. The profile reuses
the live CR0/CR4 path, S2-39d serializer, immutable target MXCSR mask, and its
defined-field write policy.

The strict fixture fixes CPL0, RAX `0x620`, an aligned private 512-byte save
region at `0x660..0x85f`, budget 9, and STOP at the byte immediately after the
program. It checks a separately authored literal image for defined fields;
bytes 464–511 are preserved, while undefined/reserved ranges are not asserted.
Earlier operations retire independently. STOP, zero budget, and truncated
final fetch preserve earlier effects. A serializer callback failure leaves
the final instruction unretired and does not commit that instruction's CPU
state; earlier private RAM writes are not rolled back as a whole-memory
transaction. The result is interpreter-only local evidence. JIT, native,
C/fragment adapters, other layouts, and physical execution remain closed.

See the [S2-39h plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-39h-exact-fp-initialization-composition-followed-by-fxsave64),
[report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-39h--exact-fp-init-plus-fxsave64-composition),
[fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-39h-fp-init-plus-fxsave64-composition),
and [fixture format](../testing/TEST_CASE_FORMAT.md#s2-39h-fp-init-plus-fxsave64-profile).

### S2-39i — Exact FP-init plus FXRSTOR64 composition

The local-only `s2-long-cr0-cr4-fp-init-fxrstor64-v1` schema-v2 profile
admits exactly the S2-25c 28-byte sequence followed by
`48 0F AE 4B 40` (`FXRSTOR64 [RBX+0x40]`), for 33 bytes and nine retirements.
It reuses the live CR0/CR4 initialization path and S2-39e staged restore. The
16 starting CR0.EM/TS × CR4.OSFXSR/OSXMMEXCPT combinations are accepted; the
preceding sequence clears EM/TS and sets OSFXSR/OSXMMEXCPT. Restore gates read
current CR0 and require OSFXSR=1. An OSFXSR-clear local profile result is
Unsupported; no fault is inferred. FXSR availability is assumed.

The strict fixture fixes CPL0, RBX `0x620`, an aligned private readable 512-byte
image at `0x660..0x85f`, budget 9 and STOP after the final instruction. Its
literal image is authored independently from the post-init CPU state. Restore
performs the existing 13 ascending read callbacks, stages fields and validates
MXCSR against `TARGET_FXSAVE_MXCSR_MASK` before replacing CPU state. Image
MXCSR_MASK, reserved/padding/software bytes are ignored and remain unchanged.
The restore applies TOP rotation and abridged physical FTW reconstruction,
copies raw x87 payloads, full FIP/FDP, low eleven FOP bits, MXCSR and XMM0–15,
and preserves selectors. No x87/SSE exception delivery is implied.

Failure at each read callback or MXCSR validation leaves the final instruction
unretired and CPU state uncommitted; the earlier eight operations remain
retired. STOP, zero budget and truncated final fetch issue no restore reads.
No combined-fault priority, physical/hardware, JIT/native/C/fragment or other
encoding claim is made. See the [S2-39i plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-39i-exact-fp-initialization-composition-followed-by-fxrstor64),
[report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-39i--exact-fp-init-plus-fxrstor64-composition),
[fixture](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-39i-fp-init-plus-fxrstor64-composition),
and [format](../testing/TEST_CASE_FORMAT.md#s2-39i-fp-init-plus-fxrstor64-profile).

## Предлагаемый профиль тестового прототипа S0-09

Прототип — изолированный пользовательский fragment runner с единым vCPU, только immutable code buffer и register-only вычислениями. Это набор для сравнения decoder → interpreter/JIT, а не профиль x86-64 машины.

### Состояние и запуск

- Режим: 64-bit instruction mode; никаких переходов режима, CPL transitions, сегментных обращений или privilege checks.
- Состояние: `RAX`, `RCX`, `RDX`, `RBX`, `RIP` и подмножество `RFLAGS`. Host-регистры не считаются архитектурным состоянием.
- Начальные значения GPR и `RIP` задаются входным manifest программы; `RIP` — byte offset внутри code buffer. Начальные арифметические flags очищены, reserved bit 1 RFLAGS установлен.
- Операции используют 64-bit width. Конкретные разрешённые prefix/opcode/ModR/M формы перечисляются в таблице ниже; прочие формы не поддерживаются.
- Исполнение останавливается при достижении `RIP == code_length`, исчерпании instruction budget или явной ошибке. Итог включает перечисленные регистры и определённые flags.

### Формы инструкций

| Инструкция | Минимальная форма S0-09 | Архитектурный эффект |
|---|---|---|
| `MOV r64, imm64` | `REX.W + B8+rd + imm64`, назначения только RAX/RCX/RDX/RBX | Записывает 64-bit immediate в назначенный GPR; flags не меняет. |
| `ADD r64, r/m64` | `REX.W + 03 /r`; оба операнда — один из четырёх разрешённых GPR, без памяти | Складывает source с destination; устанавливает CF/PF/AF/ZF/SF/OF по x86-64 semantics. |
| `SUB r64, r/m64` | `REX.W + 2B /r`; register-register | Вычитает source из destination; устанавливает CF/PF/AF/ZF/SF/OF. |
| `CMP r64, r/m64` | `REX.W + 3B /r`; register-register | Вычисляет destination − source, не записывает результат; устанавливает CF/PF/AF/ZF/SF/OF. |
| `JZ rel8` | `74 cb` | Если ZF=1, переход на signed rel8 от конца инструкции; иначе продолжение. |
| `JNZ rel8` | `75 cb` | Если ZF=0, переход на signed rel8 от конца инструкции; иначе продолжение. |

Условный переход может вести только на начало декодированной инструкции внутри code buffer либо ровно на `code_length` (остановка). Переход в середину инструкции, за границу, назад к недекодируемому смещению и за budget завершается явным результатом runner. Нет `CALL/RET`, стека, памяти данных, системных инструкций, CPUID/MSR, x87/SSE/AVX, interrupt delivery или MMU.

Декодер читает байты через ограниченный интерфейс; один запрос не читает за концом buffer. Максимальная архитектурная длина x86 инструкции — 15 bytes; усечённая и неразрешённая форма возвращает отдельную ошибку без частичного исполнения. Перед реализацией зафиксировать детальную таблицу принимаемых байтовых форм/REX/ModR/M, чтобы decoder не принимал более широкие формы случайно.

### Flag contract

Для `ADD`, `SUB` и `CMP` результат флагов CF/PF/AF/ZF/SF/OF определяется соответствующими x86 operation semantics. `JZ/JNZ` читают только ZF. На каждом сравнении interpreter/JIT проверяются все flags, определённые данной инструкцией. Флаги или состояния, которые архитектура определяет как undefined, не используются тестами и не считаются обязательным совпадением. Другие RFLAGS биты не моделируются и в CPUID не рекламируются.

### Ошибки и корректность

- Неизвестные, неподдерживаемые и усечённые формы дают различимые decode errors; они не исполняются приблизительно.
- Некорректная цель ветвления, instruction budget exhaustion и отсутствие доступного байта — различимые причины остановки.
- Host panic, memory safety failure и JIT code fault — дефекты реализации, не guest exception.
- Interpreter и JIT используют одинаковый набор входных байтов и сравниваются по exit reason, guest RIP, GPR и flags, определённым этой версией контракта.
- Собственные hex-fixtures для этапа 0 находятся в [`tests/fixtures/x86/`](../../tests/fixtures/x86/README.md): арифметика с переполнением, зависимый `SUB/JNZ` цикл, `CMP/JZ`, загрузка immediate и неподдерживаемый opcode. Команды сравнивают interpreter и JIT; источником семантики остаётся этот контракт и Intel/AMD manuals.

## Не включено и будущие решения

| Возможность | Статус | Что нужно до объявления |
|---|---|---|
| Windows/Linux CPU profile | Не определён | Exact media/build, сбор boot requirements, обязательные CPUID/MSR/ISA и драйверные проверки |
| x86-64 application baseline | Не определён | Результаты выбранных приложений и минимальные ABI/runtime requirements |
| 32-bit compatibility | Не включена в S0-09 | Guest mode transitions, segmentation, syscall/exception behavior и тестовый набор |
| x87/SSE/AVX | Не включены в S0-09 | State layout, exception/masking semantics, feature gating и отдельная проверка каждого расширения |
| Paging/MMU и TLB | Не включены в S0-09 | GVA→GPA translation, permissions, page faults, address-width profile и invalidation contract |
| SMP, atomics, fences | Не включены в S0-09 | x86 memory ordering, locked operations, interrupt/scheduler model и stress tests |
| Privileged/system instructions, APIC/timers, exceptions | Не включены в S0-09 | Выбранный board/boot profile, точная архитектурная семантика и приоритеты событий |

### Local S2-18g STOSW/D/Q contract

The bounded interpreter accepts `66 AB` (word), bare `AB` (dword), and
effective `REX.W + AB` (qword) in Long64 with address-size 64 and implicit flat
`ES:[RDI]`. REX.W overrides 66; a REX byte before a later legacy prefix is
ignored by the shared normalizer (`48 66 AB` is word; `66 48 AB` is qword). All
`48..4F` REX.W values are accepted. Group1 prefixes, `67`, segment overrides,
effective non-W REX, and REP/LOCK are outside the profile.

Each success performs one width-sized all-or-error write of low RAX at the
pre-instruction RDI, then wraps RDI by ±width according to DF, advances RIP, and
retires once. RAX, RSI, RCX, and RFLAGS remain unchanged. RSI is never accessed or
validated. A noncanonical destination returns #GP(0); bounded-memory and
backend errors remain harness errors unless the backend explicitly reports an
architectural fault. Failure commits neither CPU state nor RAM. No LOCK/SMP
atomicity is claimed; JIT/native and physical acceptance remain deferred.

### Local S2-18h SCAS B/W/D/Q contract

The bounded Long64 interpreter accepts bare `AE` SCASB, bare `AF` SCASD,
`66 AF` SCASW, and effective `REX.W + AF` SCASQ with address-size 64 and
implicit flat `ES:[RDI]`. All `48..4F` REX.W forms are accepted. Effective
REX.W overrides 66 (`66 48 AF` is qword); a REX before a later 66 is
normalized away (`48 66 AF` is word). REP, LOCK, 67, every segment override,
effective non-W REX on `AF`, and all prefixed `AE` forms are outside the profile.

SCAS performs one read of 1/2/4/8 bytes from pre-state RDI, compares the
pre-state AL/AX/EAX/RAX with the memory value using the existing CMP result
and flag rules, and commits arithmetic flags plus the DF-directed wrapping
RDI update only after the read succeeds. It preserves all of RAX (including
the upper half after SCASD), RSI, RCX, RAM and DF. Successful retirement
advances RIP and defines `ARITHMETIC_FLAGS`; undefined flags are zero. A
noncanonical source returns #GP(0); missing mappings, permissions and backend
errors remain harness errors unless the backend returns an architectural
fault. The faulting SCAS instruction commits no CPU or memory state; any earlier
retired instruction remains committed. JIT/native admission is closed.

Interpreter checks include 6,144 full-state comparisons with independent flag
calculation, one read/no writes, all alignment residues, page/range boundaries,
wrapping and noncanonical post-index values, ignored RSI values, prefix/REX
normalization, atomic faults, and TEST→SCAS definedness. Exactly 24 literal
schema-v2 fixtures cover width/direction successes, unmapped and noncanonical
sources, zero budget, normalization, and TEST composition success/fault. The
generator serializes predetermined input/output literals only. ISSUE-016 and
ISSUE-019 remain open; physical execution is deferred to the shared final
acceptance substage.

### Local S2-18i CMPS B/W/D/Q contract

The bounded Long64 profile accepts bare `A6` CMPSB, `66 A7` CMPSW, bare
`A7` CMPSD, and effective `REX.W + A7` CMPSQ with address-size 64. All
`48..4F` REX.W bytes are accepted; effective REX.W overrides 66, while a REX
before a later 66 is normalized away (`48 66 A7` is word; `66 48 A7` is
qword). CMPSB is bare-only. REP, LOCK, 67, segment overrides and effective
non-W REX on A7 are outside this profile.

Each successful instruction performs two width-sized reads using pre-state
addresses in strict order: flat DS:[RSI], then flat ES:[RDI]. It computes
`memory[RSI] - memory[RDI]` with CMP flags, then commits only arithmetic flags,
DF-directed wrapping RSI/RDI, RIP and one retirement. RAX, RCX and RAM are
unchanged. RSI=RDI still performs two reads. Successful retirement defines
`ARITHMETIC_FLAGS`; failed reads define no additional flags and commit no CPU
state. A noncanonical start or final byte in either operand produces #GP(0).
Missing mapping, permission and backend errors remain harness errors unless the
backend explicitly reports an architectural fault; no #PF is synthesized.

If the first access fails, there is no second access. If the second fails, the
first read remains observable in the local trace while CPU commit is withheld.
The selected RSI-first order is bounded local policy and is not hardware
priority evidence for dual-invalid operands. No MMIO or side-effect rollback is
claimed. Dual-invalid winner remains open as ISSUE-020. Exactly 33 literal
schema-v2 fixtures preserve the existing schema/profile; the generator only
serializes stated inputs and expected full states. Local full-state coverage,
read-order/failure matrix, prefix boundary and address tests do not establish
native/JIT or physical x86 behavior. Mac mini/SSH/native/physical acceptance
remains part of the single final substage.

Для ещё не реализованных строк таблица задаёт группы и диапазоны кодировок,
а точные допустимые сочетания, ошибки и порядок side effects фиксируются перед
реализацией каждой формы. Whole-group CPUID bits до этого не выдаются.
Manual/generated/hardware tests S0 относятся только к исходной таблице S0-09;
новый профиль не наследует их как доказательство более широкого покрытия.

S2-16a interpreter coverage: `ConditionCode` explicitly models all 16

use signed displacements from the complete instruction's next RIP with
long-mode 64-bit wrapping. Local literal coverage and remaining unsupported
prefixes/forms are recorded in the S2-16 section of the [Stage 2 plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md).
Its 68 literal fixtures are deferred to the same final physical Mac mini
acceptance substage as the 216 S2-15 fixtures; the pool later grew to 433 with
S2-16b/c. Independent review completed cleanly with no findings. S2-16b adds
all 16 SETcc encodings for byte
register and ordinary memory destinations. It preserves all flags and
definedness, writes exactly one memory byte, and leaves CPU state uncommitted
on write fault. Independent literal coverage exercises all conditions, byte
register aliases, memory addressing, and unsupported prefix boundaries. The
79 fixtures joined the shared pool; the later S2-16c addition brings the total
to 433. S2-16c adds all 16 CMOVcc forms, reads the source even when the condition
is false, and preserves no-commit behavior on read fault. A false 32-bit form

await the same physical mini acceptance. Indirect JMP remained open after
S2-16c; S2-16d later adds a register-target near form. Other control/stack
forms remain open in S2-17. S2-17a locally adds
only 64-bit GPR PUSH/POP opcode forms `50–5F` with `REX.B`: 8 fixtures cover
RSP aliasing, a bounded guest stack, the full canonical range, `#SS(0)`, and

CALL/RET, and indirect forms remained open at S2-17a. S2-17b adds only the
64-bit immediate PUSH forms `6A ib` and `68 id`, sign-extended to qword, with
8 boundary fixtures covering stack bounds, faults, truncated fetch, and
no-commit. Independent Sol medium review is clean; physical validation remains
deferred in the shared pool, then 449 fixtures. S2-16d added three register-
target near indirect JMP cases, bringing the pool to 452; S2-16e adds 7
ordinary memory-target cases, bringing the shared pool to 459. S2-17c adds six
near relative CALL fixtures, bringing the pool to 465. S2-17d adds five
register near indirect CALL `FF /2 r/m64` fixtures, with the corrected stack

At the end of S2-17e the shared pool was 479. Independent Sol-medium reviews are clean and

noncanonical-target plus invalid-stack fault priority remains unverified across

the dual-fault case is not in the corpus. FS/GS and out-of-profile addressing,
CALL, and far transfers remain open in S2-16. Other immediate and 16-bit

and IRET remain open in S2-17.

S2-17f adds only near `RET imm16` (`C2 iw`) in 64-bit operand mode. The

S2-17g adds only 16-bit GPR PUSH/POP opcodes `50–5F` with `66` and optional

Принятое decode coverage S2-06: собственный `long_decode`
нормализует prefixes/REX/66/67/opcode maps, MOV immediate 8–64 и
register-register MOV, ADD/SUB/CMP register widths, short/near JZ/JNZ.
В checkpoint S2-06 memory addressing, SIMD и REP не поддержаны; duplicate legacy groups дают
Unsupported как граница среза. Влияет только properly located REX, ранние и
misplaced REX игнорируются по SDM. LOCK консервативно Unsupported без заявления
о приоритете #UD/fetch fault; Invalid/#UD задан только для complete UD2.
Это не расширяет execution allowlist: исполняются только S0 MOV imm64,
ADD/SUB/CMP r64 для первых четырёх регистров и short JZ/JNZ, как в S2-05.
Прошедшие 19 od-isa tests не являются native execution evidence.
Точные источники decoder — Intel SDM 093
[Vol.2A](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199), §§2.1.1–2.2.1,
ADD/CMP/Jcc/LOCK, и [Vol.2B](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/929354/253667-093-sdm-vol-2b.pdf),
MOV/SUB. Итоговый статус — в [отчёте](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-06--decoder).

S2-07 расширил decode-only coverage на ModR/M/SIB, displacement,
