## Local register-only `PADDSB` profile — S2-35.10

The exact profile `s2-long-paddsb-reg-v1` admits only legacy
`66 [one optional REX.R/B] 0F EC /r` with ModR/M.mod=3. ModR/M.reg is the XMM
destination and ModR/M.r/m is the source, extended only through XMM0–XMM15.
Each of 16 byte lanes reinterprets destination and source as signed i8, adds,
clamps to [-128, 127], and encodes the result as its raw u8 byte. This is
signed saturation: for example, `0xff + 0x01` produces `0x00`, while
`0x80 + 0x7f` produces `0xff`; unsigned saturation would differ. Bare `0F EC`
is MMX and rejected. PADDSW, signed subtraction, memory, extra prefixes,
REX.W/X, VEX/EVEX, JIT/native and physical execution are excluded.

The interpreter requires the local x87/SSE state and preserves every field
except the destination XMM register and RIP; RFLAGS and MXCSR remain unchanged.
Execution makes no data-memory callbacks. SSE2 availability, CR0.EM=0,
CR0.TS=0 and CR4.OSFXSR=1 are assumptions only. No CPUID, #UD/#NM/#GP delivery,
or universal MXCSR mask is modeled. Encoding and signed saturation follow
PADDSB in Intel SDM revision 093, Volume 2B: [official Intel SDM PDF](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/929354/253667-093-sdm-vol-2b.pdf),
[Intel SDM index](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/technical/intel-sdm.html).
S2-34, S2-35 and global `S2-35 → S2-34` remain open. See the
[S2-35.10 plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-3510--local-only-bounded-register-paddsb).

## Local register-only `PADDSW` profile — S2-35.12

The exact diagnostic profile `s2-long-paddsw-reg-v1` admits only legacy
`66 [one optional REX.R/B] 0F ED /r` with ModR/M.mod=3. The mandatory `66`
selects the XMM/SSE2 encoding from bare MMX `0F ED`; ModR/M.reg is destination
and ModR/M.r/m is source, with REX.R/B extending the indices through XMM15.
Eight independent little-endian signed i16 lanes are summed in i32 and clamped
to [-32768, 32767]. Only destination XMM and RIP change; all other state,
including flags and MXCSR, is preserved and no data-memory callback occurs.
Missing raw x87/SSE state and unsupported/truncated encodings reject atomically.
SSE2 availability and CR0.EM=0, CR0.TS=0, CR4.OSFXSR=1 are assumptions only.
No CPUID, guest exception-delivery, memory, JIT/native or physical-hardware
claim is made. See the [S2-35.12 plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-3512--local-only-bounded-register-paddsw).

## Local register-only `PCMPGTB` profile — S2-35.21

The exact diagnostic profile `s2-long-pcmpgtb-reg-v1` admits only legacy
`66 [one optional REX.R/B] 0F 64 /r` with ModR/M.mod=3. ModR/M.reg is the
XMM destination and ModR/M.r/m the source, extended to XMM0–15. Each byte lane
independently writes `FF` iff the destination interpreted as signed i8 is
strictly greater than the source interpreted as signed i8; otherwise it writes
`00`. Only destination XMM and RIP change; flags, MXCSR and other modeled state
are preserved, and the operation invokes no guest data-memory callback.

Coverage compares all 65,536 raw byte pairs against an independent signed-byte
mapping, includes asymmetric and strict/equal cases and signed boundaries,
mixed lanes, the full 16×16 XMM/REX matrix, atomic stop/budget/truncation/missing
state behavior, exact-profile negatives and a literal XMM8/XMM9 fixture. Bare
MMX, PCMPGTW/D/Q, other comparisons, memory, extra prefixes, REX.W/X,
VEX/EVEX, feature gates, exception delivery, JIT/native execution and physical
acceptance are excluded. PCMPGTQ requires SSE4.2 and is outside this SSE2 slice.
SSE2 plus CR0.EM=0, CR0.TS=0 and CR4.OSFXSR=1 are assumptions only; no CPUID
or exception-delivery claim is made. Encoding and semantics follow PCMPGTB in
Intel SDM revision 093, Volume 2B. S2-34, S2-35 and global S2-35 → S2-34 remain
open; Mac mini/SSH acceptance is deferred. See the
[S2-35.21 plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-3521--local-only-bounded-register-pcmpgtb).

## Local register-only PUNPCKHDQ slice — S2-35.29

The profile `s2-long-punpckhdq-reg-v1` admits only legacy
`66 [one optional REX.R/B] 0F 6A /r` with ModR/M.mod=3. ModR/M.reg selects the
destination XMM register and r/m selects the source. The destination becomes
the four little-endian u32 elements `[old_DEST[2], SRC[2], old_DEST[3],
SRC[3]]`; its low two input dwords and the source low two dwords are ignored.
All destination bits are overwritten. The profile assumes SSE2 and
CR0.EM=0, CR0.TS=0, CR4.OSFXSR=1; it does not implement feature/control gates.
MMX, memory, other prefixes, REX.W/X, VEX/EVEX, JIT/native execution, guest
exception delivery and physical acceptance are excluded. Parent S2-34, S2-35
and the global S2-35 → S2-34 dependency remain open.


## Local register-only PUNPCKHQDQ slice — S2-35.31

The profile `s2-long-punpckhqdq-reg-v1` admits legacy
`66 [one optional REX.R/B] 0F 6D /r` with ModR/M.mod=3. ModR/M.reg selects the
destination XMM register and r/m selects the source. The destination becomes
the two little-endian u64 qwords `[old_DEST[1], SRC[1]]`; low qwords are ignored.
PUNPCKHQDQ has no MMX form, so bare `0F 6D /r` is rejected. The profile assumes
SSE2 and CR0.EM=0, CR0.TS=0, CR4.OSFXSR=1; feature/control gates, memory, MMX,
other prefixes, REX.W/X, VEX/EVEX, JIT/native execution, guest exception
delivery and physical acceptance are excluded. S2-34, S2-35, and global
S2-35 → S2-34 remain open. See the
[S2-35.31 plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-3531--local-only-bounded-register-punpckhqdq).

## Local register-only `PAND` profile — S2-35.49

The exact schema-v2 fixture profile `s2-long-pand-reg-v1` admits only legacy
`66 [one optional REX.R/B] 0F DB /r` with ModR/M.mod=3. Mandatory `66`
selects the XMM/SSE2 form; bare `0F DB /r` is MMX and rejected. ModR/M.reg is
the destination and ModR/M.r/m the source, independently extended to XMM0–15
by REX.R and REX.B. Execution snapshots the source and computes the raw 128-bit
AND into the destination. Aliasing is supported. No memory callback occurs;
RFLAGS, MXCSR, x87, GPRs, and non-destination XMM registers are preserved.

Only the exact bounded byte form is admitted. REX.W/X, any other or duplicate
prefix, memory operands, VEX and EVEX are excluded. SSE2 availability,
CR0.EM=0, CR0.TS=0 and CR4.OSFXSR=1 are diagnostic preconditions; this profile

physical execution remain unsupported. See the
[S2-35.49 plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-3549--local-only-bounded-register-pand).

## Local register-only `PAVGB` profile — S2-35.52

The schema-v2 profile `s2-long-pavgb-reg-v1` admits long-mode
`66 [one optional REX.R/B] 0F E0 /r` only with ModR/M.mod=3. Mandatory `66`
selects the XMM/SSE2 form; unprefixed `0F E0 /r` is MMX and rejected. ModR/M.reg
is the destination and ModR/M.r/m is the source; REX.R and REX.B independently
select XMM0–XMM15. For each of the 16 unsigned byte lanes, execution computes
`(old_DEST + old_SRC + 1) >> 1` using an intermediate wider than 8 bits. The
source is snapshotted before the destination changes, so aliasing computes a
rounded self-average correctly. No data-memory callback occurs; RFLAGS, MXCSR,
x87, GPRs, and every non-destination XMM register are preserved.

Only this exact register form is admitted. MMX, memory, REX.W/X, other or
duplicate prefixes, VEX/EVEX, and PAVGW are excluded. SSE2 availability,
CR0.EM=0, CR0.TS=0 and CR4.OSFXSR=1 are diagnostic preconditions; this profile
does not implement those gates or `#UD/#NM` delivery. JIT/native admission and
physical execution remain unsupported. Semantics source: Intel SDM revision
093, Vol. 2B, PAVGB/PAVGW ([official PDF](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/929354/253667-093-sdm-vol-2b.pdf)).
See the [S2-35.52 plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-3552--local-only-bounded-register-pavgb).


## Local register-only MOVAPS profile — S2-34.11

The exact diagnostic profile `s2-long-movaps-reg-v1` admits long-mode `[one optional REX.R/B] 0F 28 /r` only when ModR/M.mod=3. ModR/M.reg is the XMM destination and r/m is the source; REX.R and REX.B independently select XMM8–XMM15. The interpreter copies all 128 raw source bits, including arbitrary floating-point bit patterns, and changes no flags, MXCSR, x87, GPRs, or other XMM registers. Alias/self-copy is supported; execution performs no data-memory access.

Memory, reverse-direction `0F 29`, MOVUPS `0F 10`, mandatory-66 MOVAPD, F2/F3, segment/address/LOCK prefixes, duplicate REX, REX.W/X, VEX/EVEX, and incomplete instruction fetches are outside the profile. SSE preconditions (CR0.EM=0, CR0.TS=0, CR4.OSFXSR=1) are assumptions; missing local SSE state refuses without commit. Alignment and memory fault semantics, real #UD/#NM gates, JIT/native execution, and physical execution are not modeled. This does not imply acceptance of parent S2-34 or coverage of MOVUPS/MOVAPD. See the [S2-34.11 plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-3411--local-only-register-movaps).

## Local register-only reverse-direction MOVAPS profile — S2-34.12

destination. Therefore `0F 29 C1` copies XMM0 to XMM1, and `45 0F 29 C1`

flags state, and performs no data-memory access. Missing local SSE state refuses
without commit. CR0.EM=0, CR0.TS=0 and CR4.OSFXSR=1 are assumed preconditions.

Memory, forward-direction `0F 28`, MOVUPS `0F 11`, mandatory-66 MOVAPD, F2/F3,
segment/address/LOCK prefixes, duplicate REX, REX.W/X, VEX/EVEX and incomplete
instruction fetches are outside this profile. Alignment and memory fault
semantics, real #UD/#NM gates, JIT/native execution and physical execution are
not modeled; the register-only profile makes no aligned-memory claim. This
slice does not imply acceptance of parent S2-34/S2-35. See the

## Local register-only MOVUPD profile — S2-34.15

## Local profile S2-34.21: `s2-long-movupd-mem-load-v1`

This local diagnostic profile admits long-mode `66 [optional REX.R only]
0F 10 /r` only for ModR/M.mod=00, r/m=000, the exact `[RAX]` address. REX is
absent, `40`, or `44`; destination is ModR/M.reg plus REX.R. It reads exactly
16 bytes once into temporary storage, validates the complete canonical-48
address range and overflow before data access, then commits all 128 destination
bits and RIP only after a successful read. Unaligned accesses are accepted by
this local backend contract; no hardware alignment or `#AC` behavior is claimed.

Displacement, SIB, RIP-relative, address-size override, REX.W/X/B, extra or
misordered prefixes, VEX/EVEX, MOVUPS and scalar profiles remain separate or
unsupported. Missing SSE state, failed range validation, memory/backend error
and truncated fetch do not commit CPU state. JIT/native admission and physical
execution remain closed; parent S2-34 remains open and physical status is
`not_run`.

## Local profile S2-34.17: `s2-long-xorpd-reg-v1`

This separate schema-v2 diagnostic profile admits exactly long-mode `66 [one optional REX.R/B] 0F 57 /r` with ModR/M.mod=3. Mandatory `66` selects legacy packed-double XORPD; ModR/M.reg plus REX.R selects destination XMM0–XMM15 and ModR/M.r/m plus REX.B selects source XMM0–XMM15. Intel SDM revision 093, Vol. 2B, XORPD entry defines this 128-bit bitwise XOR; VEX/EVEX and memory forms are excluded.

Execution XORs all 128 raw bits without host floating-point conversion, supports destination/source aliasing, and changes no MXCSR, x87, GPR, RFLAGS or other XMM register. It makes no data-memory access. SSE2 availability, CR0.EM=0, CR0.TS=0 and CR4.OSFXSR=1 are assumed profile preconditions; control gates and `#UD`/`#NM` are not modeled. Missing SSE state and truncated fetch refuse atomically. Native/JIT admission and physical execution are not supported or claimed, and parent S2-34 remains open. See the [S2-34.17 plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-3417--local-only-register-xorpd) and [fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-3417-local-register-xorpd-diagnostic-profile).

## Local profile S2-34.20: `s2-long-andnpd-reg-v1`

This separate schema-v2 diagnostic profile admits only long-mode `66 [one optional REX.R/B] 0F 55 /r` with ModR/M.mod=3. ModR/M.reg plus REX.R selects destination XMM0–XMM15; ModR/M.r/m plus REX.B selects source. Intel SDM revision 093, Vol. 2B, ANDNPD defines destination bits as `(~old_destination) & source` ([official Volume 2B PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671241)). Operand order is significant: `66 0F 55 C1` writes `~XMM0 & XMM1`, not `XMM0 & ~XMM1`.

Execution computes all 128 bits as raw bytes. It supports aliases, where self-ANDNPD produces zero, changes no MXCSR, x87, GPR, RFLAGS or other XMM register, and makes no data-memory access. Missing local SSE state and truncated instruction fetch refuse atomically. Only mandatory `66` and at most one effective REX.R/B are accepted; other prefixes, REX.W/X, memory operands, VEX/EVEX, and neighboring XORPD/ANDPD/ORPD/PANDN encodings are rejected. Legacy ANDNPS remains separate. SSE2 and CR0/CR4 prerequisites are assumed; control gates and `#UD`/`#NM` delivery are outside this profile. JIT/native admission and physical execution are not supported or claimed; parent S2-34 remains open and physical status is `not_run`. See the [S2-34.20 plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-3420--local-only-register-andnpd) and [fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-3420-local-register-andnpd-diagnostic-profile).

## Local register-only `PADDSW` profile — S2-35.12

The diagnostic fixture profile `s2-long-paddsw-reg-v1` accepts only legacy
`66 [one optional REX.R/B] 0F ED /r` with ModR/M.mod=3. The `66` mandatory
prefix selects XMM/SSE2 from the bare MMX encoding. ModR/M.reg is destination;
ModR/M.r/m is source; REX.R/B extend each register to XMM15. Eight independent
little-endian signed i16 lanes are summed in i32 and clamped to the signed word
range. Only destination XMM and RIP change. Flags, MXCSR, x87 and other XMM/GPR
state are preserved; no data memory callback is made. Missing raw x87/SSE state
and unsupported/truncated encodings are rejected atomically by this local
interpreter profile. SSE2 availability, CR0.EM=0, CR0.TS=0 and CR4.OSFXSR=1 are
assumptions, not modeled gates. No CPUID, guest exception-delivery, memory,
native/JIT, or physical-hardware claim is made. The literal fixture and local
coverage are documented in [the S2-35.12 plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-3512--local-only-bounded-register-paddsw).

## Local profile S2-34.22: `s2-long-movupd-mem-store-v1`

Admits only long-mode `66 [optional REX.R only] 0F 11 /r` with ModR/M.mod=00 and r/m=000, exactly `[RAX]`. Accepted REX bytes are absent, `40`, and `44`; REX.R extends ModR/M.reg to source XMM0–15. REX.W/X/B, displacement, SIB, RIP-relative and address-size override forms are rejected. The interpreter validates the complete `[RAX,RAX+15]` range for canonical48 and u64 overflow, copies source bytes into a local `[u8;16]`, then issues exactly one `GuestMemory::write` and commits RIP only after success. No data reads are made. The local profile permits unaligned access and makes no hardware alignment, atomicity, MMIO, SMP, `#AC`, or fault-priority claim. CPU state is preserved on missing SSE state, invalid range, fetch/budget/stop refusal, and backend write error. Arbitrary `GuestMemory` backends may partially alter memory before returning an error; only the known all-or-error FlatMemory fixture behavior guarantees memory rollback. JIT and native execution remain denied; SSE2 preconditions are assumed. Parent S2-34 remains open; physical execution is `not_run`; ISSUE-012 remains open.


## Local profile S2-34.23: `s2-long-movupd-mem-base-v1`

This separate schema-v2 diagnostic profile admits long-mode `66 [one optional REX.R/B] 0F 10/11 /r` with ModR/M memory modes 00/01/10, an ordinary 64-bit GPR base, and absent/signed disp8/signed disp32. ModR/M.reg plus REX.R selects XMM0–15; ModR/M.r/m plus REX.B selects the base. SIB (`r/m=100`), mod=00/rm=101 RIP-relative (including REX.B), register mode, REX.W/X, address-size 32, segment overrides and other malformed/extra legacy mandatory prefixes, scalar F2/F3, VEX and EVEX are rejected. RSP/R12 are unavailable without SIB; RBP/R13 require mod=01/10 displacement forms. The older exact `[RAX]` MOVUPS/MOVUPD profiles retain their previous admissions.

The decoder reuses `rm_operand`; execution uses the shared `MemoryOperand` full canonical48 and range/overflow checks for the entire 16-byte span. Loads issue one 16-byte `GuestMemory::read` into temporary storage and commit the complete raw XMM destination plus RIP only on success. Stores capture the complete raw XMM source, issue one 16-byte write, and commit RIP only on success. Unaligned accesses are accepted in this local diagnostic backend. Backend failure preserves CPU state; no rollback is claimed for arbitrary memory backends. Default segment attribution is inherited: RBP noncanonical accesses report #SS; R13 reports #GP.

Handwritten local fixtures use `66 45 0F 10 81 01 00 00 00` for `[R9+1]` load to XMM8 and `66 45 0F 11 40 F9` for XMM8 store to `[R8-7]`. Tests cover both directions, extended base/register axes, signed displacement endpoints/extrema, strict profile negatives (including RIP-relative disp32 targeting mapped data), truncation, one data callback, no CPU commit on injected backend error, interpreter output/canaries and JIT denial. SSE2/control-state preconditions are assumed; #UD/#NM delivery, hardware alignment behavior, physical execution and arbitrary-backend memory rollback are outside scope. Native admission is denied; parent S2-34 remains open, physical status is `not_run`, and ISSUE-012 remains open. See the [S2-34.23 plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-3423--local-only-movupd-basedisplacement-memory-forms) and [fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-3423-local-movupd-memory-base-diagnostic-profile).

## Local register-only `PAVGW` profile — S2-35.53

The `s2-long-pavgw-reg-v1` profile admits only long-mode `66 [REX.R/B] 0F E3 /r` with ModR/M.mod=3. REX.R extends the destination XMM index and REX.B extends the source index independently through XMM15. It computes each unsigned 16-bit lane as `(a + b + 1) >> 1`, using a widened intermediate; source/destination aliasing is valid. All other state is preserved and the instruction performs no data-memory access. SSE2 and CR0/CR4 prerequisites are assumed by this local diagnostic profile. MMX, memory, VEX, EVEX, other prefix combinations, CPUID advertisement, JIT/native admission, and physical admission remain unsupported. The opcode and operation are specified in Intel SDM revision 093, Vol. 2B, PAVGW ([official PDF](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/929354/253667-093-sdm-vol-2b.pdf)).

## Local S2-36a: raw binary32/binary64 classification and finite normalization

`Binary32` and `Binary64` are immutable raw-bit wrappers. `from_bits` and
`to_bits` preserve every encoding bit; accessors expose sign, biased exponent,
fraction, and `BinaryClass` (`Zero`, `Subnormal`, `Normal`, `Infinity`,
`QuietNaN`, or `SignalingNaN`). NaN sign and payload and signed zero are
preserved. Classification does not quiet a signaling NaN. Equality on the raw
wrappers means bit identity, not guest floating-point equality.

Binary32 uses sign bit 31, exponent bits 30:23, and fraction bits 22:0;
Binary64 uses sign bit 63, exponent bits 62:52, and fraction bits 51:0. An
all-zero exponent and fraction encodes signed zero; an all-zero exponent with
nonzero fraction is subnormal; an intermediate exponent encodes a normal with
an implicit leading one. An all-ones exponent with zero fraction is infinity;
with nonzero fraction it is a NaN: the most significant fraction bit 1 marks
`QuietNaN`, and 0 marks `SignalingNaN`.

`normalize_finite() -> Option<BinaryFinite>` returns an exact integer-only view
for zero and finite values, with the source class retained. Every nonzero
finite view uses the invariant `(-1)^sign × significand × 2^(exponent−63)` and
has significand bit 63 set. Zero retains its sign and has zero significand and
exponent; infinity and NaNs return `None`. This helper performs no floating-
point operation or rounding and changes no CPU or FP status state.

This is a reusable representation/classification primitive, not an arithmetic
engine. It defines no rounding, NaN propagation, conversion, flags/exceptions,
DAZ/FTZ, SSE instruction behavior, or x87 state transition. S2-36 remains open
for arithmetic/rounding/exception semantics, and S2-37/S2-38 remain open. The
encoding source is Intel SDM Vol. 1 Rev. 093 (September 2026), §§4.2.2/Table
4-3 and 4.8.3.1–4 ([official Intel PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/929351)).
Independent Sol medium code review completed clean; no findings remain.
Implementation and test status are recorded in the
[Stage 2 report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-36a--raw-binary32binary64-classification-and-finite-normalization)
and [plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-36a--raw-binary32binary64-classification-and-finite-normalization).

## Local S2-36b: exact finite significand multiplication

`multiply_finite_significands(lhs: BinaryFinite, rhs: BinaryFinite) ->
(bool, i32, u128)` is a pure mathematical helper over the exact finite views
from S2-36a. For nonzero operands, the tuple is `(sign, exponent, magnitude)`:
`sign = lhs.sign XOR rhs.sign`, `magnitude` is the full unsigned 128-bit
product of the two 64-bit significands, and
`exponent = lhs.exponent + rhs.exponent + 1`. It represents the exact product
`(-1)^sign × magnitude × 2^(exponent−127)`. The full product is returned
without shifting, truncation, sticky-bit formation, rounding, or packing.
Because each normalized input significand is in `[2^63, 2^64−1]`, the product
magnitude's leading bit is 126 or 127; the bounded input exponent range
produces result exponents −2147…2047.

If either input is zero, the helper returns `(false, 0, 0)`, regardless of operand signs or order. This is a signless mathematical-zero sentinel, not an architectural `+0` result. NaNs and infinities are outside the `BinaryFinite` domain. The helper returns no FP class or status, mutates no CPU state, and does not alter existing x87 state or helper behavior.

The tuple and its scale are a project mathematical contract, not a result
layout mandated by Intel. The underlying significand/value model and binary
formats follow Intel SDM Vol. 1 Rev. 093 (September 2026), §§4.8.2,
4.2.2/Table 4-3, and 4.8.4; §4.8.3.1 covers signed zero, which this sentinel
leaves to a later operation-specific decision
([official Intel PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/929351)). S2-36
rounding and exceptions, and S2-37/S2-38 instruction behavior, remain open.
Independent Sol medium code review completed clean; no findings remain. See
the [Stage 2 report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-36b--exact-finite-significand-multiplication)
and [plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-36b--exact-finite-significand-multiplication)
for tests and claim limits.

## Local S2-36c: exact finite quotient and remainder

`divide_finite_significands` accepts two `BinaryFinite` values and returns
`Option<BinaryFiniteQuotient>`. The result has private sign, exponent, quotient,
remainder, and denominator fields exposed through public `const` read-only
getters. It is an
exact mathematical decomposition, not a rounded destination value.

For nonzero operands, let `a` and `d` be the normalized significands of the
left and right inputs. If `a >= d`, set `N = u128(a) << 63` and
`e = lhs.exponent - rhs.exponent`; otherwise set `N = u128(a) << 64` and
decrement `e` by one. Set `q = N / d`, `r = N % d`, and sign to the XOR of
input signs. Preserve the original denominator `d` without reduction. The
exact quotient is `(-1)^sign × (q + r/d) × 2^(e−63)`, with `2^63 <= q < 2^64`
and `0 <= r < d`. The numerator fits `u128`, and the result exponent is
bounded to −2098…2097.

A zero denominator returns `None`, including for 0/0. This means the
mathematical quotient is undefined; it is not guest `#DE` delivery. A zero
numerator with nonzero denominator returns sign=false, exponent=0, quotient=0,
remainder=0 and preserves the actual denominator. This signless zero sentinel
does not select a guest zero sign. NaNs/infinities are outside the
`BinaryFinite` domain. No rounding, packing, exception/status state, CPU
mutation, or x87 behavior is added.

The quotient/remainder representation is a project mathematical contract;
Intel specifies the floating-point value model and rounding boundary, not this
tuple layout. The normative context is Intel SDM Vol. 1 Rev. 093 (September
2026), §§4.8.2, 4.8.4, 4.8.3.1, and 4.9
([official Intel PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/929351)). S2-36
rounding/packing and S2-37/S2-38 instruction behavior remain open.
Independent Sol medium code review completed clean; both reported findings
were resolved, and no findings remain. See the
[Stage 2 report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-36c--exact-finite-quotient-and-remainder)
and [plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-36c--exact-finite-quotient-and-remainder).

## Local S2-36d: shared exact rational precision rounding

`binary_float::round_quotient_to_precision(sign, q, r, d, precision, mode)`
returns `Option<(u128, bool)>`: an unsigned rounded magnitude and an `inexact`
indicator. It rounds the exact mathematical coefficient
`(-1)^sign * (q + r/d)` to precision 1…64. The supported mathematical modes
are nearest ties to even, toward zero, toward positive, and toward negative.
`RationalRoundingMode` is defined in a private shared module and re-exported
from both `binary_float` and `x87`.

For nonzero normalized `q`, let `k = 64 - precision`. The result keeps the top
`precision` bits as an integer magnitude; the rounded coefficient represented
by that magnitude is `magnitude * 2^k`. When composed with an S2-36c division
result with exponent `e`, its represented value is
`(-1)^sign * magnitude * 2^(e + 1 - precision)`. The rounding increment is
determined from the discarded low bits together with the exact rational
remainder. `inexact` is true exactly when discarded `q`
bits or `r` are nonzero. Nearest mode compares the full tail, including exact
ties; directed modes increment only when the result is inexact and the
requested direction is away from zero for the value's sign. A carry is
returned as magnitude `2^precision`; this helper does not change an exponent
or pack a floating-point encoding. A zero coefficient returns `(0, false)`;
no signed zero is selected.

The helper returns `None` for precision outside 1…64, `d == 0`, `r >= d`, a
nonzero `q < 2^63`, or `q == 0 && r != 0`. The existing public
`x87::round_quotient_to_precision` signature remains `Option<u128>` and
delegates to the shared helper while discarding the inexact indicator. Its
previous result behavior remains covered by x87 tests. This mathematical
contract adds no exponent adjustment, packing, status flags, exceptions, or
instruction execution. S2-36 rounding integration and S2-37/S2-38 remain open.
Normative context: Intel SDM Vol. 1 Rev. 093 (September 2026), §§4.8.2, 4.8.4,
4.8.3.1, and 4.9
([official Intel PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/929351)).
Independent Sol medium code review completed clean; no findings remain. See the
[Stage 2 report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-36d--shared-exact-rational-precision-rounding)
and [plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-36d--shared-exact-rational-precision-rounding).

## Local S2-36e: pack an already-rounded normal binary value

`Binary32::pack_normal_rounded_significand(sign, exponent, magnitude)` and
`Binary64::pack_normal_rounded_significand(...)` pack only already-rounded
normal significands, with fixed precision 24 or 53. The magnitude must satisfy
`2^(precision-1) <= magnitude <= 2^precision` and represents
`(-1)^sign * magnitude * 2^(exponent + 1 - precision)`.

When `magnitude == 2^precision`, normalize the carry to `2^(precision-1)` and
checked-increment the exponent before checking the format's normal exponent
range. Thus a carry at `exponent == emin - 1` is accepted as minimum normal.
Only after this normalization does the helper apply the normal exponent bounds.
For example, a noncarry at `emin - 1`, or a carry whose incremented exponent is
outside the normal range, returns `None`.

`None` describes an input outside this normal-packing helper's domain; it is
not a guest exception. The helpers do not round, pack zero or subnormals, define
underflow/overflow policy, or update status/exceptions. The caller retains the
S2-36d `inexact` indication. No x87 packer behavior changes. S2-36
rounding/exceptions and S2-37/S2-38 remain open; hardware validation is
deferred. The focused test suite passed 14/14; author-reported workspace,
formatting, diff, and Graphify checks passed. Independent Sol medium code
review completed clean; no findings remain. See the
[Stage 2 report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-36e--pack-an-already-rounded-normal-binary-value)
and [plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-36e--pack-an-already-rounded-normal-binary-value).

## Local S2-36f: direct exact quotient rounding to subnormal units

`Binary32::round_pack_subnormal_quotient(sign, exponent, quotient, remainder,
denominator, mode)` and the `Binary64` counterpart return
`Option<(Self, bool)>`: the raw format value and an `inexact` indication. They
consume the original S2-36c exact quotient decomposition and round it directly
in units of the least subnormal. They must not round to normal precision and
then shift the rounded result into the subnormal range, which risks double
rounding at the largest-subnormal/minimum-normal boundary.

For an exact quotient coefficient `(-1)^sign * (q + r/d)` at S2-36c exponent
`e`, the signed value in least-subnormal units is
`(-1)^sign * (q + r/d) * 2^(-k)`, where the widened integer `k = 63 + L - e`.
Binary32 uses `L=-149`, precision 24, `emin=-126`;
binary64 uses `L=-1074`, precision 53, `emin=-1022`. For `k <= 63`, round the
original `q/r/d` directly through the S2-36d helper at precision `64-k`. For
`k == 64`, handle the half-unit boundary explicitly, with ties-to-even going
to zero. For `k > 64`, nearest and toward-zero return zero; directed modes
return one least-subnormal unit only in the directed sign. Both branches for
`k >= 64` report `inexact=true` for every admitted nonzero quotient; `k <= 63`
uses S2-36d's exact inexactness result. Preserve the input sign bit in the raw
output even when the magnitude rounds to zero.

Reject `e >= emin`, `quotient < 2^63` (including exact zero), a zero
denominator, or `remainder >= denominator` with `None`. `None` denotes an input
outside this helper's domain, not a guest fault. Return only `inexact`; do not
set underflow, update MXCSR, deliver exceptions, or modify x87 behavior. No
physical execution is claimed. S2-36 exception delivery and S2-37/S2-38 remain
open. Author reports the focused binary tests passed 18/18, along with
workspace, formatting, diff, and Graphify checks. The Graphify update repeated
its existing `include/open_desktop/host_abi.h` line-68 syntax warning and
suggested label refresh after community changes. Independent Sol medium code

## Local S2-36g: bounded exact aligned addition

`add_finite_aligned(lhs, rhs)` returns `Option<(bool, i32, u128)>`. A nonzero
result represents exactly `(-1)^sign * magnitude * 2^(exponent - 63)`. The
helper chooses the smaller input exponent as the common exponent, left-shifts
the higher-exponent significand by the exponent gap in `u128`, and accepts gaps
through 64. Same-sign aligned magnitudes are added. Opposite-sign magnitudes
are subtracted, with the larger magnitude's sign retained. Exact cancellation
returns `(false, 0, 0)`.

A zero operand returns the other operand's sign, exponent, and significand;
two zero operands return the signless zero sentinel. Gaps greater than 64
return `None` because they are outside this bounded helper profile. `None` is
not guest overflow. The helper does not round, jam, report inexactness, normalize
the final result, pack a binary value, or choose a guest zero sign. It performs
no host floating-point operations and does not reuse/change x87 jam helpers.
Broader addition, wider gaps, final normalization, packing, and instruction
behavior remain open. Author reports `binary_float::tests` passing 21/21 and
workspace, formatting, diff, and Graphify checks passing; Graphify noted the
existing `include/open_desktop/host_abi.h` extractor warning and label refresh.
Independent Sol code review completed clean; no findings remain. See the
[Stage 2 report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-36g--bounded-exact-aligned-addition)
and [plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-36g--bounded-exact-aligned-addition).

## Local S2-36h: finite binary division composition

`Binary32::divide_finite(lhs, rhs, mode)` and `Binary64::divide_finite(...)`
return `Option<(Self, bool)>`: the destination encoding plus final mathematical
`inexact`. They accept `BinaryFinite` inputs, reject either zero input with
`None`, and therefore define neither zero division nor guest `#DE`. NaNs and
infinities are outside the input type's finite domain.

Each helper reuses one exact S2-36c quotient/remainder decomposition, then
branches on that original quotient exponent. Destination format selects
precision and normal exponent threshold: binary32 p=24/emin=-126, binary64
p=53/emin=-1022, even for mixed-format operands. At or above `emin`, use
S2-36d once and pack with S2-36e. Below `emin`, use S2-36f's direct subnormal
unit rounding from the original quotient; do not round normally then shift,
which can double-round at the largest-subnormal/minimum-normal boundary.

`None` includes out-of-range results such as overflow and is not a guest
exception. The returned boolean describes only mathematical inexactness. No
MXCSR PE/underflow status, exception delivery, or guest zero-sign policy is
implemented. If a nonzero result underflows to zero, the raw result retains the
quotient sign. No x87 helpers or behavior are changed. Broader arithmetic and
S2-37/S2-38 instruction/exception work remain open; hardware validation is
deferred. Author-reported focused tests passed 24/24, with workspace, format,
diff, and Graphify checks passing; independent Sol review completed clean, with
no findings. See the
[Stage 2 report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-36h--finite-binary-division-composition)
and [plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-36h--finite-binary-division-composition).

## Local S2-36i: finite binary multiplication composition

`Binary32::multiply_finite(lhs, rhs, mode)` and `Binary64::multiply_finite(...)`
return `Option<(Self, bool)>`: a destination encoding and final mathematical
`inexact`. They accept finite normalized values and return `None` for either
zero operand; they do not define guest zero multiplication, guest exceptions,
or NaN/infinity behavior. For nonzero operands the result retains the XOR sign,
including a signed zero when a tiny product rounds to zero.

The product composition uses a private, bounded normalized-product bridge. The
exact `u128` significand product has at least 22 trailing zero bits because
each normalized binary32/binary64 significand has at least 11. After at most
one left shift to normalize, the even low 64-bit half is split into
`remainder = low_half / 2` with denominator `2^63`, preserving the exact
quotient/remainder decomposition. This bridge is specialized to the formats;
it is not a generic conversion framework and does not reuse x87 jam helpers.

Destination format selects p=24/emin=-126 or p=53/emin=-1022. Compose the exact
product with one normal S2-36d round plus S2-36e packing, or use direct S2-36f
subnormal-unit rounding from the bridge without an intermediate rounding step.
Only final mathematical `inexact` is returned. No flags, exceptions, or x87
behavior change. Broader arithmetic and S2-37/S2-38 remain open; hardware
validation is deferred. Author-reported tests passed 27/27 with workspace,
formatting, diff, and Graphify checks. Independent Sol code review completed
clean; no findings remain. See
the [Stage 2 report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-36i--finite-binary-multiplication-composition)
and [plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-36i--finite-binary-multiplication-composition).

## Local S2-36j: finite binary addition composition

`Binary32::add_finite_aligned(lhs, rhs, mode)` and
`Binary64::add_finite_aligned(...)` return `Option<(Self, bool)>`: a
destination encoding and final mathematical `inexact`. Inputs are finite
normalized `BinaryFinite` values. Alignment is bounded to exponent gaps of at
most 64; a wider gap returns `None`. A single zero operand returns the other
operand rounded to the selected destination. Both-zero and exact-cancellation
results return `None`; this helper does not select the guest zero sign.
Overflow rejection is `None`, not a guest exception. No flags, exception
delivery, or NaN/infinity policy are defined.

For nonzero inputs, align their unsigned significands to the smaller exponent
in `u128`. Equal signs add magnitudes; opposite signs subtract the smaller
magnitude from the larger and take the larger magnitude's sign. The exact
aligned result is `(-1)^sign * magnitude * 2^(exponent-63)`. A private
normalization bridge moves the highest set bit to bit 127, adjusting the
exponent without losing bits. Each normalized binary32/binary64 significand
has at least 11 trailing zero bits, and the bounded alignment, addition or
subtraction, and normalization preserve an even normalized magnitude. Thus
the private bridge can split it exactly as `q=(N>>64)`, `r=(N low64)>>1`,
`d=2^63`, representing
`(-1)^sign * (q + r/d) * 2^(e-63)`. The proof is specialized to the existing
binary32/binary64 input domain and is not a generic arbitrary-integer bridge.

The destination controls precision and normal threshold, including for mixed
formats: binary32 uses p=24 and emin=-126; binary64 uses p=53 and emin=-1022.
If the exact normalized exponent is normal, use one S2-36d round followed by
S2-36e packing. Otherwise use S2-36f directly from the original exact
quotient/remainder. This avoids both intermediate precision rounding and
normal-then-subnormal double rounding. For a nonzero exact sum that rounds to
zero, the result keeps the sum's sign; `inexact` reports only mathematical
rounding. x87 APIs and behavior are unchanged.

Literal coverage includes `successor(1)+(-1)=+2^-52` and
`(-successor(1))+1=-2^-52` deep cancellation, exact minimum subnormals,
same-sign addition and opposite-sign subtraction, gap 64 accepted
and gap 65 rejected in both operand orders, zero-neutral behavior, mixed
binary32/binary64 inputs, and input immutability. The normal double-round
regression
`0x3ff0_0000_0000_0001 + 0x3c9f_ffff_ffff_ffff` rounds to
`0x3ff0_0000_0000_0001` with `inexact=true`; the binary64-to-binary32
subnormal regression rounds directly to largest subnormal `0x007f_ffff`,
also inexact. Author-reported `binary_float::tests` passed 30/30;
`cargo fmt --all -- --check && git diff --check` and
`cargo check --workspace --all-targets --offline` passed. `graphify update .`
completed at 7776 nodes/15361 edges with the known
`include/open_desktop/host_abi.h` syntax warning and label-refresh notice.
Independent Sol review completed clean, with no findings. Wider gaps, standalone subtraction,
overflow/exception policy, broader S2-36 arithmetic, S2-37/S2-38 instruction
work, and hardware validation remain open. See the
[Stage 2 report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-36j--finite-binary-addition-composition)
and [plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-36j--finite-binary-addition-composition).

## Local S2-36k: finite binary subtraction composition

`Binary32::subtract_finite_aligned(lhs, rhs, mode)` and
`Binary64::subtract_finite_aligned(...)` return `Option<(Self, bool)>`. The
wrapper negates the sign of a copied right `BinaryFinite` and delegates to
the corresponding S2-36j bounded addition helper. It does not mutate either
input. It consequently inherits the exponent-gap limit of 64, exact
alignment/normalization bridge, destination precision and rounding mode,
normal one-round path, direct subnormal path, and `None` result for overflow.
Only finite normalized inputs are admitted; this API defines no guest
exception delivery, floating-point status flags, or x87 changes.

Exact cancellation and both-zero inputs yield `None` in every rounding mode,
so guest signed-zero selection remains undefined here. A single zero operand
acts according to subtraction: `x-0` returns `x`, while `0-x` returns its
sign-negated value, rounded to the selected destination. If a nonzero exact
difference rounds to zero, the resulting signed-zero encoding retains the
exact difference's sign. The boolean is mathematical `inexact` only.

Literal tests include `1.5-1` and `1-1.5` in binary32 and binary64,
successor-of-one deep cancellation, exact minimum-subnormal results from
minimum-normal minus maximum-subnormal, both-zero and exact-cancellation
rejection in all four modes, zero identity and negation, and tiny
positive/negative differences under all four modes.
They also cover mixed formats, gap 64 accepted and 65
rejected in both operand orders, overflow rejection, and input immutability.
The normal double-round regression computes
`0x3ff0_0000_0000_0001 - 0xbc9f_ffff_ffff_ffff` as binary64 and expects
`0x3ff0_0000_0000_0001` with `inexact=true`. The direct subnormal regression
computes binary64 `0x3810_0000_0000_0000 - 0x3690_0000_0000_0001` into
binary32 and expects largest subnormal `0x007f_ffff` with `inexact=true`.
Across all four modes, equal positive and equal negative nonzero inputs return
`None` for both binary32 and binary64 sources and destinations; the binary64
signed-zero pair matrix also returns `None`.

## Local S2-36l: finite binary comparison

`compare_finite(lhs: BinaryFinite, rhs: BinaryFinite) ->
core::cmp::Ordering` provides numeric ordering for two finite normalized
values. Either signed zero compares Equal to the other signed zero, but
`Binary32` and `Binary64` retain raw-bit equality, so their positive and
negative zero encodings remain distinct under `Eq`. No wrapper `Eq`/`Ord`
implementation changes. Host floating-point operations are not used.

For nonzero finite operands, a negative value is less than a positive value.
If the signs match, compare `(exponent, significand)` lexicographically; for
negative values reverse that magnitude ordering. This order spans both source
formats because `BinaryFinite` represents the exact normalized mathematical
value independently of binary32/binary64 encoding precision.

## Local S2-36v: raw binary64-to-binary32 narrowing

`Binary32::narrow_from_binary64(source, mode) -> BinaryArithmeticResult<Binary32>`
converts one raw binary64 value using an explicit `RationalRoundingMode`.
Signed zero and signed infinity are preserved. A finite nonzero value is
normalized exactly and sent directly through the existing binary32 target
precision/range round-and-pack path once; the result reports that final
conversion's `inexact`, `overflow`, and `tiny_after_precision_rounding`
diagnostics. No host floating point, intermediate binary32 arithmetic, CPU or
MXCSR state, DAZ/FTZ, instruction dispatch, or architectural exception
delivery is involved.

NaN sign is preserved and the source fraction is truncated by dropping its
lowest 29 bits. A signaling NaN is quieted by setting the binary32 quiet bit
and reports local `invalid_operation=true`; a quiet NaN reports false. NaNs
have no rounding diagnostics. The source encoding is not mutated.

Literal tests cover signed zeros/infinities, QNaN/SNaN truncation boundaries,
exact finite encodings, both signs of ties under all rounding modes,
subnormal/tiny-after-precision-rounding boundaries, and positive and negative
overflow modes. Provenance is Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 1 Table D-12 for NaN
conversion and Vol. 2A `CVTSD2SS` §3-234–235 for rounding control
([Vol. 1](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/929351),
[Vol. 2A](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199)). These sources
support this local conversion contract, not instruction admission or hardware
validation. See the [Stage 2 plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-36v--raw-binary64-to-binary32-narrowing)
and [report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-36v--raw-binary64-to-binary32-narrowing).

The schema-v2 diagnostic profile `s2-long-rcpss-reg-v1` admits exactly one
Long64 legacy register instruction, `F3 [optional adjacent REX.R/B] 0F 53 /r`
with ModR/M.mod=3 and XMM0–15. It rejects other prefixes, REX.W/X,
nonadjacent/repeated REX, memory forms, VEX/EVEX, truncation, and neighboring
opcodes. Execution reads the source low dword before writing, applies the
deterministic `Binary32::reciprocal_sse_raw()` helper, and replaces only the
destination low dword. It preserves the destination upper 96 bits, all other
XMM/GPR/x87 state, RFLAGS, MXCSR, and RIP except normal successful retirement.
No data-memory access occurs.

The helper's normal finite policy is exact `1.0/x` rounded to binary32 using
nearest-ties-even, then flush of a subnormal result to signed zero. Signed
zeros/subnormal inputs map to same-sign infinity; infinities map to same-sign
zero; QNaN is preserved and SNaN is quieted according to the existing local
policy. Those result bits are deterministic local reference values, not a
claim of exact CPU output. ISSUE-025 records the published RCPSS/RCPPS
normal/subnormal boundary inequalities that overlap. Final physical checking
must validate relative error `<= 3/8192` for non-flushed normal outputs without
requiring exact bits; the ambiguous tiny-result boundary remains a separate

Full fetch precedes SSE bit 25, CR0.EM/CR4.OSFXSR #UD and CR0.TS #NM checks. MXCSR admission requires supported bits only, all six exception masks set, DAZ=FTZ=0 and reserved bits clear. RC and prior sticky flags are accepted and preserved; no SIMD exception or #XM delivery is modeled.

AC=1 returns local Unsupported before span checks or data callbacks; AC=0 accepts unaligned RAX. Checked `[RAX,RAX+3]` endpoints must both be canonical48 before exactly one read4. Read failure preserves CPU/SSE/MXCSR/RIP, memory and retirement. The source is the memory dword only. On success, `Binary32::reciprocal_sqrt_sse_raw()` replaces XMM0.low32, preserving XMM0.high96, all other state, MXCSR and memory, then RIP advances four bytes and the instruction retires once. The independent schema validator checks special-value relations and the `3/8192` relative-error envelope for positive normal outputs using integer arithmetic; the deterministic reference does not claim physical hardware bit equality.

JIT, native, generic, fragment and C ABI routes remain denied. No physical x86 acceptance is claimed. See the [S2-37eb plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-37eb--local-long64-memory-legacy-rsqrtss-at-rax), [report](../reports/S2_37EB_RSQRTSS_MEMORY.md), and [fixture](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/s2_37eb_rsqrtss_m32_memory_rhs.case.json).

## Local S2-37e register-only MINSS with masked status

The schema-v2 profile `s2-long-minss-reg-masked-v1` admits exactly one Long64
legacy `F3 [optional adjacent REX.R/B] 0F 5D /r` instruction with ModR/M.mod=3
and XMM0–15. It requires SSE state, all MXCSR exception masks set, DAZ and FTZ
clear, and reserved MXCSR bits 16–31 zero. Any rounding-control value and
pre-existing sticky bits are permitted. An unsupported profile precondition
returns a local refusal; it does not assert architectural #GP/#XM/#UD delivery.

MINSS selects operand 2 if either operand is QNaN or SNaN and sets IE sticky.
With DAZ clear, a subnormal input sets DE only when this operation does not
also raise invalid; invalid has higher priority than denormal for the same
operation. A pre-existing DE remains sticky. For non-NaNs, value selection uses the existing raw MINSS helper,
including operand-2 selection for equal values/signed zeros. The executor
snapshots both operands before writing, supports aliasing, updates only the
destination low dword and MXCSR IE/DE bits, and preserves the destination upper
96 bits, all other CPU state, and all other MXCSR bits. It performs no data
memory access. JIT, native and CPUID admission remain closed.

Normative source: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 1 §§4.9.2, 11.5 and Appendix D Tables D-9
and D-15, plus Vol. 2B `MINSS`. This is only the masked IE/DE subset consumed by
S2-37e. Unmasked exception delivery, #XM, CR0/CR4/OSXMMEXCPT, memory and
alignment fault ordering, and the rest of S2-38 remain open. Physical
validation is deferred to the combined final Mac mini substage.

legacy `F3 [optional adjacent REX.R/B] 0F 5F /r` register instruction with
ModR/M.mod=3 and XMM0–15. It requires SSE state, all six MXCSR exception masks
set, DAZ/FTZ clear and reserved MXCSR bits 16–31 clear. Any RC and prior sticky
status bits are accepted; unsupported state is refused without asserting
architectural fault delivery.

MAXSS selects operand 2 if either operand is QNaN or SNaN and sets IE sticky.
With DAZ clear, a subnormal input sets DE only when this operation does not
also raise invalid; invalid has higher priority than denormal for the same
operation. A pre-existing DE remains sticky. Otherwise value selection uses the existing raw
MAXSS helper, including operand-2 selection for equal values and signed zeros.
The executor snapshots both low dwords before writing and updates only the
destination low dword and IE/DE bits, preserving the upper 96 destination bits,

Normative source: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 1 §§4.9.2, 11.5 and Appendix D Tables
D-9/D-13/D-15, plus Vol. 2B `MAXSS`. This extends only the masked IE/DE subset

## Local S2-37g register-only MINPS with masked status

The schema-v2 profile `s2-long-minps-reg-masked-v1` admits exactly one Long64
legacy `[optional adjacent REX.R/B] 0F 5D /r` register instruction,
ModR/M.mod=3 and XMM0–15. The F3-prefixed `MINSS` form remains a separate
instruction/profile. The local profile requires SSE state, all six MXCSR
exception masks set, DAZ/FTZ clear and reserved MXCSR bits 16–31 zero. Any RC
and existing sticky flags are permitted. Unsupported profile state is refused
without an architectural #GP/#XM/#UD claim.

Execution snapshots both full XMM operands before computing four independent
little-endian binary32 lanes. Each lane uses the existing raw MINPS selector:
either QNaN or SNaN selects raw operand 2 and contributes IE; a subnormal input
contributes DE while DAZ is clear only if that lane does not also raise invalid.
The effective IE and DE flags aggregate across all lanes, so different lanes
can set both. A pre-existing DE remains sticky. The full destination and
sticky MXCSR IE/DE bits commit together after preflight. Raw RHS NaN payloads
and signalling bits are preserved; equal values and signed-zero ties select
operand 2. Aliasing is supported, other CPU state and MXCSR bits are preserved,
and there are no data-memory accesses.

Normative sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 1 §§4.9.2, 11.5.2, 11.5.3.1
and Appendix D Tables D-9/D-13/D-15, plus Vol. 2B `MINPS`. This expands only the masked IE/DE subset of
S2-38a; unmasked exceptions, #XM delivery/suppression, CR0/CR4/OSXMMEXCPT,
memory and fault ordering, and remaining S2-38 behavior remain open. JIT,
native and CPUID admission remain closed. Physical validation is deferred to
the combined final Mac mini substage.

Execution snapshots both full XMM operands and evaluates four independent

NaN payloads and signalling bits are preserved; equal values and signed-zero

Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 1 §§4.9.2, 11.5.2, 11.5.3.1 and Appendix D
Tables D-9/D-13/D-15 group
MAXPS with the MINSS/MAXSS/MINPS masked IE/DE behavior; Vol. 2B specifies the

## Local S2-37i register-only MINSD with masked status

The schema-v2 profile `s2-long-minsd-reg-masked-v1` admits exactly one Long64
legacy `F2 [optional adjacent REX.R/B] 0F 5D /r` instruction, ModR/M.mod=3,
XMM0–15. The mandatory-prefix variants are distinct globally: F2 selects MINSD,
F3 selects MINSS, and bare `0F 5D /r` selects MINPS. The profile requires SSE
state, all six MXCSR exception masks set, DAZ/FTZ clear and reserved bits

Execution snapshots the source and destination low qwords, uses the existing
raw Binary64 MIN selector, and commits only the destination low qword plus
MXCSR IE/DE sticky bits after preflight. Either QNaN or SNaN in either low
qword selects raw operand 2 and contributes IE; a low-qword subnormal in either

pre-existing DE remains sticky. Equal values and signed-zero ties select operand 2.
The destination upper qword, all unrelated state and other MXCSR bits are
preserved. Upper-qword NaN/subnormal values do not affect the result or flags;

Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 1 §§4.9.2, 11.5 and Appendix D Tables D-9/D-15
cover masked invalid and denormal status; Vol. 2B specifies MINSD selection. This extends

JIT/native/CPUID admission remain closed. Physical validation is deferred to
the combined final Mac mini substage.

The schema-v2 profile `s2-long-maxsd-reg-masked-v1` admits exactly one Long64

XMM0–15. F2 selects MAXSD globally; F3 remains MAXSS and bare `0F 5F /r`
remains MAXPS. Profile validation accepts only its own exact form. SSE state,
all six MXCSR exception masks, DAZ/FTZ clear and reserved bits 16–31 zero are

new DE only if that same operation does not raise IE; prior DE remains sticky.
Only destination low qword and effective IE/DE are committed. Upper destination
qword and unrelated state are preserved; high-qword values do not affect result
or flags. Aliasing is supported and no memory access occurs. Unsupported state
refuses before mutation. JIT/native/CPUID, memory and unmasked exception paths

substage.

Profile validation accepts only its exact MINPD shape. SSE state, all six
MXCSR exception masks, DAZ/FTZ clear and reserved bits 16–31 zero are required;

## Local S2-37l register-only MAXPD with masked status

legacy `66 [optional adjacent REX.R/B] 0F 5F /r` instruction, ModR/M.mod=3,
XMM0–15. `66` selects MAXPD; bare `0F 5F /r` remains MAXPS, F3 selects MAXSS
