## S2-37m — exact Long64 CVTDQ2PD XMM0,XMM1

The interpreter-only schema-v2 profile `s2-long-cvtdq2pd-reg-exact-v1` accepts
only `F3 0F E6 C1`, one executable code mapping, budget one, and stop RIP
`entry+4`. It refuses memory operands, REX/register extensions, repeated or
reordered prefixes, other ModR/M operands, VEX and EVEX encodings. These are
profile refusals; they are not claims that every excluded encoding raises
architectural #UD.

The immutable profile controls are SSE2 availability, CR0.EM, CR0.TS and
CR4.OSFXSR. Full fetch precedes #UD for absent SSE2, EM=1 or OSFXSR=0, then
#NM for TS=1. The gates apply at CPL0–3. Either fault retires zero instructions,
preserves the complete CPU snapshot and performs no data-memory access.

On success, XMM1's low two signed dwords are sign-extended to i64 and converted
exactly to binary64 in XMM0's low 128 bits. The source high64 is ignored, all
of XMM0 is replaced, and XMM1, MXCSR, flags/definedness and unrelated CPU state
are preserved. The schema supports MXCSR bits in `0x0000ffbf`; every rounding,
exception mask, sticky status and FTZ combination has the same result. No SIMD
FP exception, #XM/OSXMMEXCPT gate, x87/MMX state or transition is modeled.

Six handwritten schema-v2 fixtures cover zero, ±1, i32 minimum/maximum,
asymmetric lanes, values around 2^24, and integer patterns that resemble
floating-point NaNs. The independent validator derives binary64 result bits
from integer fields without calling the production conversion helper. CPU
tests cover the full prerequisite matrix at CPL0–3, MXCSR combinations, fetch
truncation, STOP/budget and malformed forms. JIT/native admission remains
denied. Generic CPUID, memory forms, full S2-37 and physical acceptance remain
open; Mac mini execution is reserved for the combined final hardware substage.
Sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A CVTDQ2PD pp. 3-208–3-210; §2.5 Table 2-15
p. 2-24 and §2.5.5 Table 2-22 p. 2-30
([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199)). See the
[plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-37m--exact-long64-cvtdq2pd-xmm0xmm1),
[report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-37m--exact-long64-cvtdq2pd-xmm0xmm1),
and [fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-37m-local-cvtdq2pd).

## S2-37p — canonical Long64 CVTDQ2PD XMM register pairs

The separate interpreter-only schema-v2 profile
`s2-long-cvtdq2pd-registers-v1` accepts all 256 register pairs XMM0–15,
including self-aliases. Canonical bytes are `F3 0F E6 /r` when both indices
are low; `F3 41 0F E6 /r` when only the source is high; `F3 44 0F E6 /r`
when only the destination is high; and `F3 45 0F E6 /r` when both are high.
The independent schema parser derives the register indices and length from
these bytes, requires ModR/M.mod=3, one executable code mapping, budget one,
and stop RIP `entry+length`; address addition is checked for overflow. No
redundant REX, REX.W/X, other/repeated/reordered prefixes, memory operand,
VEX/EVEX encoding or trailing byte is admitted. Such exclusions are strict
profile refusals, not architectural #UD claims.

The source is snapshotted before the destination write. Its two low signed
dwords are converted exactly to binary64 and replace the full destination;
source high64 is ignored. Self-aliasing reads both lanes from initial state.
All remaining XMM/GPR/flags/MXCSR and unrelated state are preserved. Supported
MXCSR mask is `0x0000ffbf`; RC, masks, sticky status and FTZ do not change the
result, and no FP event is generated. Four explicit controls (SSE2 available,
CR0.EM, CR0.TS, CR4.OSFXSR) are echoed and gated after complete fetch: #UD for
missing SSE2, EM, or OSFXSR, otherwise #NM for TS, at CPL0–3. Faults retire
zero instructions, preserve the full snapshot and perform no data access.
The existing exact S2-37m profile remains limited to XMM0,XMM1. JIT/native
remain denied; this profile does not implement memory m64, other modes or
encodings, generic CPUID readiness, physical acceptance, or remaining S2-00 /
S2-38 parent requirements.

Sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A CVTDQ2PD pp. 3-208–3-210; §2.2.1.2
pp. 2-8–2-9 and Table 2-4/Fig. 2-5
([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199)). See the
[plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-37p--canonical-long64-cvtdq2pd-xmm-register-pairs),
[report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-37p--canonical-long64-cvtdq2pd-xmm-register-pairs),
and [fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-37p-local-cvtdq2pd-register-pairs).

## S2-37n — exact Long64 CVTSI2SD XMM0,EAX

The interpreter-only schema-v2 profile `s2-long-cvtsi2sd-r32-exact-v1` accepts
only Long64 `F2 0F 2A C0` (`CVTSI2SD XMM0,EAX`), one executable mapping, budget
one, and stop RIP `entry+4`. REX/r64, other GPR/XMM indices, memory forms,
extra/reordered/repeated prefixes, other encodings, VEX and EVEX are profile
refusals, with no claim that each excluded form is architecturally #UD.

Execution reads only RAX[31:0], interprets it as signed i32, sign-extends to
i64 and converts exactly to binary64. It changes only XMM0[63:0], preserving
XMM0[127:64], full RAX and all other state, including RFLAGS/definedness and
MXCSR. Accepted MXCSR bits are `0x0000ffbf`; accepted RC, exception mask,
sticky and FTZ variations preserve the result. DAZ is architecturally
irrelevant to this integer source, but DAZ=1 is outside the local mask and is
rejected. Since every signed i32 is exactly
representable as binary64, this specific r32 form raises no newly generated
SIMD FP Precision, Invalid or Denormal event. PE masking and OSXMMEXCPT do not
produce #XM or #UD for this form. This is not a family-wide exception claim.

Full fetch precedes #UD for missing SSE2, CR0.EM, or CR4.OSFXSR, followed by
#NM for CR0.TS; the matrix applies at CPL0–3. Faults retire zero instructions,
preserve the full CPU state and do not call the data-memory interface. The
schema echoes OSXMMEXCPT and tests both values. Eight literal fixtures cover
zero, ±1, i32 minimum/maximum, values around 2^24, different RAX high halves
with identical EAX and XMM0 high64 preservation. The independent schema oracle
computes result bits from the signed integer directly, without production
conversion helpers. JIT and native admission remain closed. No r64, memory,
generic CPUID or broader SSE2 support is implied.

Source: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A `CVTSI2SD` pp. 3-236–3-237, Type 3 per
§2.5 Table 2-15; legacy gates §2.5.3 Table 2-20 p. 2-28
([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199)). See the
[plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-37n--exact-long64-cvtsi2sd-xmm0eax),
[report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-37n--exact-long64-cvtsi2sd-xmm0eax),
and [fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-37n-local-cvtsi2sd-r32).

## S2-37o — exact Long64 CVTSI2SD XMM0,RAX

The interpreter-only schema-v2 profile `s2-long-cvtsi2sd-r64-exact-v1` admits
only `F2 48 0F 2A C0` (`CVTSI2SD XMM0,RAX`), one executable mapping, budget one,
and stop RIP `entry+5`. It rejects other REX values, r32, other GPR/XMM
indices, memory, other/reordered/repeated prefixes, other opcodes and VEX/EVEX
as profile refusals; this does not claim architectural #UD for every excluded
form. The existing r32 profile remains separate.

The immutable controls are SSE2 availability, CR0.EM/TS, CR4.OSFXSR and
CR4.OSXMMEXCPT. Complete fetch precedes prerequisite #UD (missing SSE2, EM=1,
or OSFXSR=0), then #NM (TS=1), at CPL0–3. Prerequisite faults do not change
MXCSR or any other CPU state and make no data-memory callbacks.

On execution the full RAX is interpreted as signed i64. Conversion uses
`Binary64::from_i64` with MXCSR.RC. Only XMM0[63:0] changes on completion;
XMM0[127:64], RAX, flags/definedness and unrelated state are preserved. The
supported local MXCSR mask remains `0x0000ffbf`; DAZ=1 and reserved bits reject,
while FTZ has no effect. Only Precision can be newly generated. PE is sticky:
`PE_new = PE_old OR inexact`, and all other MXCSR bits are preserved. Exact
conversion never faults because of old PE. For inexact conversion with PM=0,
the executor commits PE first, suppresses the destination write, leaves RIP and
retirement unchanged, then reports #XM when OSXMMEXCPT=1 or SIMD-generated #UD
when it is 0. With PM=1 it commits the rounded result and sticky PE regardless
of OSXMMEXCPT. i64::MAX rounding to 2^63 is a valid finite result, not overflow.

Sixteen handwritten fixtures include signed endpoints, exact values, ties,
directed rounding, the carry boundary, masked completion and both unmasked
exception paths. The independent schema oracle uses signed magnitude and
explicit 53-bit remainder/tie/directed rounding without production conversion
helpers or host FP. Tests cover the RC × PM × OSXMMEXCPT × old-PE matrix,
prerequisites at CPL0–3, malformed/truncated forms, STOP/budget, state
preservation, zero data callbacks, schema/result/control tampering and JIT /
native denial. This is only the exact RAX/XMM0 form: the full r64 operand and
register space, memory variants, full CVTSI2SD/S2-37 and parent S2-34/S2-38
acceptance remain open. No physical execution is claimed.

Sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A `CVTSI2SD` pp. 3-236–3-237, Type 3 §2.5
Table 2-15 and §2.5.3 Table 2-20 p. 2-28; Vol. 1 §11.5.2.6 p. 11-16 and
§§11.5.3.1–3 pp. 11-16–11-18 ([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199)).
See the [plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-37o--exact-long64-cvtsi2sd-xmm0rax),
[report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-37o--exact-long64-cvtsi2sd-xmm0rax),
and [fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-37o-local-cvtsi2sd-r64).

## S2-37q — canonical Long64 CVTSI2SD register operand space

The interpreter-only schema-v2 sibling profile `s2-long-cvtsi2sd-registers-v1`
admits 512 forms: r32/r64 × XMM0–15 destination × GPR0–15 source, with
ModR/M.mod=3. Canonical r32 prefixes are `F2` for both low indices and `F2`
plus exactly REX `41` (B), `44` (R), or `45` (RB) when needed. Canonical r64
uses `F2` plus exactly `48` (W), `49` (WB), `4C` (WR), or `4D` (WRB).
Redundant `40`, X, incorrect W, unnecessary REX, repeated/reordered/other
prefixes, memory, trailing bytes, VEX and EVEX are profile refusals. These
refusals do not assert architectural #UD for excluded encodings. S2-37n and
S2-37o fixed profiles remain limited to their original exact forms.

Schema validation independently parses the full instruction bytes to derive
width, destination, source and length; it requires one executable mapping,
budget one, checked `entry+length`, stop at that address, exact input/result
and controls echoes, and supported MXCSR mask `0x0000ffbf`. r32 reads only
the selected low32 as signed i32, sign extends and converts exactly; r64 reads
the full selected signed i64 and uses MXCSR.RC. Only the selected XMM low64 is
written; its high64, other XMMs, all GPRs and remaining state are preserved.
RSP is an ordinary source and no stack or data-memory access occurs.

SSE2, CR0.EM/TS, CR4.OSFXSR and OSXMMEXCPT gates follow S2-37n/o. r64 follows
S2-37o Precision semantics: new PE is sticky, unmasked inexact conversion
suppresses result and retirement before #XM or SIMD-generated #UD, while exact
conversion is unaffected by old PE. The schema oracle independently computes
signed integer conversion; it does not call `Binary64::from_i64`. Tests iterate
all 512 forms and retain JIT/native/CPUID denial. Only canonical register forms
are covered; memory m32/m64, other modes/prefixes, and physical acceptance stay
open. Hardware runs remain in the combined final substage.

Sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A `CVTSI2SD` pp. 3-236–3-237, Type 3
Table 2-20 p. 2-28; Vol. 1 §§11.5.2.6 and 11.5.3; REX §2.2.1.2/Table 2-4
([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199)).
See the [plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-37q--canonical-long64-cvtsi2sd-register-operands),
[report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-37q--canonical-long64-cvtsi2sd-register-operand-space),
and [fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-37q-canonical-cvtsi2sd-register-space).

## S2-37r — canonical Long64 CVTSI2SS register operand space

The interpreter-only schema-v2 sibling profile `s2-long-cvtsi2ss-registers-v1`
admits all 512 r32/r64 × XMM0–15 destination × GPR0–15 source register forms,
ModR/M.mod=3 only. Canonical r32 encodings are `F3 0F 2A /r` for low indices
and `F3 41/44/45 0F 2A /r` for extended source/destination; r64 requires W
and uses `F3 48/49/4C/4D 0F 2A /r`. The independent schema parser consumes the
complete stream. Redundant `40`, X, incorrect W, noncanonical prefixes,
memory, trailing bytes, VEX and EVEX are local profile refusals, not claims
that every excluded form is architecturally #UD. S2-37p/q and earlier exact
profiles retain their own scope.

Read selected signed i32 low32 or full signed i64; r32 ignores source high32
and preserves the full source GPR. Convert directly to binary32 using MXCSR.RC,
never via binary64. Only XMM destination low32 changes; its upper96 and all
other machine state remain unchanged. Both widths may raise Precision. New PE
is sticky. With PM=1 the rounded result commits; with PM=0 PE commits before
#XM when CR4.OSXMMEXCPT=1 or SIMD-generated #UD otherwise, and destination/RIP
and retirement are suppressed. Old PE alone is not a fault. Only MXCSR mask
`0x0000ffbf` is supported; DAZ/reserved bits reject and FTZ is irrelevant.
SSE availability, CR0.EM/TS and CR4.OSFXSR prerequisites follow complete fetch
and precede conversion; prerequisite faults preserve state. CPL0–3 use the same
order. RSP is an ordinary source; this profile performs no data-memory access.

The independent oracle uses signed magnitude, u128 and explicit 24-bit
significand/remainder rounding, with no production conversion helper or host
float. Literal cases include signed precision thresholds, i32/i64 ends,
halfway neighbors, exponent carry and a direct-vs-double-rounding discriminator.
The runner checks all 512 mappings, source/destination preservation, masked
and unmasked precision behavior, RSP, malformed/truncated encodings, result and
control tampering, and backend denial. Generic capability, JIT/native/C/fragment
execution remain denied. m32/m64 memory forms, other modes/prefixes and
physical acceptance remain open.

Sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A `CVTSI2SS` pp. 3-238–3-239, Type 3
Table 2-15/Table 2-20 p. 2-28; Vol. 1 §§11.5.2.6 and 11.5.3; REX §2.2.1.2
and Table 2-4 ([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199)).
See the [plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-37r--canonical-long64-cvtsi2ss-register-operand-space),
[report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-37r--canonical-long64-cvtsi2ss-register-operand-space),
and [fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-37r-canonical-cvtsi2ss-register-space).

## S2-38b — точечные SSE2 prerequisite gates для XORPD

Schema-v2 profile `s2-long-xorpd-prerequisites-v1` принимает ровно одну
инструкцию `66 0F 57 C1` (`XORPD XMM0,XMM1`) в Long64. В профиле явно
представлены четыре prerequisite поля: `sse2_available`, `cr0_em`, `cr0_ts`
и `cr4_osfxsr`; отсутствие всего блока или любого поля отклоняется при
валидации. Это узкая неизменяемая policy state, не общий CR framework.
Интерпретатор повторяет все четыре значения в `snapshot.xorpd_prerequisites`;
сравнение требует их наличия для этого профиля, обнаруживает расхождение
между oracle results и сверяет значения с входной fixture. У старых профилей
поле не сериализуется.

После полного fetch выбранной формы выполняются gates в порядке Intel SDM
Rev. 093 Vol. 3A Table 16-1: `!sse2_available || cr0_em || !cr4_osfxsr`
возвращает CPU-side #UD; иначе `cr0_ts` возвращает CPU-side #NM; иначе
исполняется существующий bytewise XORPD. Первая ветка имеет приоритет над TS.
Источник: [Intel SDM Rev. 093, Vol. 3A, Table 16-1](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/technical/intel-sdm.html).
Правило одинаково для CPL0–3. Fault содержит вектор 6 или 7, не имеет error
code и не retirement; RIP и полный `LongModeState` сохраняются. Нет data
memory access. Входной STOP и нулевой budget завершают запуск до fetch; fetch
fault/truncation происходит до gate. На успешной ветке меняются только XMM0
и RIP обычным retirement, остальные XMM, x87/SSE auxiliary state, GPR,
RFLAGS и memory неизменны.

Схема и exact fixture ограничивают программу ровно четырьмя указанными
байтами; соседние регистры, префиксы и кодеки остаются вне admission. Другие
XORPD профили не наследуют эти gates. CPUID не изменён; OSXMMEXCPT/#XM не
добавлены, так как выбранная форма не является арифметической. JIT, native и
C adapter остаются закрыты. Открыты broader S2-38, Generic amd64 и S2-26/39/
40/41/42. Физическое исполнение `not_run` до объединённого финального Mac mini
substage. См. [план](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-38b-exact-xorpd-sse2-prerequisite-gates),
[report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-38b--точечные-sse2-prerequisite-gates-для-xorpd)
и [fixture](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/s2_38b_xorpd_sse2_absent.case.json).

## S2-38c — exact MINSS unmasked invalid-operation exit

The interpreter-only profile `s2-long-minss-invalid-controls-v1` admits only
Long64 bytes `F3 0F 5D C1` (`MINSS XMM0,XMM1`) with one executable code
mapping, budget 1 and stop RIP `entry+4`. It requires the ordinary x87/SSE
state snapshots and explicit immutable controls `sse_available`, `cr0_em`,
`cr0_ts`, `cr4_osfxsr`, and `cr4_osxmmexcpt`; missing or extra fields fail
closed. CR0.MP=1 is a fixed prerequisite. No generic CR state/write, CPUID,
memory operand or other MINSS form is implied.

After complete instruction fetch, unavailable SSE, CR0.EM=1, or CR4.OSFXSR=0
raises CPU-side #UD; if those pass, CR0.TS=1 raises #NM. These gates precede
operand inspection, are CPL-independent, have no error code, and do not
retire. An unmasked invalid-operation condition updates only sticky MXCSR.IE
and then faults with #UD when OSXMMEXCPT=0 or #XM when it is 1. The complete
destination XMM0, RIP and retirement remain unchanged on that arithmetic
exit. A prior IE bit alone is not a new exception. With IM=1, existing masked
MINSS response and sticky-status behavior is reused.

The strict MXCSR input subset has reserved bits clear, DE/ZE/OE/UE/PE masks
set, DAZ/FTZ clear; IM may be either value and any RC is accepted. Other
arithmetic exception classes and mixed unmasked exceptions are not admitted.
This exact profile does not close broader S2-38, generic amd64, parent S2-37,
guest exception delivery, or final physical acceptance. JIT, native and C
adapter remain denied; physical/Mac mini is `not_run` until the combined final
hardware substage. Behavior follows Intel SDM Rev. 093, Vol. 1 §§11.5.3.2–3
and Table 11-1; Vol. 3A Table 16-1; Vol. 2B MINSS:
[Vol. 1](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671436),
[Vol. 3A](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/technical/intel-sdm.html),
[Vol. 2B MINSS](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/929354/253667-sdm-vol-2b.pdf).

## S2-38d — exact MINSS unmasked denormal-operand exit

The local interpreter profile `s2-long-minss-unmasked-denormal-v1` admits only
the exact Long64 bytes `F3 0F 5D C1` (`MINSS XMM0,XMM1`), one executable code
mapping, budget 1, and stop RIP `entry+4`. It requires the same complete x87/SSE
state and five explicit immutable controls as S2-38c, with CR0.MP=1 fixed.
S2-38c's profile, literal fixture and stricter DM-mask policy are unchanged.

The new MXCSR policy clears reserved bits 16–31 and DAZ/FTZ, requires ZM/OM/UM/PM
set, allows IM and DM independently, permits any RC and preserves arbitrary
prior sticky bits. Complete fetch still precedes the SSE/EM/TS/OSFXSR gates;
those gates precede operand classification. A prior DE flag alone does not
fault.

For a newly detected MINSS denormal condition with no higher-priority invalid
condition, DM=0 commits `old_mxcsr | 0x2`, leaves the complete XMM0, RIP and
retirement unchanged, and selects arithmetic #UD when OSXMMEXCPT=0 or #XM when
it is 1. With DM=1 the instruction completes and accumulates DE. For a NaN and
subnormal in the same scalar operation, the new profile preserves the Rev. 093
priority/mask rules: when both IM and DM are set, only higher-priority IE is
reported and the masked MINSS result completes; when either exception is
unmasked, IE|DE status is committed and the single pre-computation #UD/#XM
exit is reported. In the all-unmasked case Vol. 1 §11.5.3.2 ORs the detected
pre-computation flags; with mixed masks §11.5.3.3 requires both flags. Local
tests cover QNaN and SNaN in both operand positions for every IM×DM×OSXMMEXCPT
combination and verify full destination/RIP/retirement behavior.

This does not broaden decoder admission beyond XMM0/XMM1 or add MAXSS, packed
operations, DAZ/FTZ, memory, additional CR state, JIT/native or C-adapter
admission. It remains local/interpreter-only; physical/Mac mini acceptance is
`not_run` until the combined final hardware substage. Normative references:
Intel SDM Rev. 093, Vol. 1 §§4.9.2, 11.5.2.1–2, 11.5.3.2–3; Vol. 3A Table 7-8
and Table 16-1; Vol. 2B MINSS:
[Vol. 1](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671436),
[Vol. 3A](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/technical/intel-sdm.html),
[Vol. 2B MINSS](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/929354/253667-sdm-vol-2b.pdf).

## S2-38m — exact MINSS unmasked memory exit for m32 [RAX]

The local schema-v2 interpreter profile
`s2-long-minss-memory-unmasked-rax-v1` admits only Long64 bytes
`F3 0F 5D 00` (`MINSS XMM0,m32 [RAX]`), length four, budget one and stop RIP
entry+4. It requires SSE (`CPUID.01H:EDX[25]`), CR0.EM=0, fixed CR0.MP=1,
CR4.OSFXSR=1, explicit immutable CR0.TS and CR4.OSXMMEXCPT controls, and
present XMM/MXCSR state. The existing masked-only
`s2-long-minss-memory-rax-v1` profile remains unchanged. Other prefixes,
REX, ModR/M/addressing forms, register pairs, VEX/EVEX and all non-interpreter
paths are denied.

The ordered local execution contract is: stop/budget; complete four-byte
fetch; exact-form and feature gates; MXCSR/state gates; AC=1 local Unsupported;
checked `RAX+3` and canonical48 inclusive-span checks; exactly one read4;
then operand classification and FP result. Missing SSE, CR0.EM=1 or
CR4.OSFXSR=0 produces CPU-side #UD before CR0.TS=1 produces #NM. AC=0 permits
unaligned m32. Address overflow, noncanonical span or read failure precedes
operand classification, so no IE/DE is newly raised even if either source is
a NaN/subnormal; architectural state and retirement remain unchanged.

MXCSR admission requires reserved bits zero, supported mask `0xffbf`, DAZ=FTZ=0,
ZM/OM/UM/PM set; IM and DM independently accept either value, RC accepts all
four modes, and all 64 prior IE/DE/ZE/OE/UE/PE histories are preserved. After
the successful memory read, the profile uses the S2-38d mixed IM/DM priority,
not the frozen S2-38c policy. MINSS NaN raises IE; a subnormal source raises
DE except when invalid-priority applies with both IM and DM set. A NaN plus
subnormal with IM=DM=1 reports IE only and completes; if either mask is clear,
IE|DE are committed and one arithmetic exit occurs. Any newly unmasked IE/DE
commits its sticky bit(s), suppresses the entire XMM0 write, leaves RIP and
retirement unchanged, and selects #XM for OSXMMEXCPT=1 or arithmetic #UD for
OSXMMEXCPT=0. Prior IE/DE alone does not trap.

Successful MINSS returns raw RHS for numeric ties, signed zero ties and NaN;
an SNaN payload remains raw. It changes only XMM0.low32 and newly raised MXCSR
sticky bits, preserving XMM0.high96, XMM1, all other MXCSR fields and unrelated
state. This contract describes only this local schema profile, not complete
SSE/MMX semantics, generic execution, or physical x86 behavior. JIT, native,
C ABI and fragment paths remain closed. Keep ISSUE-025 open and separate from
the RSQRT threshold. See the [S2-38m plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-38m-exact-long64-minss-xmm0m32-rax-memory-profile-with-mixed-imdm-exit).

## S2-38n — exact MAXSS unmasked memory exit for m32 [RAX]

The local schema-v2 interpreter profile
`s2-long-maxss-memory-unmasked-rax-v1` admits only Long64
`F3 0F 5F 00` (`MAXSS XMM0,m32 [RAX]`), length four, budget one and stop RIP
`entry+4`. It requires SSE (`CPUID.01H:EDX[25]`), CR0.EM=0, fixed CR0.MP=1,
CR4.OSFXSR=1, explicit immutable CR0.TS and CR4.OSXMMEXCPT controls and present
XMM/MXCSR state. The S2-37cy masked MAXSS memory profile, S2-38f register
unmasked profile and S2-38m MINSS memory profile remain unchanged. REX,
alternate addressing, register-form bytes, VEX/EVEX, other prefixes and all
non-interpreter paths are denied.

Execution order is stop/budget, complete fetch, exact-form and feature gates,
MXCSR/state gates, AC=1 local Unsupported, checked `RAX+3` and canonical48
inclusive span, exactly one read4, then operand classification and FP result.
Missing SSE, CR0.EM=1 or CR4.OSFXSR=0 produces #UD before CR0.TS=1 produces
#NM. AC=0 permits unaligned m32. Overflow, noncanonical span or read failure
precedes FP classification, raises no new IE/DE and preserves state/retirement.

MXCSR requires reserved bits clear, supported mask `0xffbf`, DAZ=FTZ=0 and
ZM/OM/UM/PM=1; IM/DM independently accept either value, all RCs and old sticky
histories are admitted. MAXSS-specific semantics from S2-38f apply: QNaN and
SNaN in either operand raise IE; a subnormal operand raises DE. When masked,
MAXSS selects raw source 2 for NaN, equal values and signed-zero ties; a
source-2 SNaN payload remains unquieted. For NaN plus subnormal with IM=DM=1,
invalid priority reports IE only and completes. If either relevant mask is
clear, IE|DE are committed on one arithmetic exit. Any newly unmasked event
commits required sticky bits, suppresses the entire XMM0 write, leaves RIP
unchanged and does not retire, and selects #XM for OSXMMEXCPT=1 or arithmetic
#UD for OSXMMEXCPT=0. Prior IE/DE alone does not trap. Success changes only
XMM0.low32 and newly raised stickies, advances RIP by four and retires once,
preserving high96, XMM1, other MXCSR fields and unrelated state.

Coverage requires an independent raw-bit oracle; IM×DM×OSXMMEXCPT and RC×64
prior-sticky matrices; QNaN/SNaN/subnormal in both operand orders, mixed
NaN+subnormal, signed zero, finite/infinity/equal inputs, poisoned XMM1 and
XMM0.high96. Combined tests cover truncated fetch and gate priority, AC plus
noncanonical span, address/read failure plus unmasked NaN, and successful read
followed by arithmetic exit. Callback count must prove 0/1 reads and rollback.
Strict schema/result tampering and JIT/native backend relabel denial are
required. The profile does not claim complete SSE/MMX semantics or physical x86
acceptance. ISSUE-025 stays open and unrelated to this slice. Normative sources:
Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2B `MAXSS`, pp. 4-13–4-14; Vol. 1 §§4.9.2,
11.5.2.1–.2, 11.5.3.2–.3 and Table D-9
([Vol. 2B](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671241),
[Vol. 1](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671436)). See the
[plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-38n-exact-long64-maxss-xmm0m32-rax-memory-profile-with-mixed-imdm-exit),
[MAXSS register contract](#s2-38f--exact-maxss-unmasked-invalid-and-denormal-exit),
and [S2-38m memory-order pattern](#s2-38m--exact-minss-unmasked-memory-exit-for-m32-rax).

## S2-38o — exact MINSD unmasked memory exit for m64 [RAX]

The local schema-v2 interpreter profile
`s2-long-minsd-memory-unmasked-rax-v1` admits only exact Long64 `F2 0F 5D 00`
(`MINSD XMM0,m64 [RAX]`), length four, budget one and stop RIP `entry+4`. It
requires SSE2, CR0.EM=0, CR0.MP=1, CR4.OSFXSR=1, explicit immutable CR0.TS and
CR4.OSXMMEXCPT controls, and present XMM/MXCSR state. The S2-37cw masked memory
and S2-38g register profiles remain unchanged. Other prefixes, REX, alternate
addressing, register/packed forms, VEX/EVEX and all generic, fragment, C ABI,
native and JIT paths are denied.

Execution order is stop/budget, complete four-byte fetch, exact-form selection,
SSE2/EM/OSFXSR #UD gates before TS #NM, state/MXCSR admission, AC=1 local
Unsupported, checked `RAX+7` and canonical48 inclusive span, exactly one read8,
then classification and FP result. AC=0 allows unaligned m64. Address/read
faults precede new IE/DE and preserve CPU state and retirement.

MXCSR reserved bits are clear and supported mask is `0xffbf`; DAZ/FTZ=0 and
ZE/OE/UE/PE masks are one. IM/DM are independent and all RC/prior-sticky
histories are admitted. MINSD follows the S2-38g operation policy: QNaN or SNaN
in either operand raises IE; either subnormal raises DE; masked result selects
raw source 2 for NaNs, equal values and signed-zero ties, retaining an SNaN
payload when it is source 2. If NaN and subnormal coincide with both masks set,
invalid priority commits IE only and completes. If IM or DM is open, one
arithmetic exit commits IE|DE. Any newly unmasked event suppresses the entire
XMM0 write, leaves RIP unchanged and does not retire while committing required
sticky bits; OSXMMEXCPT selects #XM or arithmetic #UD. Prior IE/DE alone does
not trap. Success changes XMM0.low64 and new stickies, advances RIP by four and
retires once, preserving XMM0.high64, XMM1 and unrelated state.

Acceptance requires an independent raw-u64 oracle, IM×DM×OSXMMEXCPT and RC×64
sticky matrices, NaN/subnormal classes in both operand positions, signed-zero
and finite/infinity ties, high64 canaries, aligned/unaligned memory, checked
span/read faults, callback count and full rollback, fetch/feature/TS priority,
strict schema/result echo and tamper rejection, and explicit native/JIT denial.
This local interpreter profile does not claim physical x86 acceptance. See the
[plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-38o-exact-long64-minsd-xmm0m64-rax-memory-profile-with-mixed-imdm-exit),
[MINSD register contract](#s2-38g--exact-minsd-unmasked-invalid-and-denormal-exit),
and [memory ordering from S2-38m](#s2-38m--exact-minss-unmasked-memory-exit-for-m32-rax).

The local interpreter/schema-v2 profile
`s2-long-maxsd-memory-unmasked-rax-v1` admits only Long64 `F2 0F 5F 00`

## S2-38e — exact FP-init, FXRSTOR64, MINSS composition

The interpreter-only schema-v2 profile `s2-long-cr0-cr4-fp-init-fxrstor64-minss-v1`
admits the exact 33-byte S2-39i prefix followed by `F3 0F 5D C1`
(`MINSS XMM0,XMM1`), 37 bytes total. Successful completion retires ten
instructions. The first nine instructions retain the exact live CR0/CR4 initialization and staged
FXRSTOR64 behavior described by S2-39i. MINSS then reads the XMM0, XMM1, and
MXCSR values restored from the literal image; no pre-restore operand is used.

The image MXCSR domain is the S2-38d domain: reserved bits zero, ZE/OE/UE/PE
masks set, DAZ/FTZ clear, and arbitrary IM, DM, RC, and prior sticky bits.
New MINSS IE/DE status and arithmetic #XM behavior follow S2-38d, including its
priority when both invalid and denormal conditions are present. Successful
MINSS updates only XMM0's low dword and effective sticky MXCSR bits. An #XM
leaves the restored full XMM0 and RIP unchanged, does not retire MINSS, and
commits only the applicable IE/DE sticky bits. Pre-existing sticky bits remain
set and do not trigger a new fault by themselves.

The exact fixture image is authored independently and its XMM0/XMM1 operands
differ from pre-restore state. Paired variants toggle only image IM or DM for
masked completion versus #XM; result validation recomputes the required state
from the image. Tests cover status combinations and all 16 initial
CR0.EM/TS × CR4.OSFXSR/OSXMMEXCPT combinations for representative completed
and faulting executions. STOP/budget after FXRSTOR64, final-instruction fetch
failure, and all restore callback errors prevent MINSS execution; image bytes
remain unchanged. The native backend denies this profile.

This profile is a synthetic local composition based only on existing S2-39i
and S2-38d components. It records no Linux/Ubuntu or physical-hardware
observation. Mac mini status remains `not_run` until the combined final
hardware substage. See [plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-38e-exact-fp-init-fxrstor64-and-image-controlled-minss-composition),
[report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-38e--exact-fp-init-fxrstor64-and-image-controlled-minss-composition),
[fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-38e-fp-init-fxrstor64-and-minss),
and [format](../testing/TEST_CASE_FORMAT.md#s2-38e-s2-long-cr0-cr4-fp-init-fxrstor64-minss-v1).

## S2-40b — bounded SSE-only native XORPD oracle

The native-only schema-v2 profile `s2-long-native-xorpd-xmm0-xmm1-v1` admits
exactly `66 0F 57 C1` at the entry RIP, one instruction, and stops at
`entry+4`. It requires all XMM0–XMM15 snapshots, MXCSR exactly `0x00001f80`,
and ordinary Long64 integer state. An x87 snapshot is forbidden; a combined
x87/SSE snapshot is rejected. The instruction writes `XMM0 := XMM0 XOR XMM1`
bytewise and preserves XMM1–XMM15, MXCSR, all GPRs, defined integer flags,
and fixture memory. The oracle compares all 256 XMM bytes and MXCSR exactly.

On Linux x86_64, the ptrace transport reads the full FP-register structure
through `PTRACE_GETFPREGS`, replaces only XMM0–XMM15 and MXCSR fields, writes
the structure with `PTRACE_SETFPREGS`, and verifies initial readback before
execution. It reads the final SSE state separately from integer registers. This is the Linux ptrace FP-register transport contract; it
is not guest FXSAVE memory and it does not substitute the host `MXCSR_MASK`.
The selected CPU feature bits do not change. All prior x87/SSE state, SIMD and
FXSAVE profiles remain native-denied; JIT and the C adapter remain denied.

The local schema, codec and interpreter comparison are covered by portable
checks. Linux x86_64 transport is compile-checked only; physical execution is
`not_run` and remains part of the final Mac mini substage. S2-26, S2-39, S2-40,
S2-41 and S2-42 remain open. See [S2-40b plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-40b-узкий-sse-only-native-xorpd-oracle),
[Linux profile report](../reports/STAGE_2_LINUX_PROFILE.md#s2-40b--ограниченный-sse-only-native-xorpd-oracle),
and [fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-40b-native-xorpd-xmm0-xmm1).

### S2-27g — exact Long64 `SWAPGS`

The local `SwapgsV1` execution profile admits only bare `0F 01 F8` in Long64,
with FRED disabled. `LongModeState::kernel_gs_base: Option<u64>` holds the
mutable second architectural base; `None` is the legacy/default state and is
not inferred from immutable controls or an MSR sidecar. The profile assumes
canonical48 GS and kernel-GS bases, VMX/SMM disabled, and no guest mode other
than Long64. It does not implement IA32_KERNEL_GS_BASE as a general MSR.

CPL0 atomically exchanges `gs_base` and `kernel_gs_base`, advances RIP by 3,
and retires once. GPRs, RFLAGS and definedness, selectors/cache attributes,
FS state, and memory remain unchanged. CPL1–3 raises #GP(0) before state or
data access and does not retire. Missing profile or missing second base is
`Unsupported`. Exact LOCK-prefixed `F0 0F 01 F8` raises #UD after complete
fetch; truncated encodings retain fetch-fault priority. Other prefixes and
neighbors are `Unsupported`. A subsequent GS load consumes the exchanged
`gs_base`; if that load faults, the completed SWAPGS remains committed and
only the second instruction is unretired.

Intel SDM Rev. 093, Vol. 2B, SWAPGS pp. 4-697–4-698, defines the exact opcode,
Long64 validity, CPL0 restriction, base exchange, and unchanged flags. It also
states SWAPGS is unavailable when CR4.FRED=1 because FRED transitions perform
the swap automatically; this profile therefore assumes FRED disabled. See the
[official Vol. 2B PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671241). This local
interpreter profile does not claim JIT, native, physical, or unconditional
Long64 support.

### S2-27h — exact Long64 `CLI`

`CliProfile::NonPviLong64V1` admits only bare `FA` in Long64. It fixes
CR0.PE=1, RFLAGS.VM=0, CR4.PVI=0, and VMX/SMM disabled. CPL is supplied by
`AccessContext`; IOPL is read from RFLAGS[13:12]. When CPL<=IOPL, the
instruction clears IF only, advances RIP by one and retires exactly once,
including when IF was already clear. When CPL>IOPL it raises #GP(0) after
complete fetch with no mutation, retirement or data-memory callback, including
when IF was clear. The operation preserves IOPL, all unrelated RFLAGS bits,
and the existing arithmetic-definedness mask; IF and IOPL are concrete system
bits rather than arithmetic-defined flags.

Exact LOCK `F0 FA` raises #UD after both bytes have been fetched. Other
prefixes and neighboring instructions remain unsupported. Stop, budget and
fetch precedence follows the existing interpreter boundary. The legacy
execution APIs remain unsupported for CLI; JIT, native and C/fragment adapters
do not admit this profile. CPUID identity and masks are unchanged.

The fixture profile `s2-long-cli-v1` carries a typed CPL input only for this
profile, admits exactly bare `FA` with budget 1, and compares
`INTEGER_FLAGS|IF|IOPL`; only arithmetic `INTEGER_FLAGS` bits are required in
`rflags_defined`. Thirty-two fixtures cover IF=0/1 × CPL0–3 × IOPL0–3. A
separate composition test executes CLI then submits a new caller-owned
maskable request at the next fresh boundary: IF=0 runs the next NOP without
eligibility notification or event/data access, while IF=1 returns
`InterruptEligible` before fetch. It does not query after a CLI fault.

The selected interpretation follows Intel SDM Rev. 093, Vol. 2A,
`CLI` pp. 3-148–3-149, Table 3-7; [official Intel SDM](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/technical/intel-sdm.html).
The profile is a CPU-side decision only and does not implement #GP/#UD delivery
or claim physical, Linux, JIT, native or C execution.

### S2-27i — exact Long64 `STI` and maskable-interrupt inhibition

`StiProfile::NonPviLong64V1` admits bare `FB` and carries the explicit
`LongModeState::sti_shadow` state (`Clear` or `Blocking`). `None` means the
selected legacy contract does not model interrupt inhibition; the STI profile
requires `Some`, initialized to `Clear`. The profile fixes Long64, CR0.PE=1,
RFLAGS.VM=0, CR4.PVI=0, and VMX/SMM disabled. CPL comes from
`AccessContext`; IOPL comes from RFLAGS[13:12]. At CPL<=IOPL, STI sets IF,
advances RIP and retires once. If IF was clear on entry it sets `Blocking`;
if IF was already set it sets `Clear`. CPL>IOPL raises #GP(0) atomically.

The next successfully retired allowed instruction clears an earlier
`Blocking` state. A second STI observes IF=1 and creates no new block. CPU
fault, unsupported instruction, STOP, budget exhaustion and fetch failure do
not consume the shadow. The maskable-request entry rejects `Blocking` before
eligibility or fetch; interrupt delivery rejects it before descriptor and
stack callbacks. Legacy REP continuation entry rejects `Blocking` before token
validation, stop callbacks, fetch, data access or retirement. Fragment adapters
reject any modeled shadow, including `Clear`; the schema-v2 STI profile
serializes and compares it.

The bounded schema admits only `FB`, `FB 90`, `FB FB`, `FB FA`, and `FA FB 90`
with the documented instruction budgets; success fixtures start with IF=0 and
allowed CPL, while single-STI denial fixtures cover CPL>IOPL. The profile
compares `INTEGER_FLAGS|IF|IOPL` as concrete state without changing
`rflags_defined`. Prefix variants, legacy execution, JIT, native execution and
C/fragment execution remain outside the profile. NMI, SMI, event-delivery
ordering and scheduler integration are excluded.

The local instruction contract follows Intel SDM Rev. 093, Vol. 2B, STI
pp. 4-674–4-675, Table 4-22; [official Intel SDM](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/technical/intel-sdm.html).

### S2-27k — exact Long64 same-CPL0 `IRETQ`

`IretqProfile::SameCpl0ValidFrameV1` admits only exact bytes `48 CF` with
Long64/CPL0, `activity=Running`, `sti_shadow=Clear`, and
`rflags_defined=INTEGER_FLAGS`. The caller certifies private synchronous RAM,
FRED/CET/shadow stacks/VMX/SMM disabled, no blocked or pending NMI/debug event,
and `NT=0`. Current and restored RFLAGS contain only
`INTEGER_FLAGS|IF|IOPL`, with bit 1 set; this local profile does not model a
broader privilege or exception path.

At the old RSP, read exactly five little-endian qwords: RIP, CS, RFLAGS, RSP,
SS. Use only low 16 bits of CS/SS. Require canonical48 return RIP/RSP and
non-null GDT selectors with TI=0/RPL=0 whose descriptor bytes fit within GDTR.
Read both descriptors without writes. The only accepted CS descriptor is
present/accessed nonconforming ring-0 readable code with base 0, effective
limit 4 GiB, L=1/D=0 (access `9B`, flags `A`). The only accepted SS descriptor
is present/accessed writable expand-up ring-0 data with base 0, effective
limit 4 GiB (access `93`, flags `C`).

Only after both reads and all checks succeed, commit restored RIP, CS selector
and cache, RFLAGS, RSP, SS selector and cache; return `Retired` once with
activity Running and shadow Clear. Both caches come from the descriptors.
Preserve the frame, descriptor bytes and every other modeled state field.
Restoring IF does not create an STI shadow. Unsupported mode/state/selectors,
descriptor attributes or flags return Unsupported without CPU commit. A memory
callback failure returns terminal `ReadAborted { phase, cause }`; this is a
local harness abort, not an architectural IRET fault, fault-priority result or
delivered guest exception. Exact `F0 48 CF` returns source-backed #UD only
after all three bytes fetch; other prefix forms remain unsupported. JIT,
native and C/fragment adapters remain closed. Normative source: Intel SDM Rev.
093, Vol. 2A, IRET/IRETD/IRETQ pp. 3-490–3-498, and Vol. 3A §7.14.3;
[official Vol. 2A PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199),
[official Vol. 3A PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671190).

The `s2-long-iretq-cpl0-valid-v1` fixture profile admits one instruction and
budget 1, with distinct code/frame/GDT regions and stop RIP equal to saved RIP.
CS/SS selector/cache fields are present only in this profile; old wire shapes
omit them. Four literal cases cross restored IF=0/1 and IOPL=0/3. The local
core composition test covers `STI; HLT`, successful S2-27f delivery, IRETQ,
post-HLT continuation and all 16 old-RSP low-bit alignments. This synthetic
composition is not Linux boot, hardware, or general event-delivery evidence.

### S2-27l — exact Long64 same-CPL0 `LRETQ`

`LretqProfile::SameCpl0ValidFrameV1` admits only exact bytes `48 CB` in
Long64/CPL0, with Running activity, Clear STI shadow, `rflags_defined` equal
to `INTEGER_FLAGS`, and current RFLAGS limited to `INTEGER_FLAGS|IF|IOPL`
with reserved bit 1 set. The caller certifies private synchronous RAM,
FRED/CET/shadow stacks/VMX/SMM disabled, and no pending debug or NMI event.
Explicit current GDTR and a non-null CPL0 CS selector/cache are required. This
profile does not model guest exception delivery or broader privilege
transitions.

At old RSP, read exactly two little-endian qwords: target RIP and CS. Use only
the low 16 CS bits. Require canonical48 target RIP and the complete 16-byte
frame range including `old_rsp + 16` to be canonical without overflow. CS is
a non-null GDT selector with TI=RPL=0 and its descriptor must fit current GDTR.
Read the descriptor from current GDT even if its selector equals the cached CS.
Accept only the bounded S2-27k descriptor: present/accessed nonconforming ring-0
code, base 0, effective limit 4 GiB, L=1/D=0 (`access=9B`, `flags=A`).

After all reads and validation succeed, commit target RIP, CS selector/cache,
RSP=`old_rsp+16` and one retirement atomically. RFLAGS and its definedness,
SS selector/cache, other segments and bases, all GPR except RSP, FP, GDTR/IDTR,
memory, Running activity and Clear shadow are preserved. No target instruction
fetch is part of LRETQ. Invalid state, frame, selector or descriptor is
Unsupported without CPU commit. Callback failures are terminal
`ReadAborted { phase: Fetch|Frame|CsDescriptor, cause }`, not guest faults.
Exact `F0 48 CB` produces #UD only after all three bytes are fetched; other
prefix forms remain unsupported. JIT/native/C/fragment paths remain closed.

The `s2-long-lretq-cpl0-valid-v1` fixture admits one instruction with budget 1,
separate code/frame/GDT regions and stop RIP equal to the target RIP. Its two
qword frame stores target RIP and CS; complete CS/SS selector/cache fields are
opt-in so unchanged SS state is compared while older fixture wire forms remain
unchanged. Four literal cases cross IF=0/1 × IOPL=0/3. This is local interpreter
coverage, not Linux runtime or physical execution evidence.

This bounded local profile does not generalize far-return semantics or claim
that the selected Linux image contains these exact bytes. Linux source and
symbol evidence identify `LRETQ` in `startup_64`; the binary instruction bytes
were not independently established. Normative behavior is based on Intel SDM
Rev. 093, Vol. 2B, `RET` instruction entry; exact `F0 48 CB` #UD handling is
the source-backed LOCK-invalid rule for this profile. See the [official SDM](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/technical/intel-sdm.html)
and [S2-27l Linux evidence](../reports/STAGE_2_LINUX_PROFILE.md#s2-27l-lretq-evidence-and-local-profile).

### S2-27j — exact Long64 HLT and synchronous maskable wake

`HaltProfile::Long64V1` admits bare `F4` in Long64 with an explicit
`LongModeState::activity`. `None` means a legacy caller does not model CPU
activity; the HLT profile requires `Some(Running)` at entry and a modeled STI
shadow (`Some(Clear)` or `Some(Blocking)`). Halted plus Blocking is invalid.
The bounded assumptions are one vCPU, private synchronous RAM, VMX/SMM/debug/
NMI disabled, and no MOV-SS inhibition. CPL is `AccessContext::privilege`.

CPL0 HLT retires once, advances RIP by one, preserves GPR/RFLAGS/definedness
and memory, records `Halted`, consumes an STI Blocking shadow, and returns
`RunExit::Halted` immediately after the instruction. CPL1–3 raise #GP(0)
without retirement or state change. Exact `F0 F4` raises #UD only after both
bytes are fetched; other prefixed forms remain outside this profile. Existing
fetch, STOP and budget order is retained before instruction execution.

Re-entry while Halted does not fetch or retire instructions or access data.
Host stop/budget checks may still win at the entry boundary, but never change
activity. A caller-owned maskable request with IF=1 and shadow Clear may return
`InterruptEligible` while leaving the CPU Halted and request unconsumed; IF=0
remains Halted without fetch. The existing `deliver_maskable_interrupt` API
wakes only after it returns `Delivered`, committing `Running` after all frame
stores succeed. Its frame saves the post-HLT RIP. `DeliveryAborted` keeps the
existing terminal policy; callers must stop and must not retry. This adds no
asynchronous arrival, scheduler, APIC/timer, IRETQ, or other wake source.

The `s2-long-hlt-v1` fixture profile compares `INTEGER_FLAGS|IF|IOPL`, activity
and STI shadow, and represents the terminal outcome as `Halted` without a
`stop_rip`. Literal coverage is four CPL0 success cases and twelve CPL1–3
#GP(0) cases over IF=0/1 and IOPL=0/3, plus bounded CPL0 `FB F4`, `FA F4`, and
`FA FB F4` compositions. JIT, native and C/fragment paths reject the new state
or profile. Architecture source: Intel SDM Rev. 093, Vol. 2A, HLT p. 3-439;
[official Intel SDM](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/technical/intel-sdm.html).

## S2-25a — bounded Long64 CR0 EM/TS FP initialization

`Cr0Profile::FpInitLong64V1` is an explicit local interpreter contract. Entry
requires Long64, active IA-32e mode, CR4.PAE, EFER.LME/LMA, an available x87
unit, `Running`, `Clear` STI shadow, an x87 state with FCS/FDS selectors
unavailable, and CR0 equal to `0x80010033` with only EM (bit 2) and TS (bit 3)
variable. This represents four CR0 values only; it is not a CR0 state machine or
mode/paging transition model. `LongModeState::cr0=None` retains legacy behavior;
legacy entry points reject `Some(cr0)` before fetch.

The profile admits exact `0F 20 C0` (`MOV RAX,CR0`), `0F 22 C0` (`MOV CR0,RAX`),
`48 83 E0 F3` (`AND RAX,-13`), and `DB E3` (`FNINIT`), alone or in the exact
sequence `0F 20 C0 48 83 E0 F3 0F 22 C0 DB E3`. CR reads/writes require CPL0;
CPL1–3 raise #GP(0) after complete instruction fetch. A CPL0 write succeeds only
for one of the four allowed values; other values return local `Unsupported`
without committing state. It does not model general CR0 reserved-bit faults or
privileged control-register behavior. MOV CR preserves concrete RFLAGS while
marking arithmetic RFLAGS definedness undefined; other RFLAGS bits are retained.

FNINIT uses current mutable CR0: EM or TS raises #NM before x87 mutation, while
clear EM/TS resets FCW to `037F`, FSW to zero, FTW to `FFFF`, and FIP/FDP/FOP to
zero. The eight raw 80-bit register payloads and all SSE/XMM/MXCSR state survive.
There is no pending-unmasked-exception wait. Exact LOCK-prefixed CR0 moves and
FNINIT raise #UD before privilege/profile gates; other forms remain unsupported.

The strict `s2-long-cr0-fp-init-v1` fixture admits one executable code mapping,
one of five exact byte strings, matching instruction budget and stop RIP, and
compares integer, IF/IOPL, CR0, x87, SSE, activity and shadow state. Thirty-two
handwritten cases cover four full initial EM/TS states, the 16 FNINIT EM/TS × CPL
gates, four read and four write CPL outcomes, and four write→FNINIT gates. These
are local synthetic fixtures; they make no Ubuntu byte/runtime, native, SMP,
MMU, hardware, or physical-execution claim. CPUID and native/JIT/C/fragment
admission are unchanged.

Sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2B, MOV to/from control registers, pp. 4-32–4-34;
Vol. 2A, FNINIT, pp. 3-345–3-346; Vol. 3A §5.10.4.1.

## S2-25b — mutable CR4 OSFXSR/OSXMMEXCPT in bounded FP initialization

`Cr4Profile::FpInitLong64V1` adds optional mutable `LongModeState::cr4` only
for this profile. The admitted domain is four values: CR4.PAE (bit 5) fixed to
one, with only OSFXSR (bit 9) and OSXMMEXCPT (bit 10) varying. The associated
CR0 input remains the S2-25a fixed base with only EM/TS varying. These are
bounded profile values, not a general control-register model. Legacy `None`
state is unchanged; legacy step/run, event, REP and return paths fail closed
before fetch when CR4 is present.

The strict fixture profile admits either bare `66 0F 57 C1` (XORPD XMM0,XMM1)
or the exact `DB E3 0F 20 E0 48 0D 00 06 00 00 0F 22 E0 66 0F 57 C1`
composition (FNINIT; MOV RAX,CR4; OR RAX,0x600; MOV CR4,RAX; XORPD). CR reads
and writes require CPL0 and full fetch; non-CPL0 accesses raise #GP(0). LOCK-
prefixed CR4 moves raise #UD after full fetch, before privilege checks. CR4
writes outside the four-value domain return local `Unsupported` without
commit. The OR operation preserves preexisting CR4 bits while setting OSFXSR
and OSXMMEXCPT. The successful composition fixture requires initial CR0 to
equal the profile base (EM=TS=0), so FNINIT retires before CR4 is updated.

FNINIT and XORPD gates use the current mutable `state.cr0` and `state.cr4`.
FNINIT reports #NM for current CR0.EM or CR0.TS before x87 mutation. After
complete XORPD fetch, CR0.EM or clear CR4.OSFXSR reports #UD before CR0.TS
reports #NM; otherwise the existing bytewise XORPD operation runs. SSE2 is an
explicit fixed assumption. OSXMMEXCPT is retained and compared as state; this
non-arithmetic XORPD slice does not model #XM delivery. The profile does not
add CPUID behavior, CR3/paging/TLB state, native/JIT/C/fragment execution or
physical execution.

Six local handwritten schema-v2 fixtures cover all four CR4 domain values,
both #UD prerequisites, #UD-before-#NM priority, #NM, successful XORPD with
OSXMMEXCPT clear, and the exact FNINIT/CR4-update/XORPD composition. Testkit
validates the exact bytes, state domain, budget, stop, output CR0/CR4, XMM and
x87 state; result tampering is rejected by the profile validator and
comparator.

Normative sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2B, MOV to/from control registers,
pp. 4-32–4-34 and XORPD; Vol. 2A, FNINIT, pp. 3-345–3-346; Vol. 3A
§5.10.4.1 and Table 16-1 for the SSE2 `#UD/#NM` priority. [Official Intel SDM
index](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/technical/intel-sdm.html).

## S2-25c — exact CR0 clear, FNINIT, CR4 enable and XORPD composition

The local `s2-long-cr0-cr4-fp-init-v1` profile admits only the exact bytes
`0F 20 C0 48 83 E0 F3 0F 22 C0 DB E3 0F 20 E0 48 0D 00 06 00 00 0F 22 E0 66 0F 57 C1`.
Its initial state accepts the four S2-25a CR0 values crossed with the four
S2-25b CR4 values. The first MOV CR0 requires CPL0; CPL1–3 raise #GP(0) before
retirement. The exact successful path has eight retirements: read and clear
CR0.EM/TS, write CR0, FNINIT, read CR4, set OSFXSR/OSXMMEXCPT, write CR4, and
XORPD XMM0,XMM1. The result validator checks final CR0/CR4, RAX, RIP, x87
reset, the bytewise XMM0 result, full unrelated state, and RFLAGS. The raw
RFLAGS result is derived from the initial value: the final OR clears CF/PF/ZF/
SF/OF, preserves the concrete AF bit as the existing local undefined-flag
policy, and preserves other admitted bits. Definedness is checked separately.

The sequence is not atomic. Each instruction commits under the existing
interpreter rules, so stop, budget exhaustion, or a later fetch failure keeps
earlier retirement effects. Schema-v2 fixtures are restricted to the full
CPL0 success sequence; dedicated execution tests cover partial boundaries and
nonzero CPL. JIT, native, C, fragment and legacy entry points remain denied.
This establishes local interpreter behavior only; no hardware or physical
execution claim is made. Normative instruction semantics use Intel SDM Rev.
093 Vol. 2A FNINIT, Vol. 2B MOV CR/XORPD and Vol. 3A §5.10.4.1/Table 16-1.

## S2-25d — IA32 EFER evidence and read-only candidate

This is the source/image evidence record; the bounded runtime profile is
specified separately in S2-25e.
The authenticated Ubuntu 7.0.0-38.38 main-kernel direct64 continuation maps
`RDMSR IA32_EFER` (`0F 32`, ECX=`0xc0000080`) to
`ffffffff8139c1b4` / `arch/x86/kernel/head_64.S:385`, and a conditional
`WRMSR` (`0F 30`) to `ffffffff8139c1d5` / line 401. It sets SCE and, when
CPUID.80000001:EDX[20] reports NX, sets NXE. The write is skipped when those
bits already match. The mapping is a main-kernel success-path site, not proof
of the absolute first EFER access or of the runtime value. See the [source/image
mapping](../reports/STAGE_2_LINUX_PROFILE.md#ia32-efer-on-the-mapped-main-kernel-direct64-continuation).

The evidence motivated a read-only exact Long64
`RDMSR IA32_EFER` under a caller-selected immutable profile value; CPL0 returns
the selected 64-bit value in EDX:EAX and CPL1–3 raises #GP(0). Candidate
synthetic inputs are `0x500`, `0x501`, `0xd00`, and `0xd01`: LME/LMA are fixed
set and SCE/NXE vary independently. These values are a test domain only, not
an inferred Ubuntu entry snapshot. Do not store an unmodeled EFER field or
enable arbitrary MSRs.

Architecturally LMA (bit 10) is read-only status derived from CR0.PG and
IA32_EFER.LME; IA-32e paging also requires CR4.PAE. WRMSR mode changes, NX
page-enforcement effects and translation changes are therefore outside this
read-only CPU slice. In particular, this contract does not admit the mapped
WRMSR. The source's later compiled CR0 value `0x80050033` includes AM, while
the existing S2-25a base `0x80010033` is synthetic; neither proves initial
entry state. Absolute earlier-helper access ordering and the actual initial
EFER/CR snapshot remain open under [ISSUE-027](../KNOWN_ISSUES.md#issue-027--first-efer-access-and-startup-control-snapshot-are-unproven).

Normative reference: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2B, RDMSR/WRMSR; Vol. 3A,
IA32_EFER layout and IA-32e paging requirements
([official SDM index](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/technical/intel-sdm.html)).

## S2-25e — exact read-only Long64 RDMSR IA32_EFER

The interpreter exposes `run_with_efer_rdmsr_profile` with one immutable
caller-selected synthetic value. The only accepted values are `0x500`,
`0x501`, `0xd00`, and `0xd01`: LME and LMA are fixed to one; SCE and NXE vary
independently. This is a bounded policy domain, not an observed Linux entry
snapshot. EFER is not added to `LongModeState`, and no general MSR map is
introduced.

The profile executes only exact bare Long64 `0F 32` with ECX=`0xc0000080`.
The caller must supply current CR0 from the existing S2-25a domain and CR4 from
the S2-25b domain; both are mandatory, retaining PG=1 and PAE=1 for the fixed
LMA bit. CPL0 copies the selected 64-bit value to EDX:EAX with each dword
zero-extended, advances RIP by two, and preserves all other state. CPL1–3
raises #GP(0) after complete fetch and commits no state. Wrong index, invalid
selected value, invalid CR domains, prefixes, WRMSR and other forms are local
Unsupported outcomes. Generic legacy execution continues to reject present
optional CR0/CR4 values unless an explicit bounded API is selected.

Schema-v2 fixtures carry `efer_value` and numeric `efer_cpl` profile inputs;
CR0/CR4 remain explicit fields of the existing architectural snapshot. Strict
fixture/result validation checks the exact encoding, complete state output,
four permitted values, privilege result and memory preservation. The
independent comparator rejects tampered results. JIT, native x86, C and
fragment admission remain denied. This profile does not model WRMSR, EFER
transitions, NX page enforcement, page-table/TLB effects, guest exception
delivery or physical execution. The S2-25d startup evidence and the unproven
entry snapshot/absolute-first-access limitation remain under
[ISSUE-027](../KNOWN_ISSUES.md#issue-027--first-efer-access-and-startup-control-snapshot-are-unproven).

Normative semantics: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2B RDMSR ([official PDF](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/929354/253667-093-sdm-vol-2b.pdf)) and Vol. 3A IA32_EFER / IA-32e paging ([official SDM index](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/technical/intel-sdm.html)).
## S2-38f — exact MAXSS unmasked invalid and denormal exit

The interpreter-only profile `s2-long-maxss-unmasked-denormal-v1` accepts
only Long64 `F3 0F 5F C1` (`MAXSS XMM0,XMM1`), a single executable code region,
budget 1 and stop RIP `entry+4`. It uses a MAXSS-specific immutable five-boolean
control object (`sse_available`, CR0.EM/TS, CR4.OSFXSR and CR4.OSXMMEXCPT) and
echoes it in the result. The input MXCSR must have reserved bits clear,
ZE/OE/UE/PE masks set and DAZ/FTZ clear; IM and DM vary independently, RC and
old sticky bits are unrestricted. Existing S2-38c/d MINSS fields and profile
contracts are unchanged.

Complete fetch and bounded stop/budget checks precede SSE/EM/OSFXSR #UD gates;
TS #NM follows only if those pass. Gates are independent of CPL. Operand
classification happens after gates. MAXSS invalid conditions include QNaN and
SNaN in either operand; denormal applies to either subnormal operand. The
MAXSS-specific result selector returns raw operand 2 for either NaN, equal
values and either signed-zero tie, preserving an operand-2 SNaN payload/sign bit.
For newly detected conditions, a clear IM commits IE and a clear DM commits DE.
If either event is unmasked, the entire destination XMM0 and RIP remain
unchanged and the instruction does not retire; OSXMMEXCPT chooses #UD or #XM.
When NaN and subnormal coincide and both masks are set, invalid priority reports
IE only and MAXSS completes with its masked raw operand-2 result. If at least
one mask is clear, both pre-computation flags are committed on the single
faulting exit. Prior IE/DE flags alone do not fault. This bounded profile does
not model a handler and resumed re-execution.

The local tests cover the IM×DM×OSXMMEXCPT matrix for QNaN/SNaN/subnormal in
both operand positions, SSE/EM/OSFXSR versus TS precedence, CPL0–3, fetch
truncation, STOP/zero budget, exact form rejection, complete state preservation,
MAXSS normal/equal/signed-zero/infinity/NaN payload behavior, schema/result
tampering and comparator control echoes. JIT, native, C adapter, other registers,
memory operands, other prefixes, generic control-register state and physical
execution are excluded. Physical/Mac mini verification remains for the
combined final hardware substage.

Sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093, Vol. 2B MAXSS pp.4-13–4-14; Vol.1 §§4.9.2,
11.5.2.1–2, 11.5.3.2–3; Vol.3A Tables 7-8 and 16-1. Vol.2B explicitly lists
MAXSS invalid (including QNaN) and denormal conditions, its operand-2 selector,
and preservation of source-2 SNaN bits. Vol.1 provides exception priority,
MXCSR flag/mask behavior and combined masked/unmasked handling. These references
specify architectural conditions and flags, not the behavior of a local
single-exit test harness after a software handler changes machine state.
([Vol. 1](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671436),
[Vol. 2B](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671241),
[Vol. 3A](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671190)).
See [S2-38f plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-38f-exact-long64-maxss-xmm0xmm1-unmasked-invalid-and-denormal-exit).


## S2-38g — exact MINSD unmasked invalid and denormal exit

The interpreter-only schema-v2 profile `s2-long-minsd-unmasked-denormal-v1`
accepts only Long64 `F2 0F 5D C1` (`MINSD XMM0,XMM1`), one executable code
region, budget 1 and stop RIP `entry+4`. A profile-specific immutable control
object records `sse2_available`, CR0.EM/TS, CR4.OSFXSR and CR4.OSXMMEXCPT; the
result must echo it unchanged. Full fetch happens before the SSE2/EM/OSFXSR
#UD gates and TS #NM gate; operands are classified after these gates, at every
CPL. Other registers, REX, prefixes, memory operands, packed forms and MAXSD
are outside admission.

Reserved MXCSR bits must be clear, ZE/OE/UE/PE masks set, DAZ/FTZ clear; IM/DM,
RC and previous sticky bits are accepted. MINSD QNaN/SNaN in either operand
raises IE; either subnormal operand is retained as a raw DE classification for
this profile. If invalid and denormal coincide and both masks are set, invalid
priority reports IE only and the operation completes. If either event is
unmasked, IE|DE are committed and one bounded exit occurs. A DE-only unmasked
event commits DE. OSXMMEXCPT selects #XM (vector 19) or #UD (vector 6). Faults
preserve complete XMM0/RIP and retire zero; success writes only low qword XMM0,
preserving its upper qword and all other state. This is a local one-exit model;
handler continuation and physical hardware delivery are not claimed. The
existing masked MINSD/MAXSD status contracts are unchanged.

Local tests cover the full NaN/subnormal × operand-position × IM×DM×OSXMMEXCPT
matrix, prerequisites and CPL, truncated fetch, STOP/zero budget, exact-form
rejection, sentinels, schema/result tampering, comparator control echoes and
JIT/native denial. Sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2B MINSD pp.4-22–4-23
([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671241)); Vol. 1
§§4.9.2, 11.5.2, 11.5.3.2–3 ([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671436)). See the [plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-38g-exact-long64-minsd-xmm0xmm1-unmasked-invalid-and-denormal-exit).


## S2-38h — exact MAXSD unmasked invalid and denormal exit

The interpreter-only schema-v2 profile `s2-long-maxsd-unmasked-denormal-v1`
accepts only Long64 `F2 0F 5F C1` (`MAXSD XMM0,XMM1`), one executable code
region, budget 1 and stop RIP `entry+4`. Its immutable `MaxsdUnmaskedControls`
contains `sse2_available`, CR0.EM/TS, CR4.OSFXSR and CR4.OSXMMEXCPT and is echoed
unchanged by the result. Full fetch precedes SSE2/EM/OSFXSR #UD and TS #NM gates;
operands are classified only after the gates, at CPL0–3. Other registers,
REX/prefix variations, memory and packed forms are outside admission.

The profile requires reserved MXCSR bits clear, ZE/OE/UE/PE masks set, and
DAZ/FTZ clear. IM/DM, RC and prior sticky flags are accepted. Per the MAXSD
entry in Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2B pp. 4-11–4-12, finite operands select the
numeric maximum. Either NaN, equality or a signed-zero tie selects raw source 2;
source-2 SNaN/QNaN payload/sign are preserved. This is MAXSD-specific evidence,
not an inference from MINSD. Raw subnormal classification is kept separate from
the existing masked MAXSD/MINSD status path. For mixed NaN+subnormal with both
masks set, invalid priority reports IE only and completes. If IM or DM is
unmasked, IE|DE are recorded and one #XM (OSXMMEXCPT=1) or #UD
(OSXMMEXCPT=0) occurs. A DE-only unmasked input records DE. Faults preserve full
XMM0/RIP and retire zero; completion updates only XMM0 low qword and RIP. Old
sticky IE/DE bits alone do not fault. No handler continuation is modeled.

Fixed local evidence includes the full NaN/subnormal/mixed × operand-position ×
IM × DM × OSXMMEXCPT matrix, SSE2/EM/OSFXSR/TS controls, CPL0–3, partial fetch,
STOP/zero budget, exact-form rejects, finite/equal/signed-zero/infinity cases,
raw payloads, upper-qword sentinels, independent result validation, tamper and
comparator checks. All 88 literal MAXSD fixtures run through the interpreter
profile; JIT/native are rejected. C/fragment and physical admission remain
closed. Normative source: [Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2B](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671241),
MAXSD pp. 4-11–4-12, SHA-256
`a261998ace8e07f624bf3e2486bb6cfe950fb8be8d0dc9631bcecb4c5ec953e4`; Vol. 1
§§4.9.2, 11.5.2.1–2, 11.5.3.2–3 and Vol. 2A Table 2-20. See the
[plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-38h-exact-long64-maxsd-xmm0xmm1-unmasked-invalid-and-denormal-exit).


## S2-38i — exact MINPD unmasked invalid and denormal exit

The interpreter-only profile `s2-long-minpd-unmasked-denormal-v1` accepts only
Long64 `66 0F 5D C1` (`MINPD XMM0,XMM1`), one executable code region, budget
one and stop RIP `entry+4`. Its immutable `MinpdUnmaskedControlSnapshot`
records SSE2 availability, CR0.EM/TS, CR4.OSFXSR and CR4.OSXMMEXCPT and is
echoed exactly by the result. Fetch is complete before SSE2/EM/OSFXSR #UD and
then TS #NM gates; both lanes are examined only after gates, independent of CPL.
Reserved MXCSR bits, DAZ and FTZ must be zero; ZE/OE/UE/PE masks must be set;
IM/DM, RC and prior sticky status are permitted.

Both full XMM operands are snapshotted. Each binary64 lane uses the raw MIN
selector, which chooses raw operand 2 for either QNaN/SNaN, equal values and
signed-zero ties. Raw IE and DE conditions are collected per lane. If any newly
detected event is unmasked, the instruction ORs all detected IE/DE flags from
both lanes into MXCSR and reports one #XM (OSXMMEXCPT=1) or #UD
(OSXMMEXCPT=0), preserving complete XMM0/RIP with zero retirement. If all
detected events are masked, invalid priority suppresses denormal only in the
same lane; the two lane results and aggregated effective IE/DE commit with the
full destination XMM. Existing sticky flags alone do not fault. This bounded
model has no handler continuation and does not claim hardware delivery. Existing
masked MINPD remains unchanged; JIT/native/C/fragment and physical execution
remain closed.

Local fixed evidence includes the 128 class × class × IM × DM × OSXMMEXCPT
fixtures and 16 supplemental selector/sticky fixtures, complete
control/fetch/budget/form checks, independent result validation,
control/result tampering, comparator echoes and JIT/native denial.
Normative sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2B MINPD pp. 4-16–4-18
([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671241)); Vol. 1
§§4.9.2, 11.5.3.1–3 ([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671436)). See the [plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-38i--exact-long64-minpd-xmm0xmm1-unmasked-invalid-and-denormal-exit).

## S2-38j — exact MAXPD unmasked invalid and denormal exit

The interpreter-only profile `s2-long-maxpd-unmasked-denormal-v1` accepts only
Long64 `66 0F 5F C1` (`MAXPD XMM0,XMM1`), one executable code region, budget one
and stop RIP `entry+4`. Its immutable `MaxpdUnmaskedControlSnapshot` records
SSE2 availability, CR0.EM/TS, CR4.OSFXSR and CR4.OSXMMEXCPT and is echoed exactly
by the result. Complete fetch precedes SSE2/EM/OSFXSR #UD and then TS #NM gates;
both lanes are examined only after these gates, independent of CPL. Reserved
MXCSR bits, DAZ and FTZ must be zero; ZE/OE/UE/PE masks must be set; IM/DM, RC
and prior sticky status are permitted.

Both full XMM operands are snapshotted and both binary64 lanes are precomputed.
MAXPD selects raw SRC2 for either NaN, equal values and signed-zero ties. A
source-2 SNaN is forwarded unchanged. For other operands, SRC1 is selected only
when SRC1 is strictly greater. Raw IE and DE conditions are collected across
both lanes before exception disposition. If any newly detected event is
unmasked, every detected IE/DE flag is ORed into MXCSR and one #XM
(OSXMMEXCPT=1) or #UD (OSXMMEXCPT=0) is reported, preserving full XMM0/RIP with
zero retirement. If all events are masked, invalid priority suppresses DE only
in its own lane; the complete XMM result and effective aggregate status commit.
Existing masked MAXPD remains unchanged. There is no handler continuation.

JIT/native/C/fragment and physical execution remain closed. The bounded local
evidence uses 128 literal lane-class × IM × DM × OSXMMEXCPT fixtures plus 16
selector/sticky cases and an independent raw-bit validator. Normative sources:
Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2B MAXPD pp. 4-5–4-7
([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671241)); Vol. 1
§§4.9.2, 11.5.3.1–3 ([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671436)).

## S2-38k — exact MINPS unmasked invalid and denormal exit

The interpreter-only profile `s2-long-minps-unmasked-denormal-v1` admits only
Long64 `0F 5D C1` (`MINPS XMM0,XMM1`), one executable code region, budget one
and stop RIP `entry+3`. Its immutable control snapshot records SSE availability,
CR0.EM/TS, CR4.OSFXSR and CR4.OSXMMEXCPT. Complete fetch precedes #UD for
missing SSE, CR0.EM or CR4.OSFXSR, then #NM for CR0.TS; lane evaluation happens
after those gates, independent of CPL. With CR4.OSXMMEXCPT clear, a newly
unmasked SIMD FP event reports #UD; otherwise it reports #XM.

MXCSR reserved bits, DAZ and FTZ are zero; ZE/OE/UE/PE masks are one; IM/DM,
rounding control and prior sticky flags may vary. The interpreter snapshots both
XMM operands and evaluates all four binary32 lanes before deciding whether to
commit. MINPS selects raw SRC2 for either NaN, equal values and signed-zero
ties; SRC2 SNaN bits and payload/sign are preserved. Raw IE/DE are aggregated
across all lanes. If either event is newly unmasked, all discovered IE/DE bits
are ORed into status and one exception is returned with XMM0 and RIP unchanged
and no retirement. Otherwise, each lane with IE suppresses only its own DE
status, then all result lanes commit atomically. Existing masked MINPS is
unchanged and is specified by S2-37g.

Sixteen literal lane/control and sixteen result/status fixtures are validated
independently from the production selector. JIT/native/C/fragment admission,
handler continuation and physical execution are not included. Normative source:
Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2B MINPS pp. 4-19–4-21
([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671241)); Vol. 2A
Table 2-19 ([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199));

([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671436)). See the

## S2-38l — exact MAXPS unmasked invalid and denormal exit

The interpreter-only profile `s2-long-maxps-unmasked-denormal-v1` admits only
Long64 `0F 5F C1` (`MAXPS XMM0,XMM1`), one executable code region, budget one
and stop RIP `entry+3`. Immutable controls record SSE availability, CR0.EM/TS,
CR4.OSFXSR and CR4.OSXMMEXCPT. Complete fetch precedes #UD for missing SSE,
CR0.EM or CR4.OSFXSR, then #NM for CR0.TS; CPL does not change these gates.
A newly unmasked SIMD event reports #XM when OSXMMEXCPT is set and #UD when it
is clear.

The supported MXCSR subset requires reserved bits, DAZ and FTZ clear; ZE/OE/UE/PE
masked. IM, DM, RC and prior sticky flags may vary. Both XMM inputs are
snapshotted and all four binary32 lanes are precomputed before global event
disposition. MAXPS returns raw SRC2 for either NaN, equal values and signed-zero
ties; a source-2 SNaN is forwarded unchanged. Otherwise it selects SRC1 only
when SRC1 is greater than SRC2. An unmasked IE or DE preserves full XMM0 and RIP,
sets every discovered raw IE/DE sticky flag, retires zero instructions and
reports one exception. Masked completion applies IE-over-DE only within each
lane and commits all of XMM0 atomically. Existing masked MAXPS is unchanged.

The 2048-case ISA matrix crosses `{none,I,D,I+D}^4`, IM, DM and OSXMMEXCPT.
Thirty-two literal schema-v2 fixtures cover lane/control anchors and source
selection cases; the independent validator derives lane events and MAXPS result
bits without calling the production selector. Exact-form, gate-order, CPL,
fetch/truncation, STOP/budget, no-memory-callback and JIT/native-denial checks
are included. Other MAXPS forms, memory, prefixes, DAZ/FTZ, handler continuation,
transitions and physical execution remain outside this profile.

Normative sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2B MAXPS pp. 4-8–4-10
([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671241)); Vol. 2A
Table 2-19 ([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199));
