([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671436)).

## S2-37s — canonical Long64 CVTDQ2PS XMM register pairs

The interpreter-only schema-v2 profile `s2-long-cvtdq2ps-registers-v1` accepts
all 256 XMM0–15 destination/source register pairs, including self-aliases.
Canonical bytes are `0F 5B /r` with ModR/M.mod=3; when either register is high,
the stream uses exactly one REX byte: `41` for a high source, `44` for a high
destination, or `45` for both. The independent schema parser derives both
indices and instruction length from the full stream and requires one executable
code mapping, budget one, and checked stop RIP `entry+length`. It refuses
REX40/W/X, memory, mandatory/repeated/reordered prefixes, trailing bytes,
VEX and EVEX as profile exclusions only. In particular, `66 0F 5B` and
`F3 0F 5B` are not treated as CVTDQ2PS. These refusals make no broad
architectural #UD claim. Earlier conversion profiles retain their original
bounds.

After complete fetch, missing SSE2, CR0.EM, or CR4.OSFXSR produces #UD; CR0.TS
then produces #NM. The prerequisite gates apply at CPL0–3 and preserve full
state with no data-memory callback or retirement. The profile echoes SSE2,
EM, TS, OSFXSR and OSXMMEXCPT controls. It accepts MXCSR bits under mask
`0x0000ffbf`; FTZ is irrelevant. It models newly generated Precision only.

Execution snapshots the complete source XMM before any destination write, sign
extends its four dwords, and converts each directly to binary32 using MXCSR.RC
through `Binary32::from_i64`. All four converted lanes replace the full
destination. Inexactness is ORed across lanes and sets only sticky MXCSR.PE;
all other MXCSR bits remain unchanged. If any lane is inexact and PM=0, PE is
committed before #XM when OSXMMEXCPT=1 or SIMD-generated #UD when it is zero.
That fault suppresses every destination lane, RIP advance and retirement. A
masked or exact conversion commits the complete destination and retires once;
old PE by itself does not fault.

The independent result validator derives binary32 bits with an integer-only
oracle and computes per-lane inexactness separately before aggregating PE.
Tests execute all 256 pairs with distinct XMM sentinels and all 16 aliases; the
16 lane-inexact masks cross RC, PM, OSXMMEXCPT and old PE (512 cases). Literal
vectors include signed values around 2^24, ties, directed rounding, i32
endpoints and zero. The lane-3-only inexact case checks whole-destination
suppression. Gate/CPL and truncated-fetch tests verify full fetch order and no
data callbacks; malformed encodings, stop/schema/result/control tampering and
JIT/native denial are covered. No JIT, native, C ABI, fragment or generic CPUID
admission is provided.

This is register-only and bounded: m128 memory forms (including alignment
#GP and address/page faults), other modes/encodings, physical acceptance, and
the parent S2-37/S2-38 requirements remain open. Sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093
Vol. 2A CVTDQ2PS pp. 3-211–3-213; §2.5.2 and Table 2-19 p. 2-27; Vol. 1
§§11.5.3.1–3; REX §2.2.1.2/Table 2-4
([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199)). See the
[plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-37s--canonical-long64-cvtdq2ps-xmm-register-pairs),
[report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-37s--canonical-long64-cvtdq2ps-xmm-register-pairs),
and [fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-37s-canonical-cvtdq2ps-register-pairs).

## S2-37t — canonical Long64 CVTSS2SD XMM register pairs

The interpreter-only schema-v2 profile `s2-long-cvtss2sd-registers-v1` accepts
all 256 canonical Long64 XMM destination/source pairs. Low-register forms are
`F3 0F 5A /r`, length 4. Extended source and/or destination use exactly
`F3 41`, `F3 44`, or `F3 45` before `0F 5A /r`, length 5. ModR/M.mod must be 3.
The independent schema parser derives the complete register pair and length,
and requires one executable code mapping, budget one, and checked stop RIP
`entry+length`. Redundant REX 40, W/X REX, memory, other/additional/reordered
prefixes, trailing bytes, VEX and EVEX are profile refusals. Older profiles are
unchanged.

After complete fetch, SSE2 absence, CR0.EM, or CR4.OSFXSR produces #UD; CR0.TS
then produces #NM. These gates apply at CPL0–3. The profile echoes SSE2, EM, TS,
OSFXSR and OSXMMEXCPT. MXCSR is limited to `0x0000ffbf`, with DAZ=0; FTZ and RC
do not change the conversion.

The interpreter snapshots source XMM before writing, reads only its low 32 bits,
and preserves destination high64 and every unrelated architectural field. Raw
binary32 zero, normal and infinity widen exactly without flags. QNaN sign and
payload map into binary64 without IE. SNaN maps to a quiet binary64 NaN and
raises new IE. A binary32 subnormal widens exactly to normal binary64 and raises
new DE. Only the low binary64 destination is replaced. New IE/DE are ORed into
old sticky status. If a new IE/DE event is unmasked by IM/DM, the corresponding
sticky bit is committed first; OSXMMEXCPT selects #XM or SIMD-generated #UD,
and destination, RIP advance and retirement are suppressed. Masked completion
commits destination/status; old sticky IE/DE alone never fault. No PE/OE/UE/ZE
is generated and no data-memory callback occurs.

The independent schema oracle inspects binary32 sign/exponent/fraction bits and
constructs binary64 bits directly, including all 23 subnormal leading-bit
positions and NaN payload shifts/quieting. It does not call the production
widening helper or host floating point. Runner coverage includes all 256 pairs
and 16 aliases, ignored high96 patterns, destination high64 preservation,
zero/normal/infinity boundaries, signed QNaN/SNaN payloads, all subnormal
leading-bit positions, IE/DE mask and OSXMMEXCPT cases with old sticky bits,
prerequisite/CPL/fetch/no-callback, malformed inputs, tampering, and JIT/native
denial. JIT/native/C/fragment/generic CPUID admission and physical execution
remain closed. m32/memory, other encodings/modes, full S2-34/38, Stage 4 and
physical acceptance remain open.

Sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 1 Table D-11, Table 11-1, §§11.5.2.2,
11.5.3.1–3 ([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671436));
Vol. 2A CVTSS2SD pp. 3-240–3-241, Tables 2-15 and 2-20
([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199)). See the
[stage plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-37t--canonical-long64-cvtss2sd-xmm-register-pairs),
[report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-37t--canonical-long64-cvtss2sd-xmm-register-pairs),
and [fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-37t-canonical-cvtss2sd-register-pairs).


## S2-37u — canonical Long64 CVTPS2PD XMM register pairs

The bounded interpreter-only schema-v2 profile is
`s2-long-cvtps2pd-registers-v1`. It accepts all 256 XMM destination/source
pairs, including aliases. Low registers use canonical bare `0F 5A /r` (length
3); extended registers use exactly REX `41`, `44`, or `45` before the opcode
(length 4). ModR/M.mod is 3. One executable mapping, budget one and checked
stop RIP `entry+length` are required. Redundant `40`, W/X, memory, mandatory or
other prefixes, trailing bytes, VEX and EVEX are profile refusals. The
independent parser derives both register indices and instruction length.

After full fetch, SSE2 absence, CR0.EM or CR4.OSFXSR produces #UD; CR0.TS then
produces #NM at CPL0–3. The profile echoes SSE2, EM, TS, OSFXSR and OSXMMEXCPT.
MXCSR accepts only bits in `0x0000ffbf`; DAZ is refused. RC and FTZ do not
change this exact widening conversion.

The executor snapshots the source XMM, reads only low64 as two binary32 lanes,
and widens each exactly to binary64. It replaces the full 128-bit destination;
self-aliases use the initial source. QNaN sign/payload mapping adds no IE,
SNaNs are quieted and raise IE, and subnormals widen to normal binary64 and
raise DE. New IE and DE are aggregated independently across the lanes and ORed
into old sticky status while preserving all other MXCSR bits. Old sticky IE/DE
alone do not fault. If a new IE/DE is unmasked (IM/DM=0), applicable sticky bits
commit before the entire destination, RIP advance and retirement are suppressed;
OSXMMEXCPT selects #XM or SIMD-generated #UD. No PE/OE/UE/ZE is generated.

The independent result oracle parses source bits and applies the independent
integer-only binary32 widening oracle to each lane. Runner coverage includes all
256 pairs and 16 aliases; the 288-case Cartesian exception matrix; signed NaN
payloads, subnormal leading positions/extrema, ignored high64, whole-destination
replacement and suppression, gate/fetch/CPL/no-callback, malformed encodings,
tampering, and JIT/native denial. No memory callbacks occur. JIT/native/C ABI,
fragment and generic CPUID admission remain closed. The m64 memory operand,
other forms/modes, physical acceptance, and parent S2-37/S2-38 remain open.

Sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A CVTPS2PD pp. 3-228–3-230 and Tables 2-15
and 2-20 p. 2-28; Vol. 1 Table D-11 and §§11.5.3.1–3. See the [stage
plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-37u--canonical-long64-cvtps2pd-xmm-register-pairs),
[report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-37u--canonical-long64-cvtps2pd-xmm-register-pairs),
and [fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-37u-canonical-cvtps2pd-register-pairs).

## S2-37v — canonical Long64 COMISS and UCOMISS XMM register pairs

The bounded interpreter-only schema-v2 profile is
`s2-long-comiss-ucomiss-registers-v1`. It admits both COMISS `0F 2F /r` and
UCOMISS `0F 2E /r`, all 256 XMM destination/source pairs, and ModR/M.mod=3.
Low registers use the canonical 3-byte form; an extended destination and/or
source requires exactly REX `44`, `41`, or `45`, respectively (length 4).
The independent parser derives opcode, operand indices and length. One
executable mapping, budget one and checked stop RIP `entry+length` are required.
Other prefixes, REX `40`/W/X, memory, trailing bytes, VEX and EVEX are local
profile refusals. Existing profiles remain immutable.

Both XMM operands are snapshotted, but only each low32 is read. The full XMM
register file remains unchanged. Raw binary32 comparison treats +0 and -0 as
equal and orders finite values and infinities by sign and magnitude. On
completion, unordered sets ZF/PF/CF, greater sets none, less sets CF, and equal
sets ZF. OF/SF/AF are cleared; all other RFLAGS bits and their definedness are
preserved.

COMISS raises a new Invalid Operation for either QNaN or SNaN. UCOMISS raises
it only for SNaN; QNaN alone completes unordered. A NaN in either operand has
priority over a subnormal in the other operand and suppresses new Denormal
status. In the absence of NaNs, either subnormal raises new DE. New IE/DE are
ORed into old MXCSR sticky status; preexisting sticky bits alone do not fault.
If an applicable event is unmasked, sticky status is committed before #XM
when CR4.OSXMMEXCPT=1 or SIMD-generated #UD otherwise. The compare then
preserves full old RFLAGS, RIP and zero retirement. Masked events commit status
and comparison flags. No other new SIMD exception flag is generated.

Full fetch precedes SSE availability/CR0.EM/CR4.OSFXSR #UD and then CR0.TS
#NM, at CPL0–3. The control inputs, including OSXMMEXCPT, are echoed in the
result. MXCSR accepts only bits in `0x0000ffbf`; DAZ is refused, and RC/FTZ are
irrelevant. Only the interpreter profile accepts this operation. JIT, native,
C ABI, fragment and generic CPUID admission remain closed. Memory forms, other
modes, physical acceptance and the parent S2-37/S2-38 scope remain open.

Normative sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A COMISS pp. 3-201–3-202
([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199)); Vol. 2B
UCOMISS pp. 4-735–4-736 ([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671241));
Vol. 1 Tables D-6/D-7, §4.9.2 NaN-before-denormal priority, and
§§11.5.2.2/11.5.3 ([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671436)).

## S2-37w — canonical Long64 COMISD and UCOMISD XMM register pairs

The bounded schema-v2 interpreter-only profile is
`s2-long-comisd-ucomisd-registers-v1`. It admits COMISD `66 0F 2F /r` and
UCOMISD `66 0F 2E /r`, all 256 XMM destination/source pairs, and ModR/M.mod=3.
Low pairs use the canonical 4-byte form; extended operands require the exact
prefix order `66 41/44/45 0F opcode /r` and length 5. The independent parser
derives opcode, operand indices and length. One executable mapping, budget one
and checked stop RIP `entry+length` are required. Other or duplicate prefixes,
REX.W/X, reordered prefixes, memory, trailing bytes, VEX and EVEX are profile
refusals.

Both operands are snapshotted, only their low64 values are read, and the full
XMM file is preserved. Raw binary64 comparison treats signed zeros as equal
and orders finite values and infinities by sign and magnitude. COMISD raises
new IE for QNaN or SNaN; UCOMISD raises it only for SNaN. If either operand is
NaN, new DE is suppressed; otherwise either subnormal raises DE. New sticky IE
and DE are ORed into MXCSR. Only newly raised unmasked events fault. Sticky
status is committed before #XM when CR4.OSXMMEXCPT=1 or SIMD-generated #UD
otherwise. An unmasked fault preserves full RFLAGS, RIP and retirement.
Completion sets ZF/PF/CF for unordered, ZF for equal, CF for less, and clears
OF/SF/AF while preserving all other RFLAGS bits and definedness.

Full fetch precedes SSE2 availability/CR0.EM/CR4.OSFXSR #UD then CR0.TS #NM,
at CPL0–3. MXCSR accepts supported bits only, DAZ is refused, and RC/FTZ are
irrelevant. The control inputs including OSXMMEXCPT are echoed. JIT, native,
C ABI, fragment and generic CPUID admission remain closed. Memory forms, other
modes, physical acceptance, and parent S2-37/S2-38 remain open. The final
combined Mac mini acceptance stage is deferred.

Normative sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A COMISD pp. 3-199–3-200
([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199)); Vol. 2B
UCOMISD pp. 4-733–4-734 ([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671241));
Vol. 1 Tables D-6/D-7, §4.9.2 NaN-before-denormal priority, and
§§11.5.2.2/11.5.3 ([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671436)).

## S2-37x — canonical Long64 CMPSS XMM register pairs

The schema-v2 interpreter-only profile `s2-long-cmpss-registers-v1` admits
legacy `F3 0F C2 /r ib` with ModR/M.mod=3, all 256 XMM pairs, and immediate
predicates 0–7. Low register pairs use the canonical 5-byte encoding. Extended
operands use exactly REX `41`, `44`, or `45` after F3 (6 bytes). The fixture
parser independently derives opcode, registers, predicate and length. One
executable mapping, one-instruction budget and checked stop RIP are required.
Other/repeated/reordered prefixes, REX.W/X, memory, trailing bytes, VEX/EVEX,
and immediate values above 7 are profile refusals. High immediate bits are
locally rejected without asserting architectural #UD.

Both XMM inputs are snapshotted; only low32 is consumed. Comparison uses raw
binary32 classification and signed-magnitude ordering, with +0 and -0 equal.
Predicate bits 0–7 mean, in order: ordered equal, ordered less, ordered
less-or-equal, unordered, unordered-or-not-equal, unordered-or-not-less,
unordered-or-not-less-or-equal, ordered. Completion writes all ones or zero to
destination low32, preserving its high96 and every other register/state field.

SNaN raises new IE for every predicate. QNaN raises new IE for predicates 1,
2, 5, and 6. If either operand is NaN, new DE from a subnormal other operand
is suppressed; otherwise either subnormal raises DE. New IE/DE are ORed with
old sticky bits. Existing sticky bits alone do not fault. Only a newly raised,
unmasked event exits: commit MXCSR status first, return #XM when
CR4.OSXMMEXCPT=1 or SIMD-generated #UD otherwise, and preserve destination,
RIP and retirement. Full instruction fetch precedes SSE availability/CR0.EM/
CR4.OSFXSR #UD and then CR0.TS #NM at CPL0–3. JIT, native, generic CPUID, C ABI
and fragment admission remain closed. Memory forms, other modes, physical
acceptance and parent S2-37/S2-38 remain open; hardware acceptance is deferred
to the final combined stage.

Normative sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A CMPSS pp. 3-189–3-192, Table 3-8
([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199)); Vol. 1
§4.9.2 NaN-before-denormal priority and §11.5.3
([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671436)).

claim is made for high immediate bits.

Predicate bits 0–7 mean, in order: ordered equal, ordered less, ordered

SNaN raises new IE for every predicate. QNaN raises new IE for predicates 1,

The independent fixture oracle classifies raw u64 binary64 values and applies

code. Coverage builds all 2048 encodings and checks truth relations and

## S2-37z — canonical Long64 CMPPD XMM register pairs

The local schema-v2 interpreter profile `s2-long-cmppd-registers-v1` admits
legacy `66 0F C2 /r ib` for every XMM register pair and predicate 0–7. It accepts
only canonical low-register length-5 and extended length-6 encodings; the latter
use exactly REX `41`, `44`, or `45` after `66`. Memory operands, other REX bits,
redundant/reordered prefixes, trailing bytes, VEX/EVEX, and imm8 above 7 are
profile refusals, not claims of architectural #UD for reserved immediate bits.
The executable fixture maps exactly one instruction, sets budget 1 and checks
the following RIP.

Both complete source XMM registers are snapshotted before execution. The two
raw binary64 lanes each compare according to one of the eight legacy predicates
and independently produce `0xffffffffffffffff` or zero. Signed zeros compare
equal. SNaN raises IE; QNaN raises IE for predicates 1, 2, 5 and 6. A NaN only
suppresses DE in its own lane, so exception flags aggregate across lanes. New
IE/DE are ORed with sticky status. A newly unmasked exception commits MXCSR
status first, then delivers #XM when OSXMMEXCPT is set or SIMD #UD otherwise,
without writing either result lane, advancing RIP or retiring. Completion writes
both destination lanes and preserves flags/unrelated state.

After complete instruction fetch, missing SSE2, CR0.EM or missing CR4.OSFXSR
produces #UD; CR0.TS then produces #NM, at CPL0–3. DAZ/reserved MXCSR bits are
profile refusals; RC, FTZ, exception masks and prior sticky bits are admitted.
Only the interpreter profile is admitted. JIT/native, generic CPUID, C ABI and
fragment paths remain closed, and parent S2-37/S2-38 remain open. Memory forms
and hardware acceptance are outside this bounded profile; physical validation
is deferred to the final combined substage.

Normative sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A CMPPD pp. 3-168–3-174, Table 3-8
([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199)); Vol. 1

([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671436)).

## S2-37ab — canonical Long64 CVTSS2SI register space

The bounded schema-v2 profile `s2-long-cvtss2si-registers-v1` accepts exactly
512 canonical register encodings: r32/r64 destination × XMM0–15 low32 source.
`F3 0F 2D /r` selects r32; `F3 REX.W 0F 2D /r` selects r64. ModR/M.mod=3
is mandatory; REX.R extends the GPR destination and REX.B the XMM source.
Noncanonical prefixes, REX.X, memory, trailing bytes, VEX and EVEX are local
profile refusals. Only the interpreter profile is admitted.

The operation reads only source XMM low32 and applies MXCSR.RC. r32 writes zero
extended bits to the destination GPR. All XMM state, unrelated GPRs and RFLAGS
are preserved. Masked Invalid writes integer indefinite; exact signed minimum
is valid and can be distinguished by IE. Invalid sets IE and suppresses PE;
valid fractional rounding sets PE. Sticky IE/PE update precedes unmasked #XM or
SIMD-generated #UD. An unmasked new event suppresses destination, RIP advance
and retirement atomically; old sticky status alone does not fault. CVTSS2SI does
not signal DE for subnormal input, including when DM is unmasked. Full fetch
precedes SSE/EM/OSFXSR #UD and then TS #NM, uniformly at CPL0–3. No data-memory
access occurs. DAZ/reserved MXCSR settings are refused by this local profile.
JIT, native, generic, C and fragment paths remain closed. Memory forms, other
modes/prefixes and physical acceptance are not claimed; parent S2-37/S2-38 stay
open and hardware acceptance remains in the combined final stage.

The fixture oracle independently parses and rounds raw binary32 fields using
integer arithmetic. It does not call production conversion helpers. Provenance:
Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A `CVTSS2SI` pp. 3-242–3-243; Vol. 1 §11.5.2.2
explicitly excludes this conversion from denormal exception signaling
([official SDM](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199)).

The fixture oracle parses raw binary64 fields and performs integer rounding and

## S2-37af — canonical Long64 CVTPS2DQ XMM register pairs

The schema-v2 interpreter profile `s2-long-cvtps2dq-registers-v1` accepts all
256 XMM destination/source pairs in Long64. It requires `66 0F 5B /r`,
ModR/M.mod=3, and exactly one REX `41`, `44`, or `45` after `66` when an XMM
index is extended. Memory, REX.W/X/40, repeated/reordered/other prefixes,
trailing bytes, VEX and EVEX are bounded-profile refusals only. Runtime
admission is independent of CVTDQ2PS; JIT, native, C ABI, fragment and generic
CPUID paths remain closed.

Execution snapshots the complete source before writing, rounds all four raw
binary32 lanes using MXCSR.RC, then checks signed-i32 range. A masked invalid
lane returns `0x80000000`; exact −2^31 remains valid. New IE is accumulated
before computation; new PE is accumulated only from valid inexact lanes. With
IM=0, any new IE commits IE and faults before adding PE from another lane. With
IM=1, invalid lanes do not suppress PE from valid inexact lanes; IE|PE is
committed and PM controls the post-computation fault. Old sticky bits are
preserved and alone do not fault. Unmasked new IE/PE suppresses the entire XMM
destination, RIP and retirement, then selects #XM or SIMD-generated #UD by
OSXMMEXCPT. This conversion raises no DE; the local profile rejects DAZ and
ignores FTZ.

Full fetch precedes SSE2/EM/OSFXSR #UD and TS #NM gates at CPL0–3. No data
memory callbacks occur. The result oracle classifies and rounds raw `u32` bits
with independent integer arithmetic. It exercises the complete lane-event ×
RC × masks × OSXMMEXCPT × sticky-status matrix, aliases, tie and signed-range
boundaries, subnormals, atomic destination suppression, gates/fetch and strict
metadata refusal. Memory m128, other modes, hardware acceptance, and parent
S2-37/S2-38 remain open. Hardware evidence is reserved for the combined final
stage. Source: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A CVTPS2DQ pp. 3-225–3-227; Vol. 1
§§11.5.3.2–3 ([official SDM](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199)).

precedes SSE2/EM/OSFXSR and TS gates at CPL0–3; no data callbacks occur. The
profile may refuse DAZ and reserved MXCSR bits; FTZ is irrelevant.

sticky combinations, RC invariance, boundaries, aliasing, atomicity, gates,
malformed forms, metadata tampering and backend denial. Memory sources, other
modes and physical acceptance remain open. See the [plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-37ai--canonical-long64-cvttpd2dq-xmm-register-pairs),

and [report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-37ai--cvttpd2dq-register-pair-interpreter-profile-2026-10-30).

## S2-37ak — canonical Long64 SQRTPS XMM register pairs

The strict schema-v2 interpreter-only profile `s2-long-sqrtps-registers-v1` admits all 256 canonical Long64 `0F 51 /r` XMM register pairs with ModR/M.mod=3. Low-register forms are three bytes; an extended destination or source requires exactly one adjacent REX `41`, `44`, or `45` before `0F`, making a four-byte encoding. It rejects mandatory/other/redundant/reordered prefixes, REX.W/X/40, memory, trailing bytes, VEX and EVEX. JIT/native/C ABI/fragment/generic paths are closed.

SQRTPS uses the SSE/CR0/CR4 gate: full fetch precedes SSE-disabled/CR0.EM/CR4.OSFXSR #UD and then CR0.TS #NM at CPL0–3. The profile snapshots the four source binary32 lanes and replaces the whole destination XMM only after success. It rejects DAZ and reserved MXCSR bits, accepts all RC values, FTZ, masks and prior sticky flags, and performs no data callbacks.

Each lane independently contributes precompute IE for negative nonzero finite/infinity or SNaN, and precompute DE for a positive subnormal. A negative subnormal is the terminal other-invalid case for its lane and contributes IE only. QNaN passes without IE. Aggregate IE/DE across lanes before computing; if any new pre-event is unmasked, commit all new IE/DE sticky bits and fault without adding new PE from any lane. If those events are masked, compute every lane using MXCSR.RC and aggregate PE. Commit new sticky flags before #XM when CR4.OSXMMEXCPT=1 or SIMD-generated #UD otherwise; an unmasked pre/post event suppresses the complete XMM result, RIP advance and retirement. Old sticky bits alone do not fault. FTZ does not change finite positive SQRTPS results because their square roots are normal.

The independent schema-v2 oracle classifies raw `u32` lanes and performs integer-only square-root rounding, then aggregates packed pre/post events without using od-isa floating-point helpers or host FP. Local tests and the literal fixture establish interpreter behavior only; they are not physical acceptance. Memory forms, other execution modes and parent S2-37/S2-38 remain open. Sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2B SQRTPS pp. 4-664–4-666 ([Vol. 2B](https://cdrdv.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671241)); Vol. 1 §§11.5.2.1–.2, 11.5.3.1–.3 ([Vol. 1](https://cdrdv.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671436)); Vol. 3A Event 19 and Table 7-8 ([Vol. 3A](https://cdrdv.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671190)); Intel Floating-Point Reference Sheet v2.13 ([PDF](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/786447/floating-point-reference-sheet-for-intel-architecture.pdf)). See the [plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-37ak--canonical-long64-sqrtps-xmm-register-pairs), [report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-37ak--sqrtps-register-pair-interpreter-profile-2026-10-30), and [fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-37ak-canonical-sqrtps-register-pair).

## S2-37aj — canonical Long64 SQRTSS XMM register pairs

The strict schema-v2 interpreter-only profile `s2-long-sqrtss-registers-v1` admits all 256 canonical Long64 register pairs for `F3 0F 51 /r`, ModR/M.mod=3. It requires exactly one adjacent `41`, `44`, or `45` REX after F3 if either register is extended. Low forms are four bytes; extended forms are five. Memory, redundant/repeated/reordered/other prefixes, trailing bytes, VEX and EVEX are refused. JIT, native, C ABI, fragment and generic paths remain closed.

The source low dword is snapshotted before writing; MXCSR.RC selects rounding, the destination high 96 bits and unrelated state are preserved. This bounded profile rejects DAZ and reserved MXCSR encodings and accepts all RC values, FTZ, exception masks and preexisting sticky flags. With DAZ=0, positive subnormal input reports DE before computation; masked DE permits SQRTSS computation and any PE can then be reported. Negative nonzero input, including negative subnormal, takes the instruction's other-invalid path and reports IE only; masked invalid produces `0xffc00000`. SNaN raises IE and is quieted; QNaN passes without IE. NaN sign/payload behavior follows the local `Binary32::sqrt_raw_result` policy and is not asserted as a hardware payload guarantee. Positive finite inexact results report PE. FTZ is irrelevant because finite positive square-root outputs are normal.

New sticky flags commit before unmasked #XM if CR4.OSXMMEXCPT=1, or SIMD-generated #UD otherwise. For the single SQRTSS input, the invalid and denormal paths do not overlap: negative nonzero input, including negative subnormal, raises IE only; positive subnormal raises DE only. An unmasked positive-subnormal DE stops before computation and suppresses PE; masked DE permits computation and possible postcompute PE. All unmasked outcomes suppress the destination, RIP advance and retirement atomically. Full instruction fetch precedes SSE/EM/OSFXSR #UD and TS #NM at CPL0–3, and the instruction performs no data callbacks. See the [S2-37aj plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-37aj--canonical-long64-sqrtss-xmm-register-pairs), [fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-37aj-canonical-sqrtss-register-pair) and [implementation report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-37aj--sqrtss-register-pair-interpreter-profile-2026-10-30). Sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2B SQRTSS pp. 4-669–4-670; Vol. 1 §4.9.2 and §§11.5.2.1–.2, 11.5.3.1–.2; Vol. 3A Table 7-8; Floating-Point Reference Sheet v2.13, pp. 1–2.

## S2-37am — canonical Long64 SQRTSD XMM register pairs

The strict schema-v2 interpreter-only profile `s2-long-sqrtsd-registers-v1`
admits all 256 canonical Long64 XMM register pairs for `F2 0F 51 /r` with
ModR/M.mod=3. Low forms are four bytes; extended indices require one REX
`41`/`44`/`45` immediately after F2, for five bytes. It refuses memory, 66/F3,

SQRTPD Type 2.

The implementation snapshots the source low64 and destination full XMM before
execution. On success it writes only destination low64, preserving the old
high64 even when the source and destination alias. Source high64 is not
classified or consumed. The profile rejects DAZ and reserved MXCSR bits, and
accepts all RC modes, FTZ, masks and old sticky flags. QNaN passes without IE;

nonzero non-NaNs, including negative subnormal and negative infinity, take the
terminal invalid branch: IE only, and masked result `0xfff8000000000000`.

unmasked pre-event commits its sticky flag before fault and prevents PE; an
unmasked DE stops before computation. If pre-events are masked, compute then
apply PE. Every unmasked exception suppresses destination, RIP and retirement;
existing sticky flags alone never fault. FTZ is irrelevant to the normal
nonzero square-root result domain.

or production helper. Local tests cover all pairs, aliasing and high-half
preservation with poisoned source high64, binary64 minimum subnormal exact DE

## S2-37ao — bounded masked-range Long64 SUBPS XMM register pairs

The strict schema-v2 interpreter-only profile `s2-long-subps-registers-v1`
admits all 256 canonical Long64 `0F 5C /r` XMM register pairs with
ModR/M.mod=3. Low forms are three bytes; extended indices use exactly one REX
`41`, `44` or `45` before `0F` and are four bytes. Memory, mandatory prefixes,
reordered/repeated/redundant prefixes, REX.W/X/40, trailing bytes, VEX and EVEX
are refused. Full fetch precedes SSE/EM/OSFXSR #UD and then TS #NM at CPL0–3;
the profile performs no data callbacks. JIT/native/C ABI/fragment/generic
execution remains closed.

Admission requires MXCSR.OM=1 and MXCSR.UM=1 because the available raw
rounding result does not retain the exact-significand distinction needed for
complete OM=0 overflow semantics. DAZ and reserved MXCSR bits are rejected; RC,
FTZ, IM/DM/PM and prior sticky bits are accepted. This is a bounded masked
overflow/underflow profile.

All four lanes use snapshots of the old destination and source XMM. NaNs are
classified before the subtrahend sign transformation. SNaN raises IE and is
quieted by the local raw helper; QNaN alone does not raise IE, and a NaN
suppresses DE only in its own lane. Invalid same-sign infinity subtraction
raises IE. Otherwise subnormal operands raise precompute DE. IE and DE aggregate
across all four lanes before arithmetic. A newly unmasked pre-event commits
IE/DE, suppresses all new OE/UE/PE, and preserves the whole destination XMM and
RIP. When pre-events are masked, all lanes compute with MXCSR.RC; masked
overflow records OE|PE, while inexact tiny results record UE|PE. FTZ can flush a
tiny result to signed zero and adds UE|PE. New status is committed before an
unmasked #XM (OSXMMEXCPT=1) or SIMD-generated #UD otherwise; that outcome keeps
the full XMM unchanged. Prior sticky flags alone do not fault. Success replaces
all 128 destination bits atomically.

The schema oracle uses independent raw-u32 integer arithmetic and rounding,
without host floating point or production helpers; its vectors cover all four RC
settings independently of execution. Production interpreter tests run the
halfway rounding vector at each RC and check the selected result and PE. Local
checks include all 256 pairs and aliases, four-lane routing, SNaN/QNaN and
infinity handling, rhs NaN sign/payload preservation, mixed IE/DE/OE/UE/PE
priority, FTZ, masks/stickies including old sticky bits with clear masks,
atomic PM=0 faults and result-tampering rejection. Runtime tests cover gates,
fetch, CPL and no data callbacks; JIT/native denial is explicit. These
results are local, not physical acceptance. Memory operands, other modes, full
unmasked OE/UE semantics and parent S2-37/S2-38 remain open. Sources: Intel SDM
Rev. 093 Vol. 2B SUBPS pp. 4-690–4-692 and Vol. 2A p. 2-27
([official SDM](https://cdrdv.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199)); Vol. 1
§§4.9.1.4–.6, 11.5.3 and DAZ/FTZ ([Vol. 1](https://cdrdv.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671436));
Vol. 3A Event 19/Table 7-8 ([Vol. 3A](https://cdrdv.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671190));
Intel Floating-Point Reference Sheet v2.13 ([PDF](https://cdrdv.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/786447?fileName=floating-point-reference-sheet-for-intel-architecture.pdf)).
See the [plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-37ao--bounded-masked-range-long64-subps-xmm-register-pairs),
[report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-37ao--subps-register-pair-interpreter-profile-2026-10-30),
and [fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-37ao-bounded-masked-range-subps-register-pair).

FTZ, IM/DM/PM and old sticky flags are accepted.

is the XOR of source signs. NaN propagation uses original operand order: select
the first NaN, quiet a selected SNaN, set IE for any SNaN, and do not set IE for
QNaN alone. A NaN suppresses DE for its lane. Zero×infinity raises IE and
returns `0xfff8000000000000`; otherwise a subnormal operand raises precompute
DE, including zero×subnormal and infinity×subnormal. IE/DE aggregate across both
lanes before arithmetic. A newly unmasked pre-event commits generated IE/DE
only and leaves full XMM, RIP and retirement unchanged. With pre-events masked,
MULPD uses the deterministic production raw binary64 multiply helper and
MXCSR.RC. Masked overflow records OE|PE. Tininess is determined from the
precision-rounded result with an unbounded exponent (WPR.exp), not the exact
product exponent. For `0x0010000000000001 × 0x3feffffffffffffe`, RN/RU produce
minimum-normal with PE only, independent of FTZ; RD/RZ produce maximum-subnormal
with UE|PE, or positive zero with UE|PE when FTZ is enabled. The midpoint
`minimum-normal × (1−2^-53)` remains tiny after precision rounding and retains
UE|PE in every RC mode. FTZ flushes a nonzero result whose WPR exponent is tiny
to XOR-signed zero. Post-rounding PE is aggregated, committed before unmasked #XM (OSXMMEXCPT=1)
or SIMD-generated #UD otherwise, and preserves XMM/RIP/retirement on fault.
Old sticky status alone never faults. Successful execution atomically replaces
the complete destination XMM.

The schema oracle independently multiplies raw-u64 finite significands, rounds
to precision with an unbounded exponent to classify tininess, and then applies
bounded subnormal rounding; it uses neither host floating point nor production
arithmetic helpers. The literal fixture and local tests cover strict decode
and all 256 aliases, integer-oracle validation, production halfway rounding,
the WPR near-minimum-normal boundary and the separate midpoint boundary across
RC/FTZ, full destination atomicity, and JIT/native denial. This is local evidence, not physical
acceptance. Memory forms, other modes, full unmasked OE/UE behavior and parent
S2-37/S2-38 remain open. Sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2B MULPD
pp. 4-142–4-143; Vol. 2A Type 2/Table 2-19; Vol. 1 §§4.9.1.4–.6, 11.5.3 and
DAZ/FTZ; Vol. 3A Event 19/Table 7-8; Intel Floating-Point Reference Sheet v2.13.

## S2-37as — bounded masked-range Long64 MULPS XMM register pairs

The strict schema-v2 interpreter-only profile `s2-long-mulps-registers-v1`
admits all 256 canonical Long64 `0F 59 /r` XMM register pairs with
ModR/M.mod=3. Low forms are three bytes; extended indices use exactly one REX
`41`, `44` or `45` immediately before `0F`, giving a four-byte form. `66`,
F2/F3, memory, reordered/repeated/redundant prefixes, REX.W/X/40, trailing
bytes, VEX and EVEX are refused. Complete fetch precedes SSE/EM/OSFXSR #UD and
then TS #NM at CPL0–3. Data memory is never accessed. JIT/native/C ABI/fragment/
generic execution is closed.

Schema and public runtime require MXCSR.OM=1 and MXCSR.UM=1, reject DAZ and
reserved bits, and allow all RC, FTZ, IM/DM/PM and existing sticky bits. Both
operands are snapshotted before evaluating four packed binary32 products. NaN
selection follows original operand order; selected SNaNs are quieted and any
SNaN raises IE, while QNaN alone does not. A NaN suppresses DE in its lane.
Zero×infinity raises IE and returns `0xffc00000`; otherwise either subnormal
operand raises precompute DE, including zero×subnormal and infinity×subnormal.
IE/DE aggregate across all lanes before arithmetic. A newly unmasked pre-event
commits generated IE/DE only and suppresses the whole destination, RIP advance
and retirement. Masked pre-events proceed through production
`Binary32::multiply_raw_result` under MXCSR.RC. Masked overflow records OE|PE.
Tininess and FTZ are determined with the helper's
`tiny_after_precision_rounding` WPR diagnostic, not exact-product tininess or
only the final subnormal encoding. For `0x00800000 × 0x3f7fffff`, every RC
raises UE|PE; RN/RU produce minimum-normal, RD/RZ maximum-subnormal, and FTZ
flushes to zero. For `0x00800001 × 0x3f7ffffe`, RN/RU produce minimum-normal
with PE only regardless of FTZ; RD/RZ produce maximum-subnormal with UE|PE or
zero under FTZ. Aggregate status commits before unmasked post-rounding PE
raises #XM when OSXMMEXCPT=1 or SIMD-generated #UD otherwise. Full XMM, RIP and
retirement remain unchanged on a fault; success atomically replaces XMM.

The independent schema oracle uses raw integer significands and its own
rounding/exception logic, with no host floating point or production helper. The
literal fixture and focused tests cover strict forms, all 256 pairs, RC/FTZ
boundaries, production halfway rounding, signed overflow, NaN/SNaN selection,
pre/post exception atomicity, controls/CPL, and JIT/native denial. This is local
evidence, not physical acceptance. Memory forms, other modes, complete
unmasked overflow/underflow behavior and parent S2-37/S2-38 remain open.
Sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2B MULPS pp. 4-145–4-147; Vol. 2A Type 2,
Table 2-19; Vol. 1 §§4.9.1.4–.6, 11.5.3 and DAZ/FTZ; Vol. 3A Event 19/Table
7-8; Intel Floating-Point Reference Sheet v2.13.


## S2-37at — bounded masked-range Long64 MULSD XMM register pairs

The strict schema-v2 interpreter-only profile `s2-long-mulsd-registers-v1`

Schema and runtime require MXCSR.OM=1 and MXCSR.UM=1 because complete unmasked
overflow/underflow delivery is outside the bounded profile. DAZ and reserved
MXCSR bits are rejected; all RC modes, FTZ, IM/DM/PM and old sticky flags are
accepted. Both XMM operands are snapshotted. Only old destination.low64 is
multiplied by source.low64; destination.high64 is preserved and source.high64

positive zero. For the adjacent product

only regardless of FTZ; RD/RZ produce maximum-subnormal with UE|PE or positive
zero under FTZ. An unmasked post-rounding PM event commits status before #XM when
OSXMMEXCPT=1 or SIMD-generated #UD otherwise, preserving the complete XMM and
RIP. Old sticky flags alone do not fault.

The independent schema oracle uses raw-u64 integer arithmetic and a scalar
wrapper around its independently implemented finite-lane routine; it uses no
host FP or production arithmetic helpers and does not manufacture a packed
second lane. Local checks cover all pairs and aliases, poisoned source/destination

## S2-37av — bounded masked-range Long64 DIVPD XMM register pairs

The local schema-v2 profile `s2-long-divpd-registers-v1` admits only canonical
Long64 `66 0F 5E /r` with ModR/M.mod=3 and all 16×16 XMM pairs. Low forms are
four bytes; extended registers use exactly `66 41/44/45 0F 5E /r`. Memory,
F2/F3, reordered/repeated/redundant prefixes, REX.W/X/40, trailing bytes, VEX
and EVEX are rejected. Fetch precedes SSE2/CR0.EM/CR4.OSFXSR #UD and then CR0.TS
#NM, at CPL0–3; the profile does no data callbacks. It is interpreter-only;
JIT, native, C ABI, fragment and generic paths remain closed.

Admission requires MXCSR.OM=1 and UM=1, rejects DAZ and reserved MXCSR bits,
and accepts RC, FTZ, IM/DM/ZM/PM and prior sticky flags. The interpreter takes
both source and destination XMM snapshots and computes old destination/source
for both binary64 lanes. NaNs select the first original operand; selected SNaNs
are quieted and any SNaN raises IE. NaNs suppress same-lane ZE and DE. `0/0`
and `∞/∞` raise IE and produce the masked indefinite. Finite or subnormal
numerator over zero raises ZE; `∞/0` does not. Outside those cases, a subnormal
operand raises precompute DE. IE/ZE/DE aggregate across lanes before arithmetic;
unmasked pre-events commit the generated status and fault without XMM/RIP/
retirement changes. With pre-events masked, `Binary64::divide_raw_result`
provides the raw result under MXCSR.RC. Masked overflow records OE|PE. Underflow
tininess uses the precision-rounded unbounded exponent (WPR), not the encoded
exponent. Tiny inexact results raise UE|PE; FTZ flushes tiny nonzero values to
signed zero with UE|PE. Post flags aggregate across lanes before unmasked PM;
old sticky bits alone do not fault.

The independent schema oracle performs raw-u64 quotient/remainder arithmetic
with u128 and no host FP or production helpers. It avoids overflow for large
exponent gaps and rounds only once. The fixture covers `1/3`, the
minimum-normal/2^53 half-minsub tie, exact minimum-normal/2, the `maxsub/2`
half-minsub tie, and `minnormal/nextafter(1,+)` across RC/FTZ. The half-minsub
ties are inexact and raise UE|PE. The additional `subnormal/0` case with ZM=1
and DM=0 raises ZE only because zero-divisor classification precedes DE in that
lane. Focused tests cover all register pairs and aliases, IE/ZE/DE aggregation,
NaN suppression, masks/stickies, atomicity, gates/fetch/CPL, malformed inputs,
tampering and JIT/native denial. These local checks do not establish physical
acceptance. Memory forms, other modes, full unmasked OE/UE behavior and parent
S2-37/S2-38 remain open.

rows in Table 2-19. The explicit Type 2/Table 2-19 cross-reference on p. 3-269
is for VEX forms and is not applied to legacy DIVPD. Vol. 1 §§4.9.1.4–.6,
11.5.2–11.5.3 and DAZ/FTZ; Vol. 3A Event 19/Table 7-8; Intel Floating-Point
Reference Sheet v2.13.

The independent schema oracle uses raw-u32 exact rational arithmetic with no
host FP or production helpers and bounds large exponent shifts. The fixture
covers `1/3` (`3f800000/40400000`): RN/RU return `3eaaaaab`, RD/RZ return
`3eaaaaaa`, with PE. `minnormal/2^24` rounds to zero for RN/RD/RZ and

maxsub for RD/RZ, UE|PE. `minnormal/nextafter(1,+)` returns maxsub
for RN/RD/RZ and minnormal for RU, UE|PE. Exact `minnormal/2` returns

gates/fetch/CPL/no-callback, malformed/tampered inputs and JIT/native denial.

## S2-37az — canonical Long64 ADDPD XMM register pairs

The local schema-v2 profile `s2-long-addpd-registers-v1` admits canonical

SNaN raises IE. NaNs suppress same-lane DE. Opposite-sign infinities raise IE
and return masked indefinite `fff8000000000000`; other infinity results keep

subnormal. IE/DE aggregate before arithmetic. Unmasked pre-events commit all

no production helper. The literal vector adds 2^-53 to 1.0; RN/RD/RZ return 1
with PE and RU returns the next value. Exact tiny

with UE|PE. Overflow midpoint `7fefffffffffffff + 7c90000000000000` returns
infinity with OE|PE under RN/RU and maxfinite with PE only under RD/RZ.
By contrast, maxfinite+maxfinite raises OE|PE in every RC mode, even when
directed rounding returns maxfinite. The handwritten literal contains the

## S2-37du — masked-only Long64 ADDPD XMM0,m128 [RAX]

The local schema-v2 interpreter profile `s2-long-addpd-memory-rax-v1` admits
only exact legacy `66 0F 58 00`, a complete four-byte fetch, budget one and
stop RIP entry+4. It requires SSE2 (`CPUID.01H:EDX[26]`); full fetch precedes

lanes and OR into old sticky status; old ZE and unrelated state are preserved.
Success replaces XMM0 and advances RIP by four. The independent validator
uses fixture data bytes as RHS, compares the full state/memory/control echo and
does not call production arithmetic. The handwritten fixture contains exact
`1.0+2.0` and `2.0+5.0` lanes; runner checks include #UD, #GP, tampering and

## S2-37ba — canonical Long64 ADDPS XMM register pairs

The local schema-v2 profile `s2-long-addps-registers-v1` admits canonical
Long64 legacy `0F 58 /r`, ModR/M.mod=3, for all 256 XMM pairs. Low forms are
three bytes; extended indices use one REX `41`, `44` or `45` before `0F`, for
four bytes. It rejects 66/F2/F3, memory, reordered/repeated/redundant prefixes,
REX.W/X/40, trailing bytes, VEX and EVEX. Full fetch precedes SSE/CR0.EM/
CR4.OSFXSR #UD and then CR0.TS #NM at CPL0–3, with no data callbacks. ADDPS is
SSE, not SSE2. JIT/native/C ABI/fragment/generic execution remains closed.

Admission requires MXCSR.OM=1 and UM=1, rejects DAZ and reserved bits, and
accepts all RC modes, FTZ, IM/DM/ZM/PM and prior sticky flags. Execution
snapshots both XMM inputs and adds four old-destination/source binary32 lanes.
NaNs select the first original operand; the selected SNaN is quieted and any
SNaN raises IE. QNaN alone does not raise IE; NaNs suppress same-lane DE.
Opposite-sign infinities raise IE and return masked indefinite `ffc00000`; other
infinity results keep their sign. Any subnormal input raises DE, including
infinity plus subnormal. IE/DE aggregate before arithmetic. Unmasked new
pre-events commit only the new IE/DE status and suppress every post flag and
the full XMM write. Otherwise `Binary32::add_raw_result` uses MXCSR.RC. Exact
cancellation is -0 only for round-down; same-sign zeros preserve their sign.
Masked overflow is OE|PE; directed overflow to maxfinite may be PE-only.
Tininess is after p=24 precision rounding using the unbounded WPR exponent.
Finite same-format sums are multiples of minsub, so an unflushed exact
subnormal result raises neither UE nor PE. FTZ flushes only tiny nonzero results
to signed zero with UE|PE. Post status commits before unmasked PM delivery,
while XMM/RIP/retirement remain unchanged. Old sticky flags alone do not fault.

The independent schema oracle uses raw-u32 integer arithmetic, no host FP and
no production arithmetic helper. The literal fixture covers positive and
negative halfway ties, an exact subnormal, and the overflow midpoint. Independent
vectors cover all RC modes, exact/FTZ tiny, large exponent gaps with DM masked,
NaN order and quieting, opposite infinities, infinity plus subnormal, event
aggregation, and sticky-flag independence. The runtime checks all 256 pairs,
full fetch and gates, CPL0–3, no data callbacks, malformed encodings, atomic
pre/post exits, PM, and backend denial.

## S2-37bd — canonical Long64 CVTPD2PS XMM register pairs

The local schema-v2 profile `s2-long-cvtpd2ps-registers-v1` admits only canonical
Long64 legacy `66 0F 5A /r` with ModR/M.mod=3, covering every XMM register pair.
An unextended encoding is four bytes; one adjacent REX `41`, `44` or `45` after
66 extends the destination and/or source register and makes it five bytes.
Memory operands, F2/F3, reordered/repeated/redundant prefixes, REX.W/X/40,
trailing bytes, VEX/EVEX, other modes and generic/JIT/native execution are
excluded. The interpreter fetches the full instruction before SSE2/CR0.EM/
CR4.OSFXSR #UD and then CR0.TS #NM checks; the bounded register form issues no
data callbacks and admits CPL0–3.

MXCSR admission requires OM=UM=1, DAZ=0 and all reserved bits clear. RC, FTZ,
IM/DM/ZM/PM and preexisting sticky flags are accepted. Both source lanes are
snapshotted before narrowing. Source.low64 becomes destination.low32 and
source.high64 becomes destination.high32; successful completion zeroes
destination.high64. The old destination never contributes to conversion.

The value conversion is binary64-to-binary32 narrowing with one precision
rounding. Signed zero and infinity keep their sign. NaNs preserve sign and the
high payload bits; SNaNs are quieted and set IE, while neither QNaN nor SNaN
sets PE. Each subnormal source sets DE. IE and DE are aggregated across both
lanes before post-conversion events. An unmasked IE or DE commits only its
sticky status, suppresses all OE/UE/PE effects and leaves the full destination,
RIP and retirement unchanged. Masked overflow sets OE|PE. Tiny inexact results
set UE|PE; FTZ flushes any nonzero tiny result to signed zero and sets UE|PE.
With FTZ clear, exact tiny results do not set UE/PE. An unmasked PM commits
status but leaves the entire destination unchanged. When
OSXMMEXCPT is clear, SIMD numeric faults map to #UD; otherwise they map to #XM.

The independent fixture oracle constructs binary32 results from raw integers
and MXCSR rounding controls without host floating point or production helpers.
The local tests cover all register pairs and aliases, rounding and exponent
boundaries, NaN payload rules, pre/post events, fault atomicity, instruction
gates and backend denial. These checks do not establish physical acceptance,
memory-form support, or parent S2-37/S2-38 completion. Normative references:
Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A CVTPD2PS pp. 3-219–3-222 and the legacy opcode row
in Table 2-19. The Type 2/Table 2-19 note on p. 3-222 applies to VEX forms, not
this legacy instruction. Also Vol. 1 §§4.9.1.4–.6, 11.5.2–11.5.3 and DAZ/FTZ;
Vol. 3A Event 19/Table 7-8; Intel Floating-Point Reference Sheet v2.13.


## S2-37be — canonical Long64 CVTSD2SS XMM register pairs

The interpreter-only schema-v2 profile `s2-long-cvtsd2ss-registers-v1` accepts all 256 canonical Long64 XMM register pairs: legacy `F2 0F 5A /r`, ModR/M.mod=3, with exactly one `41`, `44` or `45` REX byte immediately after F2 if either register is extended. Low forms are four bytes; extended forms are five. Memory, REX.W/X/40, bare/redundant REX, repeated/reordered/other prefixes, trailing bytes, VEX/EVEX and other modes are rejected as profile refusals. JIT, native, C ABI, fragment and generic execution remain denied.

Execution snapshots source.low64 before any write, converts the raw binary64 value to binary32 using MXCSR.RC and `Binary32::narrow_from_binary64`, writes only destination.low32 and preserves destination bits 127:32. Source.high64 and old destination bits are not conversion inputs; source snapshotting defines aliases. The profile accepts RC, FTZ, exception masks and prior sticky status, requires OM=UM=1, DAZ=0 and reserved MXCSR bits clear. QNaN sign/payload follows the deterministic narrowing helper without IE. SNaN is quieted with sign and truncated payload preserved and raises IE. Binary64 subnormal input raises DE. IE/DE are pre-events; an unmasked new IE or DE commits generated pre-event status and stops before post-conversion OE/UE/PE. On masked pre-events, overflow reports OE|PE, inexact conversion reports PE, and tiny inexact results report UE|PE. New unmasked OE/UE/PE status commits before numeric #XM when OSXMMEXCPT=1 or SIMD-generated #UD otherwise; destination, RIP and retirement remain unchanged. Old sticky status alone does not fault.

The independent schema oracle classifies raw u64 values and rounds with integer operations; it does not call production conversion helpers or host floating point. Coverage includes every register pair and alias, ignored source.high64, preserved destination.high96, RC/ties, normal/subnormal boundaries, exact and inexact tiny values with FTZ both ways, overflow, signed NaN payloads, DE/IE/PE masks, sticky bits, pre/post atomicity, fetch/gate/CPL/STOP/budget behavior, malformed input, metadata/result tampering and backend denial. Memory forms and physical acceptance remain open.

Normative source: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A CVTSD2SS pp. 3-234–3-235; the Type 3/Table 2-20 reference on p. 3-235 describes VEX forms and is not claimed for this legacy encoding. The schema-v2 interpreter profile `s2-long-cvttps2pi-register-masked-v1` admits only bytes `0F 2C C1`, with one instruction, budget 1 and stop RIP=entry+3. JIT/native/C ABI/fragment/generic execution remains closed.

Tests cover signed zero and fractions, halfway values, i32 boundaries, QNaN/SNaN/infinity/subnormals, all MXCSR rounding modes, mixed IE/PE lanes and old sticky flags, XMM high64 poison, incoming TOP/tag variations, physical-register selection, exponent word, unrelated-state preservation, full fetch/gate priority, CPL, STOP/budget, malformed forms and backend denial. Physical x86 acceptance and broader CVTTPS2PI forms remain open.

## S2-37bu — bounded Long64 CVTTPS2DQ XMM0,[RAX] aligned m128 memory profile

The schema-v2 interpreter profile admits exact legacy `F3 0F 5B 00`, Long64,
instruction budget 1 and stop RIP=entry+4. It fetches all four instruction
bytes before the bounded prerequisite checks: absent SSE2 (CPUID bit 26),
CR0.EM or CR4.OSFXSR produces #UD, then CR0.TS produces #NM. This ordering is
local profile policy. CPL0–3 are accepted.

The source is exactly one aligned 16-byte span beginning at RAX. The complete
span is checked for canonical48 before alignment and before the single data
read. Misalignment produces #GP(0) without a callback, regardless of CPL or
RFLAGS.AC; aligned AC=0 and AC=1 accesses are accepted. A failed read leaves
the entire CPU state unchanged.

Four raw binary32 lanes are converted to signed i32 by truncating toward zero,
independent of MXCSR.RC. Invalid NaN, infinity, or out-of-range lanes produce
`0x80000000` and sticky IE; valid inexact lanes contribute sticky PE. Lane
flags are OR-combined with incoming status. An invalid lane does not contribute
PE; DAZ=0 subnormals convert to zero and may contribute PE, never DE. The full
128-bit XMM0 destination is replaced. The local supported MXCSR mask is
`0xffbf`; this profile requires IM=PM=1 and DAZ=0. Other local MXCSR admission
failures return Unsupported. No unmasked SIMD exception delivery is modeled.

This instruction does not interact with x87 state. The executor neither gates
on pending x87 exceptions nor mutates x87 fields; arbitrary and pending x87
canaries are preserved. The testkit oracle works from raw binary32 bits using
integer arithmetic only, without host floating point or production conversion
helpers. Runner fixtures cover all RC encodings, all 16 invalid-lane masks,
clear and preexisting IE/PE histories, exact/range/subnormal boundaries, aligned AC=0/1 cases at Ring0, representative
misalignments, schema/tamper checks, and JIT/native denial. Runner snapshots do
not count callbacks. Direct ISA tests cover aligned AC=0/1 × CPL0–3, all 15
nonzero offsets × CPL0–3 × AC0/1 with #GP(0), zero reads and unchanged state,
canonical span/overflow refusals, one 16-byte read, prerequisite gates, strict
MXCSR/isolated DAZ refusals and atomic read failures. JIT, native and C ABI
remain closed. Physical x86 acceptance was not run.

Sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A CVTTPS2DQ pp. 3-249–3-251; Vol. 1
§11.5.2.2 for subnormal handling and Table 14-21 for aligned m128 memory;
Vol. 3A §16.1.3 Table 16-1 p. 16-3 for legacy SSE2 gates ([official Vol. 3A PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671190)). The VEX-only Type 2/Table 2-19 entry does not describe this legacy encoding. See the [plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-37bu--bounded-long64-cvttps2dq-xmm0rax-aligned-m128-memory-profile), [report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-37bu--cvttps2dq-xmm0rax-aligned-m128-memory-profile), and [fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-37bu-cvttps2dq-xmm0rax-aligned-m128-memory-profile).

## S2-37bv — bounded Long64 CVTPS2DQ XMM0,[RAX] aligned m128 profile

The schema-v2 interpreter admits exact legacy `66 0F 5B 00`, Long64, budget 1, and stop RIP=entry+4. It fetches the full instruction before the bounded SSE2 prerequisite gates. Missing SSE2 (CPUID bit 26), CR0.EM, or CR4.OSFXSR produces #UD; CR0.TS produces #NM after those checks. This priority is local profile policy, and CPL0–3 are admitted.

The operand is one aligned 16-byte source span beginning at RAX. The checked canonical48 span and 16-byte alignment are validated before one data read. Misalignment faults #GP(0), without a callback, for any CPL and either AC value; aligned AC=0/1 is accepted. A failed read commits no CPU state.

Each binary32 lane is rounded to signed i32 using MXCSR.RC before checking representability. A NaN, infinity, or rounded out-of-range value returns `0x80000000` and contributes IE. A valid inexact result contributes PE; an invalid lane does not also contribute PE. IE and PE are OR-combined across lanes and with prior sticky flags. DAZ=0 is required; subnormals follow RC, may set PE, and do not set DE. The local supported MXCSR mask is `0xffbf`, with IM=PM=1 as profile admission policy; no unmasked SIMD exception delivery is modeled. Other supported control/status bits are preserved. Full XMM0 is replaced after the successful read.

This instruction has no x87 state effect. The bounded profile allows and preserves arbitrary or pending x87 state without a pending-exception gate. The independent testkit oracle is raw-bit integer-only and does not use host FP or production conversion helpers. Runner tests cover all RC values, positive/negative ties and subnormals, range boundaries, mixed IE+PE and sticky histories, Ring0 aligned AC=0/1, schema negatives, tampering, and JIT/native Unsupported. Direct ISA tests provide full CPL×AC alignment coverage, all 15 misalignment offsets, zero-read/unchanged-state checks, exact 16-byte read and rollback. Runner snapshots do not establish callback counts. Native execution and physical x86 acceptance were not performed.

Sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A CVTPS2DQ pp. 3-225–3-227; Vol. 3A §16.1.3 Table 16-1 p. 16-3 for legacy SSE2 gates; Vol. 1 Table 14-21 for aligned m128 access. Type 2/Table 2-19 is VEX-only and is not used for this legacy form.

## S2-37bw — bounded Long64 CVTTPD2DQ XMM0,[RAX] aligned m128 profile

The schema-v2 interpreter admits exact legacy `66 0F E6 00`, Long64, instruction
budget 1 and stop RIP=entry+4. It fetches all four bytes before the local SSE2
prerequisite checks: missing CPUID.SSE2 (bit 26), CR0.EM, or CR4.OSFXSR causes
#UD; CR0.TS causes #NM after those checks. The priority is bounded local policy,
not a universal SDM exception-priority claim. CPL0–3 are accepted.

The source is exactly one aligned 16-byte span `[RAX..RAX+15]`. The complete
span is checked for canonical48 using checked addition, then alignment is
checked before one read callback. Misalignment produces #GP(0) regardless of
CPL or RFLAGS.AC; it does not produce #AC. Aligned accesses accept AC=0 and
AC=1. A failed read preserves the complete CPU state.

Each raw binary64 lane is truncated toward zero independently of MXCSR.RC, then
the truncated integer is checked against signed i32 bounds. Exact -2^31 is
valid. Thus `2147483647.75` becomes INT32_MAX+PE and `-2147483648.75` becomes
INT32_MIN+PE; `+2^31` and `-2147483649` are invalid. NaN, infinity, and other
out-of-range results produce the indefinite bits `0x80000000` and contribute
IE. A valid inexact lane contributes PE; an invalid lane contributes no PE.
IE/PE are OR-combined across lanes and with incoming sticky status. With DAZ=0,
nonzero subnormals convert to zero+PE and do not raise DE. FTZ does not affect
this integer conversion. The successful result replaces all 128 bits of XMM0:
two i32 lanes followed by zeroes in bits 127:64.

The local MXCSR policy requires supported mask `0xffbf`, DAZ=0 and IM=PM=1;
other exception masks may be clear. This admission boundary does not model
unmasked SIMD exception delivery. x87 state, including pending-exception
canaries, is not gated or changed. The testkit oracle is an independent raw-u64
integer implementation with no host floating-point arithmetic and no
production conversion helper. JIT, native, C ABI, fragment, and generic
admissions remain closed. No physical x86 acceptance is claimed.

Normative sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A CVTTPD2DQ pp. 3-244–3-247
(legacy operation p. 3-246); Vol. 1 §§11.5.2.2, 11.5.2.6, 11.5.3, 11.5.5
and Table 14-21; Vol. 3A §§16.1.3–16.1.4, Table 16-1. See the [Stage 2 plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-37bw--bounded-long64-cvttpd2dq-xmm0rax-aligned-m128-memory-profile), [report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-37bw--cvttpd2dq-xmm0rax-aligned-m128-memory-profile), and [literal fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-37bw-cvttpd2dq-xmm0rax-aligned-m128-truncation-profile).

## S2-37bx — bounded Long64 CVTPD2DQ XMM0,[RAX] aligned m128 profile

when SSE2 (CPUID bit 26) is absent or CR0.EM/CR4.OSFXSR blocks SSE, then #NM

RAX supplies one aligned 16-byte span. Checked canonical48 `RAX+15` and 16-byte

accepted. A failed read does not commit CPU changes. On success, two binary64

low 64 bits of XMM0 receive those values and its high 64 bits become zero.
NaN, infinity and rounded out-of-range lanes produce indefinite `0x80000000`
and sticky IE; valid inexact lanes add PE, invalid lanes do not add PE. Flags
OR across lanes and preserve prior sticky bits. Exact −2^31 is valid. DAZ=0

bits using integer arithmetic only, with no host FP or production helper.

## S2-37ca — bounded Long64 CVTSD2SS XMM0,[RAX] m64 memory profile

The exact schema-v2 interpreter-only encoding is legacy `F2 0F 5A 00` in
Long64. Fetch all four bytes before the local SSE2/EM/OSFXSR #UD then TS #NM
gates; CPL0–3 are admitted. This is bounded test ordering, not a universal
exception-priority claim. RAX names one checked canonical48 `[RAX..RAX+7]`
span, read exactly once after preflight. Unaligned m64 reads are allowed when
RFLAGS.AC=0; AC=1 is a profile-local Unsupported refusal. CPU state is not
committed if the read fails.

The input binary64 is rounded to binary32 according to MXCSR.RC. Tininess is
determined after rounding to 24-bit precision with unbounded exponent (WPR),
before final exponent range encoding. Thus the rounded value's encoded
exponent alone does not determine UE. With FTZ=0, a WPR-tiny inexact result
raises UE|PE, while a WPR-tiny exact result raises neither. With FTZ=1, every
WPR-tiny result is flushed to signed zero and raises UE|PE, including an exact
tiny result; WPR-normal outputs are not flushed. Overflow contributes OE|PE.
SNaNs are quieted, preserve sign and narrowed payload, and contribute IE only;
QNaNs add no IE/PE. DAZ=0 means nonzero source subnormals contribute DE and can
also cause underflow. Existing MXCSR sticky status is preserved. Only
XMM0.low32 changes; XMM0[127:32], architectural state above 127, MXCSR control
bits and unrelated state are preserved. x87/MMX has no gate and is untouched.

Admission requires MXCSR mask `0xffbf`, DAZ=0, and IM/DM/OM/UM/PM=1; ZM is
unrestricted. No unmasked SIMD exception delivery is modeled. A missing SSE
snapshot yields Unsupported after the prerequisite gates and before any data
read. The independent raw-u64 oracle uses integer-only bit construction, not
host FP or production conversion helpers. Native/JIT/C ABI/fragment/generic
execution remains closed; no physical x86 acceptance is claimed.

Normative sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A CVTSD2SS pp. 3-234–3-235; Vol. 1
§§4.9.1.4–4.9.1.6, Table 4-12, §10.2.3.3, §§11.5.2–11.5.3, 11.5.5, Table
D-12, Table 14-21; Vol. 3A §§16.1.3–16.1.4, Table 16-1; Intel Floating-Point
Reference Sheet v2.13 p. 2. Type 3/Table 2-20 is VEX-specific and is not used
as a legacy alignment source. See the [Stage 2 plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-37ca--bounded-long64-cvtsd2ss-xmm0rax-m64-memory-profile), [report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-37ca--cvtsd2ss-xmm0rax-m64-memory-profile), and [fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-37ca--cvtsd2ss-xmm0rax-m64-memory-profile).

full four-byte fetch, budget one and stop RIP entry+4. Local prerequisite gates

## S2-37cc — bounded Long64 CVTSI2SD XMM0,dword ptr [RAX] m32 memory profile

four bytes, then applies SSE2/CR0.EM/CR4.OSFXSR `#UD` and CR0.TS `#NM` gates in

derivation, not a claim that the generic CVTSI2SD Precision-exception entry

remain unchanged. All supported MXCSR rounding modes, FTZ settings, sticky bits,
and exception masks including PM=0/IM=0 are admitted; local supported mask is

## S2-37cd — bounded Long64 CVTSI2SD XMM0,qword ptr [RAX] m64 memory profile

Exact bytes: `F2 48 0F 2A 00` (F2 precedes REX.W). The schema-v2 profile fetches
all five bytes, then applies the local SSE2/CR0.EM/CR4.OSFXSR `#UD` and CR0.TS
`#NM` gates in that order, for CPL0–3. This is a bounded ordering policy, not a

fail-closed refusal, not a host panic.

The checked canonical48 source span is `[RAX,RAX+7]`. The local profile requires
AC=0 while permitting unaligned m64 addresses. It performs exactly one eight-byte
little-endian read, then commits output; memory read failure preserves all CPU
state. On success signed i64 converts directly to binary64 using MXCSR.RC,
writing only XMM0.low64. Binary64 can exactly represent the full i64 exponent
range, so conversion has no overflow. Inexact conversions set sticky PE; exact
conversions add no flags. Existing MXCSR control and status bits are preserved.
Strict fixture admission requires MXCSR mask `0xffbf`, DAZ=0, and PM=1; other supported
exception masks, all RC and FTZ settings, and existing sticky flags are allowed. PM=0, DAZ=1, and reserved MXCSR bits are malformed fixture inputs; direct ISA tests separately verify runtime fail-closed behavior.
XMM0.high64, other XMM registers, and optional x87 state—including pending
canaries—are preserved.

The profile is interpreter-only. Native, JIT, C ABI, and generic backend
admission remain closed; no physical x86 acceptance is claimed. See the [plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-37cd--exact-legacy-long64-cvtsi2sd-xmm0qword-ptr-rax), [report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-37cd--cvtsi2sd-xmm0qword-ptr-rax-m64-memory-profile), and [fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-37cd--cvtsi2sd-xmm0qword-ptr-rax-m64-memory-profile).

## S2-37ce — bounded Long64 CVTSI2SS XMM0,dword ptr [RAX] m32 memory profile

Exact bytes are `F3 0F 2A 00`. The profile fully fetches four bytes before its
local CPUID.SSE (bit 25), CR0.EM, and CR4.OSFXSR `#UD` gates, followed by CR0.TS
`#NM`, for CPL0–3. This is a bounded local ordering policy, not a universal
hardware-priority statement. Missing SSE state after gates returns local
Unsupported rather than panicking.

The checked canonical48 source span is `[RAX,RAX+3]`, followed by exactly one
four-byte little-endian read. Unaligned access is permitted with local RFLAGS.AC
clear; AC set is a local refusal. A read failure or any earlier refusal leaves
CPU state unchanged.

The source is signed i32 and converts directly to binary32 according to
MXCSR.RC. Successful execution changes only XMM0.low32 and sticky MXCSR.PE when
the conversion is inexact; PE is ORed with the old sticky value. Exact inputs
add no status bits, and PE is the only possible newly generated SIMD status.

legacy `F2 48 0F 2C 00`. It fetches five bytes and executes one instruction.
SSE2 feature bit 26 is required; CR0.EM=1 or CR4.OSFXSR=0 produces local
`#UD`, then CR0.TS=1 produces `#NM` under the bounded local ordering. This is
not a universal SDM fault-priority claim. Missing SSE state is refused after
these gates.

Execution captures original RAX, validates canonical48 `[RAX,RAX+7]`, and
performs exactly one eight-byte little-endian read before committing CPU
state. Unaligned m64 is allowed at local RFLAGS.AC=0. AC=1 is a valid negative
fixture that returns local `Unsupported` before span checking or memory
access. A failed read is atomic. Success writes full RAX, using the captured
source address rather than the updated destination.

The binary64 source truncates toward zero regardless of MXCSR.RC, then is
range-checked as signed i64. Masked invalid returns
`0x8000000000000000` and adds sticky IE; valid inexact input adds sticky PE;
invalid input does not add PE. Exact `-2^63` is valid with no IE despite
matching the indefinite bits. Nonzero subnormals add PE but no DE, and FTZ is
irrelevant. The profile uses supported MXCSR mask `0xffbf`, DAZ=0 and IM=PM=1;
all RC and FTZ settings are admitted. XMM, x87, unrelated GPRs, RFLAGS, and
other MXCSR state are preserved. Native/JIT/C/fragment/generic paths remain
closed.

The independent oracle consumes raw binary64 bits and uses integer
classification/conversion only. The runner passed 1/1 with 304 oracle
comparisons in Ring0. The focused testkit filter passed the neighboring R32
oracle helper (1/1), not a standalone R64 oracle test; native-local classifier
passed 1/1. Focused decoder/direct ISA tests passed 3/3. Formatting, layout,
diff check, Graphify update, CN cross-document anchors and independent
code/docs reviews passed. Full suites passed: ISA 1,662; testkit 449; runner
112 unit + 470 fixtures; x86-runner 8+4. Workspace all-target check passed.
No physical x86 acceptance is claimed.

Sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A `CVTTSD2SI` pp. 3-253–3-254; Vol. 1
§11.5.2.2 and Table 14-21; Vol. 3A §16.1.3/Table 16-1. The instruction
entry scopes its Type 3/Table 2-20 reference to VEX forms; Table 2-20 itself
also contains legacy SSE conditions. See the [plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-37cn--exact-legacy-long64-cvttsd2si-raxqword-ptr-rax),
[report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-37cn--cvttsd2si-raxqword-ptr-rax-m64-to-r64-memory-profile), and
[fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-37cn--cvttsd2si-raxm64).

## S2-37co — bounded Long64 COMISD XMM0,qword ptr [RAX] m64 memory profile

The strict schema-v2 profile `s2-long-comisd-memory-rax-v1` admits only the
exact legacy encoding `66 0F 2F 00`. It fetches four bytes and executes one
instruction. SSE2 feature bit 26 is required. CR0.EM=1 or CR4.OSFXSR=0 causes
local `#UD`, followed by `#NM` for CR0.TS=1 under the bounded local ordering;
this is not a universal SDM fault-priority claim. Missing SSE state is refused
after those gates. The direct comparison-relation loop covers CPL0–3; direct
gate/refusal/span/read-failure probes use Ring0.

Execution reads XMM0.low64 as the left binary64 operand and one little-endian
64-bit value from the checked canonical48 span `[RAX,RAX+7]` as the right
operand. Exactly one eight-byte memory read occurs after all pre-read checks.
AC=0 allows unaligned m64 addresses; AC=1 is an admitted negative fixture
that returns local `Unsupported` before span checking or memory access.
Noncanonical spans cause `#GP(0)`. A failed read preserves the complete CPU
state. All GPRs, all XMM registers, x87/MMX state, and unrelated RFLAGS bits
are preserved.

On success, COMISD sets CF/PF/ZF according to the relation: greater=`0`,
less=`CF`, equal=`ZF`, unordered=`CF|PF|ZF`. It clears OF/SF/AF. QNaN or SNaN
adds sticky IE. When either operand is NaN, the comparison does not add DE,
even if the other operand is subnormal. Without NaNs, a subnormal in either
operand adds sticky DE. Prior MXCSR status bits are preserved. The profile
requires the supported MXCSR mask `0xffbf`, DAZ=0, IM=1, and DM=1; PM may be
clear. RC and FTZ have no effect on the comparison. Unmasked exception
delivery is outside this profile.

This interpreter-only profile is closed to native, JIT, generic, C ABI, and
fragment execution. Focused evidence: decoder 1/1 and direct ISA execution
2/2; testkit test-target compilation passed; raw-bit oracle test 1/1; runner
fixture 1/1 with 192 oracle comparisons; native-local-only classification
1/1. Full suites passed: ISA 1,665; testkit 450; runner 112 unit + 471
fixtures; x86-runner 8+4. Workspace all-target check, formatting, layout,
Graphify, diff check, 13 anchors, and independent code/docs reviews passed.
No physical x86 acceptance is claimed.

Vol. 1 §4.9.2, §§11.5.2.2 and 11.5.3, Tables D-6 and D-7; Vol. 3A
§16.1.3/Table 16-1. The instruction entry scopes its Type 3/Table 2-20
reference to VEX forms; Table 2-20 itself also contains legacy SSE
conditions. See the [plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-37co--exact-legacy-long64-comisd-xmm0qword-ptr-rax),
[report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-37co--comisd-xmm0m64), and

## S2-37cs — bounded Long64 CMPSS XMM0,m32 [RAX],imm8 memory profile

The separate strict schema-v2 profile admits exact legacy `F3 0F C2 00 pp`
for `pp=0..7`. It fetches five bytes including the immediate, performs one
four-byte read from the checked canonical48 span `[RAX,RAX+3]`, retires once,
and stops at entry+5. AC=0 permits unaligned reads; AC=1 is local
`Unsupported` after the SSE/TS gates and before memory access. Immediate
values above 7 are local profile refusals after the full fetch and before gate
faults, span checks, or reads; they are not architectural `#UD`. A failed read
or pre-read refusal preserves the entire CPU state.

CMPSS compares XMM0.low32 with the m32 source using its predicate immediate.
It writes all ones or zero to XMM0.low32 only; XMM0.high96, the other XMM
registers, GPRs, x87 state, RFLAGS, and unrelated CPU state are preserved.
For greater/less/equal/unordered relation rows, predicate truth values are
pp0 F/F/T/F; pp1 F/T/F/F; pp2 F/T/T/F; pp3 F/F/F/T; pp4 T/T/F/T; pp5 T/F/T/T;
pp6 T/F/F/T; pp7 T/T/T/F. SNaN adds sticky IE for all predicates. QNaN adds IE
only for pp1, pp2, pp5, and pp6. Any NaN suppresses new DE; otherwise a
subnormal operand adds DE. Existing IE/DE status is sticky. The bounded
profile requires SSE CPUID bit 25, MXCSR supported mask `0xffbf`, DAZ=0, and
IM=DM=1; PM, RC, and FTZ may vary. EM=1 or OSFXSR=0 produces `#UD`, then
TS=1 produces `#NM` for in-range predicates under this local gate order.
Native/JIT/C/fragment/generic execution remains closed.

## S2-37dd — masked-only Long64 SQRTPS XMM0,m128 [RAX]

The interpreter-only schema-v2 profile `s2-long-sqrtps-memory-rax-v1` accepts only exact legacy `0F 51 00`, a three-byte fetch, budget one and stop RIP entry+3. It rejects all prefixes/REX/67, alternate ModR/M, SIB, displacement, truncation/trailing bytes, VEX and EVEX. Full instruction fetch precedes gates. It requires SSE (`CPUID.01H:EDX[25]`), not SSE2; missing SSE, CR0.EM=1 or CR4.OSFXSR=0 yields #UD before CR0.TS=1 yields #NM. XMM/MXCSR state must be present.

Admission is masked-only. MXCSR must have reserved bits clear, no bits outside supported mask `0xffbf`, DAZ=FTZ=0, and all six exception masks set. Any RC and old sticky history are accepted. Unmasked/#XM execution is not implemented. RAX must be 16-byte aligned regardless of AC/CPL. The full canonical48 span `[RAX,RAX+15]` is validated before exactly one `read16`; invalid alignment or span faults #GP(0) before callback. A read error leaves CPU/MXCSR/RIP and retirement unchanged.

All four output lanes derive only from the memory operand; old XMM0 is irrelevant. Each memory lane uses `Binary32::sqrt_raw_result(MXCSR.RC)`. Negative nonzero inputs, including negative subnormal and −∞, yield IE and canonical `0xffc00000`; SNaN follows the helper quieting/payload policy and yields IE; QNaN passes without IE; positive subnormal yields DE; inexact roots yield PE. New IE/DE/PE are aggregated across lanes according to the existing same-lane ordering, then ORed with prior sticky state. Success replaces all XMM0 bits and advances RIP by three, preserving GPRs, RFLAGS, other XMM registers and RAM. Native/JIT/C ABI/generic/fragment routes remain closed.

The independent `independent_sqrtps` testkit oracle uses raw-bit integer arithmetic, not production code or host floating point. Fixture coverage includes all RC modes, poisoned XMM0, zeros/infinities, normal/subnormal inputs, negative normal/subnormal, QNaN/SNaN, and mixed IE|DE|PE, plus strict schema/result/backend controls and fetch/gate/read atomicity. See the [standalone implementation report](../reports/S2_37DD_SQRTPS_MEMORY.md), [plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-37dd--exact-legacy-long64-sqrtps-xmm0m128-rax), [Stage 2 report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-37dd--sqrtps-xmm0m128-rax), and [fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-37dd--sqrtps-xmm0m128-rax).

The schema-v2 profile `s2-long-maxss-memory-rax-v1` accepts only legacy `F3 0F 5F 00`, a four-byte fetch, budget one, and stop RIP entry+4. It requires SSE availability (CPUID.01H:EDX[25]), CR0.EM=0, CR4.OSFXSR=1, and CR0.TS=0; #UD checks precede #NM. The local path checks the full canonical48 span `[RAX,RAX+3]` before exactly one four-byte read. AC=1 returns local Unsupported before span validation or data access; AC=0 admits aligned or unaligned addresses.

Local MXCSR admission allows only supported bits (`mxcsr & 0xffbf`), requires all six exception masks (`mxcsr & 0x1f80 == 0x1f80`), DAZ=0, FTZ=0, and reserved bits 16–31 clear. Any RC and old sticky IE/DE values are accepted. MAXSS selects the raw second operand on ties, including signed-zero ties, and whenever either operand is NaN. NaNs raise IE; a subnormal operand raises DE only when neither input is NaN. New IE/DE are ORed with prior sticky state. Success modifies only XMM0.low32 and effective MXCSR IE/DE, preserving XMM0.high96, the rest of the CPU state, RFLAGS, and definedness. A failed read leaves the full state unchanged. Native/JIT/C ABI/generic/fragment execution remains closed.

## S2-37dg — masked-only Long64 SQRTSS XMM0,m32 [RAX]

The interpreter-only schema-v2 profile `s2-long-sqrtss-memory-rax-v1` accepts only exact legacy `F3 0F 51 00`, a four-byte fetch, budget one, and stop RIP entry+4. MXCSR admission is masked-only: supported bits mask `0xffbf`, all six exception masks set, DAZ=FTZ=0, and reserved bits clear. Any rounding-control mode and previous sticky flags are allowed. Unmasked exceptions/#XM are not modeled. This scalar Type 3 memory form has no 16-byte alignment requirement. AC=1 returns local Unsupported before address validation or data reads; AC=0 admits unaligned addresses. Checked `[RAX,RAX+3]` endpoints must both be canonical48 before exactly one read4. The source is memory m32 only. `Binary32::sqrt_raw_result(MXCSR.RC)` determines the low32 result; only XMM0.low32 changes, with high96 and unrelated state preserved. The SQRTSS terminal invalid path for negative nonzero inputs, including negative subnormal and −∞, raises IE without DE; positive subnormal raises DE and inexact positive results raise PE. FTZ does not affect positive finite square-root results because they are normal. Native/JIT/C ABI/generic/fragment execution and physical x86 acceptance are not claimed.
