## S2-37dh — bounded Long64 MINSS XMM0,m32 [RAX] memory profile

The interpreter-only schema-v2 profile `s2-long-minss-memory-rax-v1` accepts only exact legacy `F3 0F 5D 00`, fetches four bytes, executes one instruction, and stops at entry+4. It requires Long64, SSE availability (CPUID.01H:EDX[25]), CR0.EM=0, CR4.OSFXSR=1, CR0.TS=0, and XMM/MXCSR state. The complete instruction fetch precedes these gates: missing SSE, EM=1, or OSFXSR=0 yields #UD before TS=1 yields #NM. Alternate ModR/M/addressing forms, extra prefixes/REX, VEX/EVEX, truncation, trailing bytes, and non-XMM0 forms are outside the profile.

MXCSR admission allows only supported bits (`0xffbf`), requires all six exception masks (`mxcsr & 0x1f80 == 0x1f80`), DAZ=0, FTZ=0, and reserved bits clear. Every RC mode and all six prior sticky bits are admitted. Unmasked exceptions and #XM delivery are not modeled. The scalar m32 form has no 16-byte alignment requirement: AC=1 returns local Unsupported before span validation or data access; AC=0 allows unaligned RAX. Checked `RAX+3` and both canonical48 endpoints for `[RAX,RAX+3]` must succeed before exactly one read4. A read error preserves CPU/SSE/MXCSR/RIP, RAM, and retirement.

The operation uses only memory m32 and the existing `Binary32::min_sse_raw_result`. It replaces XMM0.low32 and preserves XMM0.high96, unrelated state, RFLAGS, definedness, and memory. Numerical ties, including either signed-zero order, and either QNaN/SNaN select the raw RHS; SNaN payloads are not quieted. Any NaN sets IE and suppresses DE for this scalar operation. Otherwise either subnormal operand sets DE. Generated IE/DE are ORed with prior sticky flags. JIT/native/C ABI/generic/fragment execution remains closed, and no physical x86 acceptance is claimed.

The independent testkit oracle compares raw integer binary32 encodings and does not call the production helper or host floating point. Tests cover all four RC modes × all 64 old sticky histories, RHS source selection, NaNs, denormals, poisoned XMM0, gates and AC/address precedence, exactly one read4, read-failure rollback, schema/result tampering, and backend denial. It requires Long64 and SSE (`CPUID.01H:EDX[25]`), with CR0.EM=0, CR4.OSFXSR=1, CR0.TS=0 and XMM/MXCSR state. ## Local S2-30cx: bounded `FDIV ST(i), ST(0)` (`DC F8..FF`)

The interpreter extends exact bare Long64 `DC F8..FF` to direct x87 FCW
precision division. It computes old `ST(i)/ST(0)` through the existing
bounded reverse-division helper, rounded once at PC24/53/64 under RC. Unlike
addition/subtraction profiles, this division has no normalized-exponent-gap
cutoff. Require present x87 state, absent instruction/data selectors,
`FSW & 0x80df == 0`, supported all-masked FCW, Valid tags for used physical
registers and canonical nonzero Normal binary80 operands. Accept only finite
Normal quotient/result. The self alias `i=0` validates only old ST(0) and
produces exact +1.

Success writes only old physical `(TOP+i)&7`, does not pop, makes PE sticky
from old PE OR inexact, replaces C1 from the helper's incremented result,
preserves C0/C2/C3 by local policy, records FIP=old RIP, advances RIP by two
and retires once. Every refusal is atomic. The previous exact-only S2-30v p64
numeric result domain remains supported, including operands with different
exponents. Other DC directions, D8 and DE forms, architectural x87 exception
delivery, native/JIT and physical x86 acceptance remain outside this local
profile. See the [Stage 2 plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-30cx-bare-fdiv-sti-st0-with-bounded-fcw-precision),
[shared report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-30cx--bounded-fdiv-sti-st0), and
[standalone report](../reports/S2_30CX_X87_FDIV_REVERSE_PRECISION.md).
Normative sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A `FDIV/FIDIV` pp. 3-333–3-335;
Vol. 1 §8.1.5.2/Table 8-2, §8.1.5.3 and §8.5.6.



## Local S2-30cy: bounded `FDIVR ST(i), ST(0)` (`DC F0..F7`)

The interpreter admits only exact bare Long64 `DC F0..F7` and reuses the
bounded reverse-division helper for old `ST(0)/ST(i)`, rounded directly under
the x87 FCW at PC24/53/64. The profile requires present x87 state, absent FCS
and FDS, `FSW & 0x80df == 0`, one of twelve all-masked precision/rounding FCWs,
Valid tags for used registers and canonical nonzero Normal operands. Only a
finite Normal quotient is accepted. There is no exponent-gap cutoff. Alias
`i=0` validates the sole used register and produces exact +1.

Success writes old physical `(TOP+i)&7` without popping, makes PE sticky from
old PE OR inexact, replaces C1 from the rounded-magnitude increment result,
preserves C0/C2/C3 and unrelated state, records FIP=old RIP, advances RIP by
two and retires once. The previous exact p64 result domain is preserved by
comparison with `exact_fdiv_result(state, 0, i)`, including unequal exponents.
Invalid controls, status, selectors, tags, malformed/special/zero operands and
non-Normal outputs refuse atomically. Other directions, exception delivery,
JIT/native admission and physical x86 acceptance are outside this profile.

See the [Stage 2 plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-30cy-bare-fdivr-sti-st0-with-bounded-fcw-precision),
[shared report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-30cy--bounded-fdivr-sti-st0),
and [standalone report](../reports/S2_30CY_X87_FDIVR_REVERSE_PRECISION.md).
Normative sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A `FDIVR/FIDIVR` pp. 3-336–3-338;
Vol. 1 §8.1.5.2/Table 8-2, §8.1.5.3 and §8.5.6.

## S2-37do — masked-only Long64 DIVSS XMM0,m32 [RAX]

The interpreter-only schema-v2 profile `s2-long-divss-memory-rax-v1` admits exactly legacy `F3 0F 5E 00`, four-byte fetch, budget one and stop RIP entry+4. DIVSS requires SSE (`CPUID.01H:EDX[25]`), Long64, CR0.EM=0, CR0.TS=0, CR4.OSFXSR=1 and XMM/MXCSR state. Fetch all four bytes before #UD/#NM gates. The local MXCSR contract admits supported bits `0xffbf`, reserved bits clear, all six exception masks set, DAZ=FTZ=0, all RC modes and prior sticky histories. AC=1 returns Unsupported before span/address/data-read work; AC=0 allows unaligned m32. Check checked `RAX+3` and both canonical48 endpoints before exactly one read4; failures preserve state and retirement.

Divide old XMM0.low32 by the actual memory RHS via `Binary32::divide_raw_result` and the raw-u32 `independent_divss` oracle. Preserve XMM0.high96 and unrelated state; merge IE/DE/ZE/OE/UE/PE. Classify original NaNs first, then finite-nonzero/zero ZE, then DE, then result flags. WPR tiny/underflow uses tininess after rounding; exact tiny raises no UE. The Type 3 note on Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A p. 3-276 refers to VEX forms, not this legacy SSE encoding. JIT/native/C ABI/generic/fragment and unmasked/#XM paths remain closed. No physical x86 acceptance is claimed.

See [Stage 2 plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-37do--masked-only-legacy-long64-divss-xmm0m32-rax), [shared report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-37do--divss-xmm0m32-rax), [standalone report](../reports/S2_37DO_DIVSS_MEMORY.md), and [fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-37do--divss-xmm0m32-rax).


## S2-37dp — masked-only Long64 DIVSD XMM0,m64 [RAX]

The interpreter-only schema-v2 profile `s2-long-divsd-memory-rax-v1` admits
exactly legacy `F2 0F 5E 00`, length four, budget one and stop RIP entry+4.
Require Long64, SSE2 (`CPUID.01H:EDX[26]`), CR0.EM=0, CR4.OSFXSR=1,
CR0.TS=0 and present XMM/MXCSR state. Fetch all four bytes before #UD/#NM
gates; adjacent prefix, REX, alternate ModR/M/addressing and VEX/EVEX forms
remain unsupported.

Admit MXCSR supported bits `0xffbf`, reserved bits clear, all six exception
masks set and DAZ=FTZ=0; all four RC modes and every prior sticky history are
allowed. AC=1 refuses before span validation or data access. For AC=0, check
`RAX+7` without overflow and both canonical48 endpoints before exactly one
read8; read failure leaves CPU, SSE, MXCSR, RIP and retirement unchanged.

Divide original XMM0.low64 by the actual memory RHS using
`Binary64::divide_raw_result` with MXCSR RC. Classify original NaNs and invalid
0/0 or infinity/infinity before finite nonzero divided by zero; ZE excludes
infinity/zero and NaN operands. DE applies only to a subnormal input when no
higher-priority IE/ZE applies. Generate OE/UE/PE from the binary64 result and
WPR tininess-after-rounding; merge IE/DE/ZE/OE/UE/PE into prior sticky flags.
Success writes only XMM0.low64, preserving XMM0.high64, other XMM registers and

closed. No physical x86 acceptance is claimed.

The Type 3 note on Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A p. 3-274 describes VEX-encoded
forms and does not modify this legacy DIVSD contract. See [Stage 2 plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-37dp--masked-only-legacy-long64-divsd-xmm0m64-rax), [shared report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-37dp--divsd-xmm0m64-rax), [standalone report](../reports/S2_37DP_DIVSD_MEMORY.md), and [fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-37dp--divsd-xmm0m64-rax). ## S2-37dt — masked-only Long64 DIVPS XMM0,m128 [RAX]

The local profile accepts only legacy `0F 5E 00`, with Long64, SSE bit 25,
CR0.EM=0, CR4.OSFXSR=1 and CR0.TS=0. It fetches the complete three-byte
encoding before #UD/#NM gates; missing SSE, EM or OSFXSR produces #UD before
TS produces #NM. Only the interpreter admits this form. Other encodings,
unmasked/#XM behavior, JIT/native/C ABI/generic/fragment paths are unsupported.

MXCSR must contain only supported bits in `0xffbf`, have all six exception
masks set, and have DAZ, FTZ and reserved bits clear. Every RC mode and old
sticky history is admitted. The memory operand requires 16-byte alignment
regardless of AC. Checked addition and canonical48 checks cover the inclusive
`[RAX,RAX+15]` span before one read16. Alignment, span and read failures leave
architectural state and retirement unchanged.

The four results use old XMM0 lanes as numerators and loaded memory lanes as
denominators through `Binary32::divide_raw_result`. Flags IE/DE/ZE/OE/UE/PE are
merged into the prior MXCSR. Original NaNs suppress same-lane ZE/DE; `0/0` and
`∞/∞` raise IE and return the masked indefinite; finite nonzero or subnormal
numerators over zero raise ZE; infinity over zero returns signed infinity
without ZE. Unrelated state is preserved.

The strict schema/result validator independently recomputes results with the
raw-u32 rational `independent_divps` oracle and the actual memory RHS. The
literal fixture and runner tests exercise 1/3 under every RC and all 64 prior
sticky combinations, NaN/zero/infinity/subnormal classes, overflow, mixed lane
flags, exact encoding and gates, alignment, canonical spans, read rollback,
tampering and backend denial. No physical x86 acceptance or complete unmasked
exception behavior is claimed. Sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A DIVPS pp.
3-270–3-272 and Table 2-19; Vol. 1 §§4.9.1.4–.6, 11.5.2–11.5.3 and DAZ/FTZ;
Vol. 3A Event 19/Table 7-8; Intel Floating-Point Reference Sheet v2.13. The
Type 2 note on p. 3-272 applies to VEX forms, not this legacy SSE encoding.

See [Stage 2 plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-37dt--masked-only-legacy-long64-divps-xmm0m128-rax), [shared report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-37dt--divps-xmm0m128-rax), [standalone report](../reports/S2_37DT_DIVPS_MEMORY.md), and [fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-37dt--divps-xmm0m128-rax).

## S2-37dx — masked-only legacy Long64 DIVPD XMM0,m128 [RAX]

The local strict schema-v2 profile `s2-long-divpd-memory-rax-v1` admits only

selected through a dedicated memory operation and runner path; the existing
register-pair DIVPD selector is unchanged. Require Long64, SSE2
(`CPUID.01H:EDX[26]`), CR0.EM=0, CR4.OSFXSR=1 and CR0.TS=0. Fetch all four
bytes before gates; missing SSE2, EM or OSFXSR raises #UD before TS raises #NM.

native, C ABI, generic and fragment execution remain closed.

span before exactly one atomic read16. Alignment, endpoint, and memory errors

## S2-38q — exact MINPD memory unmasked IM/DM

The interpreter-only schema-v2 profile admits only exact Long64
`66 0F 5D 00` (`MINPD XMM0,m128 [RAX]`), one executable code mapping, budget
one, and stop RIP `entry+4`. It has its own immutable controls and remains
distinct from masked S2-37db memory MINPD, unmasked S2-38i register MINPD, and
S2-38p MAXSD memory. Fetch all four bytes before rejecting any non-exact form;
then missing SSE2, CR0.EM=1, or CR4.OSFXSR=0 raises #UD before CR0.TS=1 raises
#NM. XMM/MXCSR state must be present.

MXCSR must use supported bits `0xffbf`, have reserved bits clear, DAZ=FTZ=0,
and all exception masks except IM and DM set. IM, DM, RC, and prior sticky
history are variable. RAX must be 16-byte aligned regardless of RFLAGS.AC;
AC=0 and AC=1 both admit an aligned address. Misalignment or an invalid
canonical48 inclusive span `[RAX,RAX+15]` raises #GP(0) without a memory
callback. A valid span is followed by exactly one all-or-error `read16`;
alignment, span, and read faults precede floating-point classification and
preserve CPU, XMM, MXCSR, RIP, memory and retirement.

Both old XMM0 lanes and the loaded 128-bit operand are snapshotted. Each lane
uses binary64 MINPD raw source-2 selection: numerical minimum, with either NaN,
equal values, and signed-zero ties selecting raw RHS bits. Raw IE and DE are
classified across both lanes before commit. If a newly raised event is
unmasked, all raw IE/DE events are ORed into MXCSR sticky state, one #XM or
arithmetic #UD is reported according to OSXMMEXCPT, the complete XMM0 and RIP
are preserved, and retirement is zero. When no event is unmasked, IE suppresses
DE only in its own lane; then the complete XMM0, sticky status and RIP commit
atomically. JIT/native/C ABI/generic/fragment execution remains closed.

The schema oracle must use independent raw-bit integer classification and
ordering. Verification covers the lane event product, source/lane permutations,
payload/tie cases, all RC and prior-sticky histories, AC=0/1 aligned access,
fault precedence and callback counts, backend/result tampering, and literal
interpreter fixtures. This is local interpreter evidence; it makes no physical
x86 acceptance claim. Integrated verification passed: od-isa 1,912, od-testkit
455, od-runner 125 unit + 526 fixture, and od-x86-runner 8 library + 4 binary
tests; workspace check, formatting, layout, diff check, and Graphify passed.
Sol/high review is clean. See the [implementation report](../reports/S2_38Q_MINPD_MEMORY_UNMASKED.md)
and [plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-38q--exact-long64-minpd-xmm0m128-rax-with-unmasked-imdm-exits).

## S2-38am — exact SUBPS memory profile with unmasked exceptions

Add immutable schema-v2 interpreter-only profile
`s2-long-subps-memory-unmasked-rax-v1` for exact Long64 legacy `0F 5C 00`
(`SUBPS XMM0,m128 [RAX]`), separate
`subps_memory_rax_unmasked_controls`, one executable mapping, one read-only
m128 mapping, budget one and stop RIP=entry+3. Require SSE bit 25; preserve
masked-memory S2-37dr and register SUBPS behavior. Fetch all three bytes and
check exact form before feature/CR0.EM/CR4.OSFXSR `#UD`, then CR0.TS `#NM`, at
CPL0–3. Noncanonical instruction-fetch byte spans fault `#GP(0)` before those
gates. Require supported MXCSR bits `0xffbf`, reserved bits clear, DAZ=FTZ=0
and OM=UM=1; allow all RC, IM/DM/ZM/PM and prior sticky histories.

The m128 operand requires 16-byte alignment regardless of RFLAGS.AC.
Misaligned RAX returns `#GP(0)` with no data callback for AC=0 and AC=1. After
alignment, check overflow and both canonical48 endpoints of `[RAX,RAX+15]`,
then exactly one read16. Noncanonical fetch, data span or read failure preserves
state and retirement.

Subtract each of four memory lanes from the pre-execution XMM0 lane using the
existing raw SUBPS operation and an independent integer-only raw-u32 oracle
over the actual memory RHS. Classify original operands before changing the RHS
sign: if both operands are NaNs, select the first original source (XMM0); if
only one is NaN, select it. Quiet the selected value only when it is SNaN and
preserve its original sign/payload; any SNaN raises IE, while QNaN alone does
not. A NaN suppresses DE only in its own lane. Same-sign infinities raise IE
and produce the masked negative indefinite; opposite-sign infinities produce
the valid signed infinity. Other subnormal operands contribute lane-local DE,
including when the other operand is infinite.

Aggregate IE|DE across all lanes before checking IM/DM. If any applicable
pre-event is unmasked, commit all applicable new IE/DE flags and suppress every
later OE/UE/PE plus the full XMM destination, RIP and retirement. Otherwise
compute every lane using MXCSR.RC, merge post-status and apply PM atomically;
unmasked PE also suppresses the entire destination, RIP and retirement. WPR
tininess-after-rounding applies; exact subnormal outputs add no UE/PE, and no
inexact-tiny case is required for same-format subtraction. OSXMMEXCPT=1 delivers
`#XM` vector 19; zero delivers SIMD-generated `#UD` vector 6; neither has an
error code. Old sticky bits alone do not fault. Success updates XMM0, applicable
MXCSR status, RIP and retirement, preserving RFLAGS and unrelated state.

Exercise actual interpreter results against the independent actual-memory-RHS
oracle. Cross six lane-event representatives (exact cancellation, SNaN/IE,
subnormal/DE, halfway/PE, normal-minus-minsub/DE+PE, overflow/OE+PE) over
`6^4` lane combinations and all 16 IM/DM/ZM/PM settings × both OSXMMEXCPT
mappings: 41,472 executions at fixed RC/sticky state. Add 48 selected
cross-lane/boundary vectors across all RC, 64 prior sticky histories, masks and
both delivery mappings: 393,216 additional executions. Cover signed QNaN/SNaN
positions and payloads, NaN+subnormal, infinity signs, signed zeros, exact tiny,
halfway/adjacent values, cancellation, exponent gaps, overflow and midpoint,
IE/DE/PE cross-lane aggregation and lane permutations. Verify full-state
suppression, fetch/form/gates/CPL, AC-independent alignment, canonical spans,
one-read rollback, strict schema, fixtures, result/status/control/exception
tampering, masked-profile permissions and backend denial. Sources: Intel SDM
Rev. 093 Vol. 2B SUBPS pp. 4-690–4-692; Vol. 2A §2.5.2/Table 2-19 p. 2-27;
Vol. 1 §4.8.3.5/Table 4-8, §§4.9.2 and 11.5.3.1–3; Vol. 3A Event 19/Table
7-8. Native/JIT/C ABI/generic/fragment routes and physical x86 acceptance
remain closed.

retirement. Otherwise compute both lanes with MXCSR.RC, merge post-status and
apply PM atomically; an unmasked PE suppresses the whole destination, RIP and
retirement. WPR tininess-after-rounding applies; exact subnormal results do not
generate UE/PE. OSXMMEXCPT=1 delivers arithmetic exceptions as `#XM` vector 19;
zero delivers SIMD-generated `#UD` vector 6; neither has an error code. Old
sticky bits alone do not fault. Success updates both XMM0 lanes, applicable
MXCSR status, RIP and retirement, preserving RFLAGS and unrelated state.

Exercise actual interpreter results against an independent raw-u64 oracle with
the actual memory RHS. Cross six lane representatives (neutral, IE, DE-only,
PE-only, DE+PE, OE+PE) over `6^2` lane combinations and all 16 IM/DM/ZM/PM
settings × both OSXMMEXCPT mappings. Add mixed-lane boundary vectors across
all RC, 64 prior sticky histories, masks and both delivery mappings: IE+DE in
different lanes, pre-event suppressing PE/OE in another lane, masked DE then
unmasked PE, lane permutations, signed SNaN/QNaN positions, exact tiny,
cancellation, halfway, exponent gap and overflow midpoint. Same-format
addition has no inexact-tiny result requirement. Verify full-state/no-partial
writes, gates/fetch/CPL, alignment at AC=0/1, canonical code/data spans and
rollback, callback counts, strict schema, fixtures, status/result/control/
exception tampering, old masked permissions and backend denial. Sources: Intel
SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A ADDPD pp. 3-16–3-18, §2.5.2/Table 2-19;
Vol. 1 §§4.9.1.4–.6, 4.9.2, 11.5.1–11.5.3; Vol. 3A Event 19/Table 7-8.
Native/JIT/C ABI/generic/fragment routes and physical x86 acceptance remain
closed.

## S2-38ao — exact MULPS memory profile with unmasked exceptions

Prepare a distinct immutable schema-v2 interpreter-only profile
`s2-long-mulps-memory-unmasked-rax-v1` for exact Long64 legacy `0F 59 00`
(`MULPS XMM0,m128 [RAX]`), with dedicated
`mulps_memory_rax_unmasked_controls`, one executable region, one read-only m128
region at RAX, budget one and stop RIP=entry+3. Require SSE
(`CPUID.01H:EDX[25]`). Preserve masked-memory S2-37ds, register MULPS and the
scalar S2-38ag profile. Fetch the full three-byte instruction and verify its
exact form before SSE/CR0.EM/CR4.OSFXSR `#UD`, then CR0.TS `#NM`, at CPL0–3;
noncanonical fetch span faults `#GP(0)` before those gates. Reject all other
prefix, REX, ModR/M/addressing, VEX/EVEX and register forms.

Require supported MXCSR bits `0xffbf`, reserved bits clear, DAZ=FTZ=0,
OM=UM=1, and admit all RC values, IM/DM/ZM/PM settings and six prior sticky
histories. RAX must be 16-byte aligned regardless of RFLAGS.AC; a misaligned
operand faults `#GP(0)` without a data callback at AC=0 or 1. Check the
canonical48 span `[RAX,RAX+15]` and address overflow before exactly one atomic
read16. Fetch, gate, alignment, span and read failures preserve architectural
state and retirement.

Compute all four lanes from pre-execution XMM0 and the actual memory RHS with
MXCSR.RC. Use an independent integer-only raw-u32 oracle that does not call the
production multiply helper or host floating point. If both inputs are NaNs,
select original XMM0; otherwise select the sole NaN, quieting a selected SNaN
while preserving its sign and payload. Any SNaN and `0×∞` raise IE; a QNaN
alone does not. NaN suppresses DE only in its lane; other non-NaN subnormal
operands contribute DE. Aggregate lane IE/DE before masks. An unmasked pre-event commits applicable
new pre-event sticky bits and suppresses all post-event OE/UE/PE, every XMM0
lane, RIP and retirement. Otherwise compute every product using rounding after
the exact product, aggregate post-status, and apply PE atomically; an unmasked
PE commits applicable post-event flags while suppressing the entire XMM0
write, RIP and retirement. OM and UM remain masked. Under WPR, round the exact
product to p=24 precision with an unbounded exponent before classifying
underflow: UE requires a tiny WPR result and an inexact destination-format
result. An exactly representable destination-format tiny result does not raise
UE. Cover an inexact destination result whose WPR result is tiny and which
rounds to the minimum-normal encoding (`0x00800000 × 0x3f7fffff` under RN), as
well as the exact boundary case; final encoded bits alone do not classify
tininess. Masked overflow/underflow and
inexactness follow the profile's RC and WPR rules. When OSXMMEXCPT=1, unmasked SIMD arithmetic
exceptions deliver `#XM` vector 19; when clear they deliver SIMD-generated
`#UD` vector 6, without an error code. Old sticky bits alone do not fault.
Success writes all four XMM0 lanes and applicable MXCSR status and advances RIP
by three; preserve RFLAGS and unrelated state. JIT/native/C ABI/generic/fragment
routes and physical x86 acceptance remain closed.

Require an actual-interpreter matrix against the independent memory-RHS oracle.
Cross seven lane representatives (neutral, IE, DE-only, PE-only, DE+PE,
OE+PE, UE+PE) over `7^4 × 16` IM/DM/ZM/PM settings ×2 OSXMMEXCPT mappings
(76,832 executions at fixed RC and prior status). Add mixed-lane/boundary
vectors across every RC, 64 prior sticky histories, all masks and both
deliveries, including masked UE+PE followed by unmasked PE, pre-event IE/DE
suppressing later UE/PE in another lane, exact/inexact tiny, half-minsub,
rounding-to-min-normal, overflow, NaN signs/positions, zero-times-infinity,
signed zero/infinity, and lane permutations. Verify fetch/gates/CPL, alignment
at AC=0/1, canonical spans, callback counts, read rollback, full-state and
retirement suppression, immutable schema/result/control/exception checks,
literal fixtures, preservation of old profiles and backend denial. Sources:
Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2B MULPS pp. 4-145–4-147; Vol. 2A §2.5.2/Table 2-19;
Vol. 1 §4.8.3.5/Table 4-8, §§4.9.1.4–.6 and 4.9.2, §11.5.2.5 and
§§11.5.3.1–.3; Vol. 3A Event 19/Table 7-8.

## S2-38aq — exact DIVPS memory profile with unmasked exceptions

Reserve immutable schema-v2 interpreter-only profile s2-long-divps-memory-unmasked-rax-v1 for exact Long64 0F 5E 00 (DIVPS XMM0,m128 [RAX]). Its separate divps_memory_rax_unmasked_controls object has exactly five immutable booleans: sse_available, cr0_em, cr0_ts, cr4_osfxsr, cr4_osxmmexcpt; result snapshots echo the object exactly. Reject missing, unknown, cross-profile, or mismatched control fields. Fix one executable mapping, one read-only m128 mapping at RAX, budget one, stop RIP entry+3, and require SSE CPUID bit 25. Preserve S2-37dt masked memory and S2-37aw register profile fields and permissions.

Fetch all three bytes and check exact legacy form before SSE/CR0.EM/CR4.OSFXSR #UD, then CR0.TS #NM, at CPL0–3. Instruction-fetch span #GP(0) precedes those gates. Reject other prefixes, REX, ModR/M/addressing, VEX/EVEX and register forms. MXCSR supported mask is 0xffbf, reserved bits clear, DAZ=FTZ=0 and OM=UM=1; admit every RC, IM/DM/ZM/PM setting and old sticky history.

RAX must be 16-byte aligned regardless of AC; misalignment is #GP(0) without a data callback at AC=0 or 1. Check overflow and both canonical48 endpoints of [RAX,RAX+15], then exactly one read16. Fetch, gate, alignment, span and read failures preserve full CPU state and retirement. Compute four binary32 quotients from old XMM0 and actual memory RHS. An independent integer-only raw-u32 rational oracle derives expected lanes/status from memory bytes, never host FP or production arithmetic.

Preserve established DIVPS NaN source selection and quiet a selected SNaN without losing its sign/payload. Any original SNaN raises IE, even if an original QNaN is selected; QNaN alone does not raise IE. 0/0 and infinity/infinity raise IE and, when masked, return the architectural QNaN indefinite. Finite nonzero divided by signed zero, including a subnormal numerator with DAZ disabled, raises ZE; infinity/zero does not. A NaN in a lane suppresses same-lane ZE and DE; other subnormal operands are lane-local DE candidates. Resolve each lane's pre-computation candidates with Intel priority IE, then ZE, then DE, respecting QNaN precedence over lower-priority same-lane events; then OR surviving IE/ZE/DE candidates across lanes. If any aggregated pre-event is unmasked, commit all applicable aggregate pre-event flags and suppress post-computation OE/UE/PE, all XMM0 updates, RIP and retirement. If aggregated pre-events are masked, continue to post-computation handling.

Use MXCSR.RC. Under WPR, round at destination precision with unbounded exponent before classifying tininess. With UM masked, an exact tiny result does not set UE; an inexact tiny result sets UE+PE. Cover half-minsub and rounding around minimum-normal. Overflow produces OE+PE; OM is masked. Unmasked PE commits applicable post-event status but suppresses the full XMM0 write, RIP and retirement. Prior sticky bits alone do not fault. OSXMMEXCPT=1 delivers unmasked arithmetic as #XM vector 19; otherwise SIMD-generated #UD vector 6; neither has an error code. Success writes all four lanes, applicable MXCSR status, RIP entry+3 and one retirement while preserving RFLAGS and unrelated state. Native/JIT/C ABI/generic/fragment paths and physical x86 acceptance remain closed.

Acceptance covers signed SNaN in each source position; QNaN with zero/subnormal counterpart; 0/0, infinity/infinity, finite/subnormal nonzero over signed zero, infinity/zero, zero/subnormal and infinity/subnormal; exact/inexact quotients including 1/3; exact/inexact tiny, half-minsub, min-normal rounding, large exponent gaps, overflow+PE; and cross-lane aggregation/suppression for masked and unmasked IE/ZE/DE. Cross all RC, 64 prior sticky histories, 16 IM/DM/ZM/PM combinations and both OSXMMEXCPT mappings in actual interpreter/oracle-backed coverage. Require literal success, IE, ZE, DE, PE, UE+PE and fetch/gate/alignment/span/read-fault fixtures; verify memory-source sensitivity, atomic state/retirement, control/result/status/exception tampering, old-profile permissions and backend denial. Intel SDM Rev. 093: Vol. 2A DIVPS pp. 3-270–3-272, §2.5.2/Table 2-19 p. 2-27; Vol. 1 §§4.9.1–4.9.3, §11.5.2.3–.6, §§11.5.3.1–.3, Table 4-12. This host-side interpreter scope has passed its independent Sol/high review; no physical x86 acceptance is implied.

## S2-38as — exact CVTSS2SI m32 memory profile with unmasked exceptions

The implemented bounded interpreter profile uses a separate immutable
schema-v2 profile
`s2-long-cvtss2si-r32-memory-unmasked-rax-v1` for exact legacy Long64 bytes
`F3 0F 2D 00` (`CVTSS2SI EAX,dword ptr [RAX]`). Preserve masked profile
S2-37ch unchanged. The profile-specific
`cvtss2si_r32_memory_unmasked_controls` input and result echo contain exactly
the immutable booleans `sse_available`, `cr0_em`, `cr0_ts`, `cr4_osfxsr`, and
`cr4_osxmmexcpt`; reject absent, unknown, cross-profile, or mismatched values.
Require SSE CPUID bit 25. Require supported MXCSR mask `0xffbf`, reserved
bits clear, and DAZ=0. Permit all exception-mask bits, all four RC modes, all 64
prior status histories, and either FTZ value; FTZ is irrelevant to this
conversion. The core oracle matrix crosses the four IM/PM combinations.
Additionally sample DM/OM/UM/ZM both set and clear, proving they cannot cause
conversion events and are preserved along with all unrelated supported MXCSR
controls and old status except newly raised IE/PE.

Admit local RFLAGS.AC=0 only. Instruction-fetch span failure precedes feature
gates; within this profile SSE/EM/OSFXSR `#UD` and TS `#NM` precede AC refusal.
Only after successful fetch and gates does AC=1 produce local `Unsupported`,
before a data span check/read or CPU mutation. For AC=0, capture the original
RAX as the address, validate canonical48 `[RAX,RAX+3]`, and perform exactly
one little-endian read4 before committing state. Fetch, gate, span, and read
failures preserve full architectural state, including RAX, RIP, MXCSR and
retirement. Apply the bounded S2-37ch CPL policy without claiming universal
exception priority beyond these defined profile cases. No x87 state is
accessed or modified.

Round the raw binary32 source using MXCSR.RC before checking signed-i32 range.
Invalid input, including infinity or NaN, returns the integer-indefinite bit
pattern `0x80000000` when masked and raises IE; it does not also raise PE.
Valid inexact conversion raises PE. Subnormal inputs do not raise DE and FTZ
does not alter their conversion. The valid exact `-2^31` result aliases the
invalid-indefinite bits but raises no IE. On unmasked IE or PE, suppress the
EAX write (therefore preserve full RAX), RIP advancement and retirement; commit
the event's MXCSR sticky status before delivering `#XM` vector 19 or
SIMD-generated `#UD` vector 6 according to OSXMMEXCPT. Other incoming MXCSR
status and supported controls remain unchanged.

Acceptance requires an independent integer-only raw-u32 oracle that consumes
the actual memory RHS. Exercise vectors × 4 RC × 64 prior sticky histories × 4
IM/PM combinations × 2 OSXMMEXCPT delivery mappings in actual-interpreter
coverage. Include exact and halfway values with neighbors around ±2^31,
positive/negative infinity, QNaN, SNaN, signed zero, normal/subnormal values,
and valid `-2^31` versus invalid-indefinite alias. Check old-RAX alias and
zero-extension on success, one read4, full rollback on read errors, event
status versus destination/RIP/retirement suppression, fetch/gates, strict
schema, tampering, profile isolation and closed backends. Do not use host FP or
production conversion helpers. Sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A `CVTSS2SI`
pp. 3-242–3-243 ([PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199)); Vol. 1 §§11.5.2.2 and 11.5.3.2
([PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671436)); Vol. 3A §§4.1, 5.6–5.7, and Event 17 `#AC`
([PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671190)).
Contract status: implemented for the bounded host-side interpreter profile;
independent Sol/high review is clean. The 34,816-case actual-interpreter
oracle matrix, seven literal fixtures, targeted runner regression, schema
negative checks, workspace check, formatting and diff checks passed. The full
`od-runner` suite was stopped on a pre-fix binary and remains incomplete; no
physical x86 acceptance is claimed. See the [Stage 2 implementation
report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-38as--cvtss2si-eax-m32-memory-unmasked-exceptions).

`s2-long-cvtsd2si-r32-memory-unmasked-rax-v1` for exact legacy Long64 bytes
`F2 0F 2D 00` (`CVTSD2SI EAX,qword ptr [RAX]`). Preserve masked profile

`cvtsd2si_r32_memory_unmasked_controls` input and result echo contain exactly
the immutable booleans `sse2_available`, `cr0_em`, `cr0_ts`, `cr4_osfxsr`, and

Additionally sample DM/OM/UM/ZM both set and clear, proving they cannot cause

controls and old status except newly raised IE/PE.

The schema admits AC=1 negative cases, while conversion requires local
RFLAGS.AC=0. First validate the canonical48 four-byte instruction-fetch span
`[RIP,RIP+3]`; a fetch-span `#GP` precedes feature gates. After exact-instruction
fetch, apply the bounded SSE2/EM/OSFXSR `#UD` gates followed by TS `#NM`. AC=1
produces local `Unsupported` only after fetch and prerequisite gates succeed,
before checking the canonical data span, reading source data, or mutating CPU
state. A failing fetch or gate keeps its earlier outcome when AC=1. For AC=0,
capture the original RAX as the address, validate canonical48 `[RAX,RAX+7]`,
and perform exactly one little-endian read8 before committing state. Fetch,
gate, span, and read failures preserve full architectural state, including RAX,
RIP, MXCSR and retirement. Apply the bounded S2-37cg CPL and canonical-memory
policy without claiming universal exception priority. No x87 state is accessed
or modified.

Round the raw binary64 source using MXCSR.RC before checking signed-i32 range.
Invalid input, including infinity or NaN, returns the integer-indefinite bit
pattern `0x80000000` when masked and raises IE; it does not also raise PE.
Valid inexact conversion raises PE. Subnormal inputs do not raise DE and FTZ
does not alter their conversion. The valid exact `-2^31` result aliases the
invalid-indefinite bits but raises no IE. On unmasked IE or PE, suppress the
EAX write (therefore preserve full RAX), RIP advancement and retirement; commit
the event's MXCSR sticky status before delivering `#XM` vector 19 or
SIMD-generated `#UD` vector 6 according to OSXMMEXCPT. Other incoming MXCSR
status and supported controls remain unchanged.

Acceptance requires an independent integer-only raw-u64 oracle that consumes
the actual memory RHS. The completed actual-interpreter matrix uses 35 vectors
× 4 RC × 64 prior sticky histories × 4 IM/PM combinations × 2 OSXMMEXCPT
delivery mappings (71,680 cases), plus 32 focused DM/OM/UM/ZM/FTZ samples.
The vectors include exact and halfway values with neighbors around ±2^31,
positive/negative infinity, QNaN, SNaN, signed zero, normal/subnormal values,
and valid `-2^31` versus invalid-indefinite alias. Eight literal fixtures cover
success at a high old-RAX address and zero-extension, masked IE/PE, unmasked
IE/PE, gate #NM/#UD, and AC refusal. Direct/generated tests check instruction
fetch-span and gate precedence, one read8, full read-error rollback, event
status versus destination/RIP/retirement suppression, strict schema, tampering,
profile isolation, and fragment/C ABI backend denial. Do not use host FP or
production conversion helpers. The focused ISA test passed (1/1), od-testkit
passed (461/461), runner schema/literal/backend suites passed (2/2), actual
interpreter matrix passed (1/1), host fragment/C ABI denial passed (1/1), and
`cargo check --workspace --all-targets --offline`, formatting, and diff checks
passed. The full `od-runner` suite was not run; physical x86 acceptance is not
claimed. Sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A `CVTSD2SI`
pp. 3-232–3-233 ([PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199)); Vol. 1 §§11.5.2.2 and 11.5.3.2
([PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671436)); Vol. 3A §§4.1, 5.6–5.7, and Event 17 `#AC`
([PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671190)).

interpreter profile. See the [Stage 2 result](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-38at--cvtsd2si-eax-m64-memory-unmasked-exceptions) for checks and limits.

## S2-38au — exact CVTTSS2SI m32 memory profile with unmasked exceptions

Reserve a separate immutable schema-v2 interpreter-only profile
`s2-long-cvttss2si-r32-memory-unmasked-rax-v1` for exact legacy Long64 bytes
`F3 0F 2C 00` (`CVTTSS2SI EAX,dword ptr [RAX]`). Preserve masked profile S2-37ci
unchanged. The profile-specific `cvttss2si_r32_memory_unmasked_controls` input and
result echo contain exactly the immutable booleans `sse_available`, `cr0_em`, `cr0_ts`, `cr4_osfxsr`, and `cr4_osxmmexcpt`; reject absent, unknown, cross-profile, or
mismatched values. Require SSE CPUID bit 25. Require supported MXCSR mask `0xffbf`,
reserved bits clear, and DAZ=0. Permit all exception-mask bits, all four RC modes, all
64 prior status histories, and either FTZ value; FTZ is irrelevant to this conversion.
The core oracle matrix crosses the four IM/PM combinations. Additionally sample
DM/OM/UM/ZM both set and clear, proving they cannot cause conversion events and are
preserved along with all unrelated supported MXCSR controls and old status except newly
raised IE/PE.

Apply the bounded S2-37ci instruction-fetch/SSE/EM/OSFXSR/TS/CPL policy: fetch and
recognize the exact instruction before SSE/EM/OSFXSR `#UD`, then TS `#NM`. For
otherwise valid profile controls, local AC=0 permits conversion; AC=1 produces local
`Unsupported` only after fetch and those prerequisite gates succeed, before the
canonical data-span check, data read, or CPU mutation. Thus AC=1 plus a fetch failure
retains that fetch outcome; AC=1 plus a failing SSE/EM/OSFXSR gate gives `#UD`; AC=1
plus TS gives `#NM` when preceding gates pass. With fetch/gates passing, AC=1 plus a
noncanonical data span remains `Unsupported`. These are bounded collision rules, not a
claim of universal exception priority. For AC=0, capture original RAX as the address,
validate canonical48 `[RAX,RAX+3]`, and perform exactly one little-endian read4 before
committing state. Fetch, gate, span, and read failures preserve full architectural
state, including RAX, RIP, MXCSR and retirement. No x87 state is accessed or modified.

Truncate the raw binary32 source toward zero regardless of MXCSR.RC before checking
signed-i32 range. Invalid input, including infinity or NaN, returns the
integer-indefinite bit pattern `0x80000000` when masked and raises IE; it does not also
raise PE. Valid inexact conversion raises PE. Subnormal inputs do not raise DE and FTZ
does not alter their conversion. The valid exact `-2^31` result aliases the
invalid-indefinite bits but raises no IE. On unmasked IE or PE, suppress the EAX write
(therefore preserve full RAX), RIP advancement and retirement; commit the event's MXCSR
sticky status before delivering `#XM` vector 19 or SIMD-generated `#UD` vector 6
according to OSXMMEXCPT. Old sticky bits alone do not cause a new event. Other incoming
MXCSR status and supported controls, including RC, remain unchanged. Preserve XMM, x87,
RFLAGS, non-destination GPRs and source memory.

Acceptance requires an independent integer-only raw-u32 oracle that consumes the actual
memory RHS. Exercise vectors × 4 RC × 64 prior sticky histories × 4 IM/PM combinations ×
2 OSXMMEXCPT delivery mappings in actual-interpreter coverage, proving RC-independent
results and new events. Include exact and fractional values (including halves),
representable neighbors around ±2^31, positive/negative infinity, QNaN, SNaN, signed
zero, normal/subnormal values, and valid `-2^31` versus invalid-indefinite alias. Use
representable binary32 boundary neighbors; fractional tests near ±2^31 must not silently
round to a different input. Check old-RAX alias and zero-extension on success, direct
`GuestMemory` checks for one read4 and full rollback on injected read errors, event
status versus destination/RIP/retirement suppression, fetch/gates, strict schema,
tampering, profile isolation and closed backends. Do not use host FP or production
conversion helpers. Sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A `CVTTSS2SI` pp. 3-255–3-256
([PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199)); Vol. 1 §§11.5.2.2 and
11.5.3.2 ([PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671436)); Vol. 3A §§4.1,
5.6–5.7, and Event 17 `#AC` ([PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671190)).
Contract status: implemented and independently reviewed. Runtime verification is recorded in the
[Stage 2 report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-38au--cvttss2si-eax-m32-memory-unmasked-exceptions); physical x86 acceptance has not been run.

The strict wire schema requires an exact-width readable m32 mapping and cannot encode an
injected source-read failure. Prove read counts and runtime read-error rollback with
direct `GuestMemory` acceptance; reject unreadable/short mappings at schema validation
instead of treating those inputs as runtime fault fixtures. Include the AC=1 collisions
above and aligned/unaligned AC=0 sources with both FTZ values.

See the
[plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-38au--exact-legacy-long64-cvttss2si-eaxdword-ptr-rax-with-unmasked-exceptions)
and
[fixture format](../testing/TEST_CASE_FORMAT.md#s2-38au-cvttss2si-m32-memory-unmasked-profile).

## S2-38av — exact CVTTSD2SI m64 memory profile with unmasked exceptions

Reserve a separate immutable schema-v2 interpreter-only profile
`s2-long-cvttsd2si-r32-memory-unmasked-rax-v1` for exact legacy Long64 bytes
`F2 0F 2C 00` (`CVTTSD2SI EAX,qword ptr [RAX]`). Preserve masked profile S2-37cj
unchanged. The profile-specific `cvttsd2si_r32_memory_unmasked_controls` input and
result echo contain exactly the immutable booleans `sse2_available`, `cr0_em`,
`cr0_ts`, `cr4_osfxsr`, and `cr4_osxmmexcpt`; reject absent, unknown, cross-profile,
or mismatched values. Require SSE2 CPUID bit 26. Require supported MXCSR mask `0xffbf`,
reserved bits clear, and DAZ=0. Permit all exception-mask bits, all four RC modes, all
64 prior status histories, and either FTZ value; FTZ is irrelevant to this conversion.
The core oracle matrix crosses the four IM/PM combinations. Additionally sample
DM/OM/UM/ZM both set and clear, proving they cannot cause conversion events and are
preserved along with all unrelated supported MXCSR controls and old status except newly
raised IE/PE.

Apply the bounded S2-37cj instruction-fetch/SSE2/EM/OSFXSR/TS/CPL policy: fetch and
recognize the exact instruction before SSE2/EM/OSFXSR `#UD`, then TS `#NM`. For
otherwise valid profile controls, local AC=0 permits conversion; AC=1 produces local
`Unsupported` only after fetch and those prerequisite gates succeed, before the
canonical data-span check, data read, or CPU mutation. Thus AC=1 plus a fetch failure
retains that fetch outcome; AC=1 plus a failing SSE2/EM/OSFXSR gate gives `#UD`; AC=1
plus TS gives `#NM` when preceding gates pass. With fetch/gates passing, AC=1 plus a
noncanonical data span remains `Unsupported`. These are bounded collision rules, not a
claim of universal exception priority. For AC=0, capture original RAX as the address,
validate canonical48 `[RAX,RAX+7]`, and perform exactly one little-endian read8 before
committing state. Fetch, gate, span, and read failures preserve full architectural
state, including RAX, RIP, MXCSR and retirement. No x87 state is accessed or modified.

Truncate the raw binary64 source toward zero regardless of MXCSR.RC before checking
signed-i32 range. Thus `-2147483648.75` and `2147483647.75` are valid with PE, while
`-2147483649` and `2147483648` are invalid with IE only. Invalid input, including
infinity or NaN, returns the integer-indefinite bit pattern `0x80000000` when masked and
raises IE; it does not also raise PE. Valid inexact conversion raises PE. Subnormal
inputs do not raise DE and FTZ does not alter their conversion. The valid exact `-2^31`
result aliases the invalid-indefinite bits but raises no IE. On unmasked IE or PE,
suppress the EAX write (therefore preserve full RAX), RIP advancement and retirement;
commit the event's MXCSR sticky status before delivering `#XM` vector 19 or
SIMD-generated `#UD` vector 6 according to OSXMMEXCPT. Old sticky bits alone do not
cause a new event. Other incoming MXCSR status and supported controls, including RC,
remain unchanged. Preserve XMM, x87, RFLAGS, non-destination GPRs and source memory.

Acceptance requires an independent integer-only raw-u64 oracle that consumes the actual
memory RHS. Exercise vectors × 4 RC × 64 prior sticky histories × 4 IM/PM combinations ×
2 OSXMMEXCPT delivery mappings in actual-interpreter coverage, proving RC-independent
results and new events. Include exact and fractional values (including halves),
representable neighbors around ±2^31, positive/negative infinity, QNaN, SNaN, signed
zero, normal/subnormal values, valid `-2^31` versus invalid-indefinite alias, and the
two valid binary64 fractions outside the real-valued i32 interval stated above. Check
old-RAX alias and zero-extension on success, aligned/unaligned AC=0 sources, both FTZ
values, direct `GuestMemory` checks for one read8 and full rollback on injected read
errors, event status versus destination/RIP/retirement suppression, fetch/gates, strict
schema, tampering, profile isolation and closed backends. Do not use host FP or
production conversion helpers. Sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A `CVTTSD2SI` pp.
3-253–3-254 ([PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199)); Vol. 1 §§11.5.2.2
and 11.5.3.2 ([PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671436)); Vol. 3A §§4.1,
5.6–5.7, and Event 17 `#AC` ([PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671190)).

## S2-38aw — exact CVTPS2DQ m128 memory profile with unmasked exceptions

Reserve interpreter-only schema-v2 profile `s2-long-cvtps2dq-memory-unmasked-rax-v1`
for exact legacy Long64 `66 0F 5B 00` (`CVTPS2DQ XMM0,m128 [RAX]`). Preserve masked
S2-37bv and register S2-37af. The separate `cvtps2dq_m128_unmasked_controls` input
and result echo have exactly five immutable booleans: `sse2_available`, `cr0_em`,
`cr0_ts`, `cr4_osfxsr`, `cr4_osxmmexcpt`. Reject absent, unknown, cross-profile or
tampered controls. Require SSE2 bit 26; supported MXCSR mask `0xffbf`, reserved
bits clear and DAZ=0. Permit all exception masks, RC, prior status and FTZ values.

Fetch and recognize all four bytes before bounded prerequisite gates: missing
SSE2, EM=1 or OSFXSR=0 produces `#UD`; TS=1 produces `#NM` after those checks.
Canonical48 instruction span `[RIP,RIP+3]` faults precede those gates in both the
input validator and result oracle. After gates, check the complete canonical48
data span `[RAX,RAX+15]`, then 16-byte alignment, then perform exactly one read16.
Use checked addition for both spans. Misalignment produces `#GP(0)` at every CPL
and AC value; aligned AC=0 and AC=1 are supported. RAX remains unchanged. These
are the inherited bounded S2-37bv collision rules, not a universal exception
priority claim. Fetch/gate/span/alignment/read failures leave all CPU state
unchanged, including XMM0, MXCSR, RIP and retirement; no data read precedes span
and alignment admission. Do not add scalar AC-refusal semantics here.

Interpret the 16 source bytes as four little-endian raw binary32 lanes and round
each using MXCSR.RC before range checking. Invalid (NaN, infinity or out-of-range)
lanes produce integer indefinite `0x80000000` when masked and contribute IE only.
Valid inexact lanes contribute PE; exact `-2^31` produces the same integer bits
without IE. No lane produces DE, including subnormals; FTZ is irrelevant. Aggregate
new invalid conditions before precision conditions across the complete vector:

| New conditions / masks | New MXCSR status | Architectural commit |
|---|---|---|
| Any IE, IM=0 (either PM) | IE only; suppress new PE from every lane | Preserve all XMM0, RIP and retirement; deliver SIMD event |
| IE masked, any PE, PM=0 | IE if present, plus PE | Preserve all XMM0, RIP and retirement; deliver SIMD event |
| No new unmasked IE/PE | IE/PE from the lanes, if any | Write all four result lanes atomically; RIP+4 and retire once |

OR the permitted new status into old MXCSR; never clear old PE when suppressing
new PE. Old sticky flags alone do not cause an event; a newly encountered
condition can cause an event even when its sticky bit was already set. OSXMMEXCPT
selects `#XM`19 or SIMD-generated `#UD`6. SIMD events commit the allowed MXCSR
status while preserving the complete destination and all other CPU state; a
fetch/gate/span/alignment/read fault instead preserves MXCSR too. Source memory,
RAX, other GPRs/XMM registers, RFLAGS and x87 state are preserved in all cases.

Acceptance uses an independent integer-only raw-u32 oracle that reads actual
memory RHS, not XMM0 or production helpers. Require all 81 ordered lane classes
`{exact, IE, PE}^4 × 4 RC × 64 sticky histories × 4 IM/PM × 2 deliveries` =
**165,888 actual-interpreter cases** (matrix test 1/1, 0.44 s); commit
`640a9f0` ensures each case compares full `LongModeState` and source memory.
Numeric vectors and unrelated-mask/FTZ samples are also covered; details are in the
[result report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-38aw--cvtps2dq-xmm0-m128-memory-unmasked-exceptions).
The class split is 1 exact, 15 IE-only, 15 PE-only and 50 mixed. Check
both `[IE, PE, exact, exact]` and `[PE, IE, exact, exact]`, all-lane suppression,
prior PE retention, all six representable binary32 i32-boundary neighbors, ties,
zeros, infinities, QNaN/SNaN and signed subnormal inputs. The matrix must compare
full CPU state, status, events, memory and retirement; snapshots alone do not
prove memory callback counts.

Direct GuestMemory checks must establish one read16 for success and IE/PE events,
zero reads for failed admission, full read-error rollback, aligned AC0/1 at every
CPL, and all 15 misalignments × CPL0–3 × AC0/1 = 120 `#GP(0)` cases. Include
canonical endpoints/overflow and last-valid/first-crossing fetch spans with gate
collisions. Strict schema/result tests cover writable/unreadable/short mapping
rejection, control/result tampering, masked-profile digest preservation and
cross-denial. Exercise real generic/native/JIT/fragment/C ABI entrypoints.

Sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A CVTPS2DQ pp. 3-225–3-227
([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199)); Vol. 1
§§11.5.2.1–2, 11.5.3.1–3 and Table 14-21 p. 14-33
([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671436)); Vol. 3A
§16.1.3/Table 16-1 p. 16-3
([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671190)). The VEX-only
Type 2/Table 2-19 entry is not the legacy SSE alignment contract.
Contract status: implemented; fresh independent Sol/high review of the corrected
full-state matrix is pending. See the
[result report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-38aw--cvtps2dq-xmm0-m128-memory-unmasked-exceptions).
The full `od-runner` suite and physical x86 acceptance were not run. See the
[plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-38aw--exact-legacy-long64-cvtps2dq-xmm0-m128-rax-with-unmasked-exceptions)
and [fixture format](../testing/TEST_CASE_FORMAT.md#s2-38aw-cvtps2dq-m128-memory-unmasked-profile).

## S2-38ax — exact CVTTPS2DQ m128 memory profile with unmasked exceptions

Reserve interpreter-only schema-v2 profile `s2-long-cvttps2dq-memory-unmasked-rax-v1`
for exact legacy Long64 `F3 0F 5B 00` (`CVTTPS2DQ XMM0,m128 [RAX]`). Preserve
masked S2-37bu and register S2-37ag. The separate
`cvttps2dq_m128_unmasked_controls` input/result echo contains exactly the immutable
booleans `sse2_available`, `cr0_em`, `cr0_ts`, `cr4_osfxsr`, `cr4_osxmmexcpt`.
Reject missing, unknown, cross-profile or changed echoes.

All [S2-38aw packed memory, admission, MXCSR, event-commit and isolation rules](#s2-38aw--exact-cvtps2dq-m128-memory-profile-with-unmasked-exceptions)
apply. The arithmetic difference is fixed TowardZero for every lane, independent
of MXCSR.RC; range checking follows truncation and RC remains unchanged. Require
identical results and new IE/PE events across all four RC settings. A valid exact
`-2^31` remains distinct from invalid indefinite by IE; invalid lanes never add
PE themselves. IM=0 plus any IE commits only new IE and suppresses new PE from
all other lanes; IM=1 permits their PE, and PM=0 then suppresses the whole XMM0
write through a precision event. Old status is preserved.

The independent raw-u32 memory-RHS oracle executes the 165,888-case class
matrix. Additional numeric/control cases are separate samples. The exact
16-byte aligned read, CPL×AC
misalignment behavior, admitted aligned AC=1, fetch/gate/span/read rollback and
real backend-denial proof are identical requirements. The wire schema requires
an exact-width readable, nonwritable m128 mapping; runtime injected read-error
rollback belongs to direct GuestMemory tests, not unreadable literal mappings.

Sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A CVTTPS2DQ pp. 3-249–3-251
([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199)); the Vol. 1/3A
sources linked in S2-38aw establish packed exception ordering and alignment.

## S2-38ay — exact CVTPD2DQ m128 memory profile with unmasked exceptions

Implemented in code commit `417334b`; executable evidence is recorded in the
[Stage 2 report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-38ay--cvtpd2dq-m128-memory-unmasked-profile).
Physical x86 acceptance remains open. Build on masked-memory S2-37bx and register-unmasked
S2-37ah. Reserve interpreter-only schema-v2 profile
`s2-long-cvtpd2dq-memory-unmasked-rax-v1` for exact legacy Long64 `F2 0F E6 00`
(`CVTPD2DQ XMM0,m128 [RAX]`), budget one and stop RIP entry+4. The separate
`cvtpd2dq_m128_unmasked_controls` input/result echo contains exactly five
immutable booleans: `sse2_available`, `cr0_em`, `cr0_ts`, `cr4_osfxsr`,
`cr4_osxmmexcpt`. Reject missing/unknown/cross-profile/tampered controls.
Use the established private `Masked`/`Unmasked` execution-profile split and a
separate unmasked public wrapper; preserve the existing masked wrapper,
IM=PM=1 admission, wire shape, digest and fixtures. No public generic numeric
policy, new addressing form, CPUID advertisement, MMU or JIT capability is added.

Fetch and recognize all four bytes, checking canonical48 `[RIP,RIP+3]` with
checked addition, before SSE2 bit 26/EM/OSFXSR `#UD`, then TS `#NM`. After these
bounded prerequisite gates, check the complete canonical48 `[RAX,RAX+15]` with
checked addition, then 16-byte alignment, then perform exactly one read16.
Misalignment produces `#GP(0)` at every CPL0–3 and AC0/1; aligned AC=0 and AC=1
are both admitted. No data callback precedes successful admission. These are
inherited local collision rules, not a universal exception-priority claim.
Fetch/gate/span/alignment/read failures preserve the whole CPU state, including
MXCSR, XMM0, RIP and retirement. RAX and source memory remain unchanged.

Interpret the source as two little-endian raw binary64 lanes. Round each using
MXCSR.RC before checking signed-i32 range. NaN, infinity and rounded out-of-range
values contribute IE only and, when masked, yield indefinite `0x80000000`.
Exact `-2^31` has the same result bits without IE. Valid inexact lanes contribute
PE; invalid lanes do not contribute PE. Supported MXCSR mask is `0xffbf`,
reserved bits clear, DAZ=0; all exception masks, four RC values, all 64 prior
sticky histories and FTZ0/1 are admitted. Nonzero subnormals contribute PE, never
DE; their integer result follows RC. FTZ is irrelevant. x87 is neither gated nor
modified.

| New lane conditions / masks | New status, ORed into old MXCSR | Commit |
|---|---|---|
| Any IE, IM=0 (either PM) | IE only; suppress new PE from the other lane | Preserve all 128 XMM0 bits, RIP and retirement; deliver SIMD event |
| IE masked, any PE, PM=0 | IE if present, plus PE | Preserve all 128 XMM0 bits, RIP and retirement; deliver SIMD event |
| No new unmasked IE/PE | Aggregate lane IE/PE, if any | Write two i32 results in low64, **zero high64**, advance RIP by four and retire once |

Preserve every old sticky flag, including old PE when new PE is suppressed.
Old flags alone do not trigger an event, but a newly encountered condition may
fault even if its status bit was already set. OSXMMEXCPT chooses `#XM`19 or
SIMD-generated `#UD`6. An event commits only the allowed MXCSR status; high64
zeroing must not occur before successful completion. Preserve other GPRs/XMM
registers, RFLAGS, x87 state and source bytes on success and events.

Acceptance requires an independent integer-only raw-u64 oracle reading the
actual memory RHS, with no host FP or production conversion helper. Use an
XMM0 canary distinct from source bytes and with nonzero high64. Run all nine
ordered `{exact, IE, PE}^2` lane distributions ×4 RC ×64 old sticky histories
×4 IM/PM combinations ×2 delivery mappings = **18,432 actual-interpreter cases
per profile**. The nine classes split into 1 exact, 3 IE-only, 3 PE-only and
2 mixed. Every matrix iteration must compare the entire `LongModeState` and
all 16 source bytes, including high64 zeroing versus full destination rollback.
Representative lanes may use `3ff0000000000000` (exact 1), `7ff8000000000042`
(QNaN/IE) and `3ff8000000000000` (1.5/PE). Both `[IE, PE]` and `[PE, IE]`
orders must prove unmasked IE suppression, masked IE|PE aggregation, unmasked
PE destination suppression, old PE preservation and both deliveries.

Additional generated numeric/control cases cover signed zeros, normals, signed
subnormals, infinities, QNaN/SNaN, ties and neighbors around ±0.5/±1.5/±2.5,
exact INT32_MIN/MAX and raw-u64 neighbors around both i32 limits. Binary64
fractions at the limits are real representable inputs: `+2147483647.75`
(`41dffffffff00000`) yields IE for nearest/up and INT32_MAX+PE for down/zero;
`-2147483648.75` (`c1e0000000180000`) yields IE for nearest/down and
INT32_MIN+PE for up/zero. Also cover `+2147483647.5` (`41dfffffffe00000`),
`-2147483648.5` (`c1e0000000100000`), and raw neighbors of `+2147483648`
and `-2147483649`; nearest-even on the negative half tie yields valid
INT32_MIN+PE. These are extra vectors, not part of the class-product count.
Sample DM/OM/UM/ZM each both ways and FTZ0/1, proving no additional event.

Require 15 nonzero alignment offsets ×4 CPL ×2 AC = 120 `#GP(0)` cases with no
data callback, plus separate aligned AC0/1 ×CPL0–3 success/event checks.
Exercise canonical endpoints, checked-add overflow, last-valid instruction RIP
`0x00007ffffffffffc`, first-crossing `0x00007ffffffffffd`, and gate/data-fault
collisions. Direct GuestMemory tests must prove exactly one read16 on success
and IE/PE events, no early data read, and full CPU/memory rollback on an injected
read error. STOP and zero-budget paths preserve state without memory callbacks.
Strict schema/result checks reject tampered controls, destination high64,
status, event, retirement or source memory and prove masked/profile cross-denial.
Exercise actual generic, native, JIT, host fragment and C ABI entrypoints;
unknown CLI engine strings alone do not establish backend denial.

Sources verified against Intel SDM Rev. 093: Vol. 2A CVTPD2DQ pp. 3-214–3-217
(legacy operation p. 3-216), [official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199);
Vol. 1 §§11.5.2.1–2 (pp. 11-14–11-15), §§11.5.3.1–3 (pp. 11-17–11-18),
Table 14-21 (p. 14-33), [official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671436);
Vol. 3A §16.1.3/Table 16-1 (pp. 16-2–16-3),
[official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671190).
The VEX Type 2 exception table is not the legacy SSE alignment contract.
See the [plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-38ay--exact-legacy-long64-cvtpd2dq-xmm0-m128-rax-with-unmasked-exceptions)
and [fixture format](../testing/TEST_CASE_FORMAT.md#s2-38ay-cvtpd2dq-m128-memory-unmasked-profile).

## S2-38ba — exact CVTDQ2PS m128 memory profile with unmasked exceptions

Implemented in code commit `6058525`; the 16,384-case interpreter matrix,
16 literal fixtures and focused schema/fault/backend checks are complete. The
full `od-runner` suite timed out at 110 seconds and physical x86 acceptance was
not performed.
Build on [S2-37bt masked memory](#s2-37bt--bounded-long64-cvtdq2ps-xmm0rax-aligned-m128-memory-profile)
and [S2-37s register-unmasked semantics](#s2-37s--canonical-long64-cvtdq2ps-xmm-register-pairs).
Reserve strict interpreter-only schema-v2 profile
`s2-long-cvtdq2ps-memory-unmasked-rax-v1` for exact legacy Long64 `0F 5B 00`
(`CVTDQ2PS XMM0,m128 [RAX]`), budget one and checked stop RIP entry+3.
The separate `cvtdq2ps_m128_unmasked_controls` input/result echo contains exactly
five immutable booleans: `sse2_available`, `cr0_em`, `cr0_ts`, `cr4_osfxsr`,
`cr4_osxmmexcpt`. Reject absent, unknown, foreign or changed controls. Use the
established private masked/unmasked profile distinction and a dedicated
unmasked wrapper; preserve S2-37bt PM=1 admission, wrapper, wire shape, fixtures
and digests. This adds no generic numeric policy, CPUID advertisement, MMU,
addressing form or backend capability.

STOP and zero budget are checked before instruction fetch. Fetch and recognize
all three bytes, checking canonical48 `[RIP,RIP+2]` with checked addition,
before prerequisite gates: SSE2 bit 26 absent, CR0.EM=1 or CR4.OSFXSR=0 gives
`#UD`6; then CR0.TS=1 gives `#NM`7. Only after those gates check the complete
canonical48 `[RAX,RAX+15]` with checked addition, then 16-byte alignment, then
perform exactly one data read of 16 bytes. All nonzero alignment offsets give
`#GP(0)` irrespective of CPL0–3 and RFLAGS.AC; aligned AC=0 and AC=1 are both
admitted. No data callback precedes admission. These are local collision rules,
not a universal exception-priority claim. Fetch, gate, span, alignment and read
failures preserve the complete CPU state, including MXCSR, XMM0, RIP and
retirement. Source memory is read-only and unchanged throughout.

Interpret the memory RHS as four little-endian signed i32 lanes and convert
each directly to binary32 under MXCSR.RC (nearest-even, down, up or toward-zero).
All i32 values are finite and within binary32 range; only Precision can arise.
No new IE, DE, ZE, OE or UE is generated. Aggregate inexactness across all four
lanes; OR new PE into incoming sticky status without clearing any old flag.
The supported MXCSR mask is `0xffbf`, reserved bits clear and DAZ=0. Admit all
six exception-mask bits, all four RC values, all 64 prior sticky histories and
FTZ0/1; FTZ is irrelevant to this conversion. Pending x87 state neither gates
execution nor changes.

| New condition / PM | Status and delivery | Destination and retirement |
|---|---|---|
| At least one inexact lane, PM=0 | Set sticky PE; `#XM`19 if OSXMMEXCPT=1, otherwise SIMD-generated `#UD`6; no error code | Preserve every XMM0 bit, RIP and retirement |
| At least one inexact lane, PM=1 | Set sticky PE; no event | Commit all four binary32 lanes, advance RIP by three, retire once |
| All four lanes exact, either PM | Preserve MXCSR, including old sticky flags; no event | Commit all four binary32 lanes, advance RIP by three, retire once |

Old PE alone does not trigger an event. A newly inexact lane does trigger an
unmasked event even when PE was already set. Stage all lanes before any XMM0
write; a late inexact lane suppresses the entire destination. Preserve every
GPR, every other XMM register, RFLAGS, x87 state and memory on both success and
SIMD events. A SIMD event commits only new sticky PE; prerequisite `#UD` does
not commit PE and must remain distinguishable from arithmetic `#UD` by state.

Acceptance requires an independent integer-only i32→binary32 oracle consuming
the actual memory RHS, without host FP or production conversion helpers. Use
four-lane XMM0 canaries distinct from memory. Run **16 lane-inexact masks ×4 RC
×64 old sticky histories ×2 PM ×2 OSXMMEXCPT = 16,384 actual-interpreter cases**.
Each iteration compares complete `LongModeState`, exit metadata and all 16
source bytes. Include each-lane-only inexact masks and all-exact old-PE histories.
Additional numeric cases cover zero, ±1, exact powers/multiples representable
above 2^24, signed boundary neighbors around ±2^24, nearest-even ties whose
retained significand is even or odd for both signs, all directed roundings,
significand carry (e.g. 33554431), INT32_MIN and INT32_MAX. Sample each of
IM/DM/ZM/OM/UM and FTZ both ways, proving no additional event or status change.
These extra vectors do not inflate the class-product count.

Require 16 literal success/PE/delivery/gate fixtures as specified in the fixture
format, plus generated runner/direct checks. Exercise all 15 nonzero alignment
offsets ×4 CPL ×2 AC = 120 `#GP(0)` cases with zero data callbacks, and separate
aligned AC0/1 ×CPL0–3 success/event checks. Cover canonical endpoints, checked-add
wrap, three-byte fetch endpoints (last wholly canonical low-half start
`0x00007ffffffffffd`, first crossing start `0x00007ffffffffffe`), fetch/gate/data
span collisions and STOP/zero-budget without callbacks. Direct GuestMemory
tests prove exactly one read16 for success and PE events, no early data read,
and full CPU/source-memory rollback on injected read error. Strict mapping
rejection is not runtime read-error coverage.

Reject tampered controls, destination lanes, MXCSR status, exit/event metadata,
RIP, retirement and source bytes. Prove masked/profile cross-denial and
unchanged masked regressions/digests. Exercise actual generic, native, JIT,
host fragment and C ABI rejection paths; unknown CLI names are insufficient.
Physical x86 acceptance remains open, as do parent S2-37/S2-38 and broad SSE2
readiness.

Sources inherited from S2-37bt/S2-37s: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A CVTDQ2PS
pp. 3-211–3-213 ([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199));
Vol. 1 §§11.5.2.6–11.5.3.2 (Precision/PM), Appendix C §C.4/Table C-4 and
Table 14-21 (legacy alignment),
[official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671436);
Vol. 3A §16.1.3/Table 16-1 (legacy prerequisite gates),
[official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671190).
The VEX-only Type 2 table is not this legacy alignment contract. See the
[plan](../plans/STAGE_2.md#s2-38ba--exact-legacy-long64-cvtdq2ps-xmm0-m128-rax-with-unmasked-exceptions)
and [fixture format](../testing/TEST_CASE_FORMAT.md#s2-38ba-cvtdq2ps-m128-memory-unmasked-profile).

### Paged `LIDT` entry `PagedLidtLong64V1` (S4-18a)

`step_paged_lidt` is a separate exact entry with the bare `0F 01 5C 24 ib`
encoding and existing `load_idtr` semantics. It fixes Long64,
CR0=`0x80010033`, CR4=`0x20`, EFER=`0xd00`, physical36/four-level/4 KiB
paging, and requires `state.idtr == Some(_)`. The source is SS:RSP plus the
signed displacement; the machine adapter admits a complete ten-byte range
inside one guest page, with the complete source span canonical.

To keep the complete instruction fetch within the profile's bounded fetch
page, instruction starts whose page offset is `0xff2` through `0xfff` are
rejected before any fetch. Offset `0xff1` remains admitted and can fetch all
five bytes from the current page.

The entry reuses the existing decoder and pseudo-descriptor loader. It fetches
the complete instruction before operand access, raises `#UD` for exact LOCK
after full fetch, reports fetch faults before operand faults, and raises
`#GP(0)` for CPL1–3 before descriptor access. A halted CPU returns `Halted`
without fetching; a blocking STI shadow is rejected before fetch. Success
changes only IDTR and RIP, retires once, and preserves other CPU state and
RFLAGS definedness. Descriptor-source faults leave CPU state unchanged. The
loaded IDT base is not walked. Other encodings and control states remain
unsupported.

### S4-18d — bounded paged LTR AX state

`LongModeState::tr` carries `TaskRegisterCache` (selector, 64-bit base, limit with the G
bit applied, descriptor access byte and the AVL/G nibble). It is populated only by
`prepare_paged_ltr_commit(..).commit(..)` after the caller has written the busy descriptor
image; `validate_tss_descriptor` is a pure check (CPL0, selector/GDT limit, available 64-bit
TSS, present, canonical base, in that order) that faults with `#GP(0)`, `#GP(selector)` or
`#NP(selector)`. The legacy fragment adapter rejects a present `tr`. No TSS contents,
task switching or stack switching are modelled. See the
[machine contract](MACHINE_CONTRACT.md#paged-ltr-ax-s4-18d).

### S4-18e — bounded paged MOV DS/ES/FS/GS state

`od_isa::execute::step_paged_mov_ds/es/fs/gs` gate the existing GDT segment loaders
(`load_*_gdt_selector`) behind the exact two-byte `MOV Sreg,AX` forms. The hidden `ds_cache`,
`es_cache`, `fs_cache` and `gs_cache` must already be present; the selector, cache (and base for
FS/GS) and RIP change only after the descriptor read and the optional accessed-bit write have
succeeded. See the [machine contract](MACHINE_CONTRACT.md#paged-mov-dsesfsgs-ax-s4-18e).

### Расширение S4-37a6a — RDTSC в paged-пробе через явный источник времени

`od_isa::execute::step_paged_probe_with_rdtsc` расширяет `PagedCpl0ProbeV1` (Long64/CPL0) одной формой:
голый `RDTSC` (`0F 31`, длина 2, без префиксов `66`/REX/`F2`/`F3`). Форма допускается только в базовом
профиле `PagedCpl0ProbeV1` и только если вызывающий передал явный источник времени
`&mut dyn FnMut() -> u64`.

- Источник вызывается ровно один раз на выполненную (retired) инструкцию. Значение: `EAX` = младшие 32 бита,
  `EDX` = старшие 32 бита; обе записи обнуляют старшие половины `RAX`/`RDX`. `RIP` += 2, `RFLAGS`
  не меняются, `instructions_executed` = 1.
- За TSC отвечает источник; инструкция сама время не продвигает и не читает часы напрямую.
- Без источника (`step_paged_probe`, а также stack/CR3/CR0.WP-варианты, которые источник не
  принимают) результат остаётся `Unsupported { opcode: 0x31 }`, состояние и источник не затронуты.
  Формы `66 0F 31`, `REX.W 0F 31`, `F3 0F 31` и `F2 0F 31` тоже остаются `Unsupported` и источник не
  вызывают. LOCK-форма `F0 0F 31` в базовом профиле даёт `#UD`, а не `Unsupported`.
- CPL3-варианты (`step_paged_cpl3_load`/`step_paged_cpl3_mov`) сначала читают трёхбайтный предфильтр:
  на Ring3 первый байт `0x0F` даёт `Unsupported { opcode: 0x0f }`, на Ring0 результат —
  `Rejected(WrongPrivilege)`; до `0F 31` дело не доходит.
- `CR4.TSD` и CPL>0 здесь не моделируются: профиль CPL0-only. `RDTSCP` и `LFENCE` не добавлены.

## Набор CPL0 (S2-45)

`od_isa::execute::Cpl0ProfileSet` и входы `run_with_cpl0_profile_set` /
`run_with_cpl0_profile_set_and_pio` исполняют в одном вызове интерпретатора несколько
принятых профилей Long64/CPL0. Назначение: плата (Linux-профиль, S4-38L3) вызывает один
интерпретатор вместо одного профиля на вызов. Поля набора приватны; старые входы (`run`,
`run_with_cli_profile`, `run_with_cr0_profile`, ...), paged-пробы и их `PagedCpl0ProbeV1`
не меняются, allowlist пробы набором не расширяется (S7-03).

**Политика CR0/CR4.** `ControlRegisterPolicy::Cpl0BaseLong64V1` держит CR0 и CR4 смоделированными
в `LongModeState` без профиля на регистр. Допустимые значения — предикаты
`Cr0Profile::FpInitLong64V1.accepts` и `Cr4Profile::FpInitLong64V1.accepts` (CR0 = `0x8001_0033`
с произвольными EM/TS, CR4 = `0x20` с OSFXSR/OSXMMEXCPT); второго списка значений нет, новых
вариантов `Cr0Profile`/`Cr4Profile` не добавлено. Формы `MOV r64,CRn` / `MOV CRn,r64` для CR0 и
CR4 (`0F 20 C0`, `0F 22 C0`, `0F 20 E0`, `0F 22 E0`) исполняются только внутри политики; запись
значения вне политики — `Unsupported { opcode: 0x22 }` без мутации, `LOCK`-форма — `#UD`.
Значения CR4 Linux (PGE, AM, MCE) в набор не входят.

**Допуск до первого fetch.** Типизированные `Cpl0ProfileSetInputError`, состояние не меняется:
`WrongMode`, `WrongPrivilege` (только Ring0), `InvalidRflagsDefined`, `Cr0Missing` /
`Cr0OutsidePolicy`, `Cr4Missing` / `Cr4OutsidePolicy`, `Cr3NotAdmitted` (CR3 смоделирован без
`with_cpu_owned_cr3`), `Cr3Missing` / `InvalidInitialCr3` (с владением CR3: нет значения или
больше 36 бит), `FpStateNotAdmitted` (x87/SSE смоделированы), `ActivityMissing`, `NotRunning`,
`StiShadowMissing`, `StiShadowActive`, `CliPreconditionFailed` (с CLI: CR0.PE = 0, CR4.PVI = 1
или RFLAGS.VM = 1).

**Выходы** (`Cpl0ProfileSetExit<E>`): `Run(RunExit)` — обычные выходы интерпретатора, в том числе
`Unsupported { opcode }` и `Fault`; `TranslationContextChange(Cr3Write { old_cr3, new_cr3 })` —
`MOV CR3, RAX` (`0F 22 D8`) удалилась, прогон остановлен на следующей границе инструкции до
следующего fetch (приоритет над STOP, запросом остановки и бюджетом на той же границе;
`instructions_executed` считает MOV CR3); `PortIo(E)` — ошибка порта в `IN AL,DX`/`OUT DX,AL`:
инструкция не удалилась, RIP на ней. Вход без порта использует непредставимый тип ошибки `Infallible`.

**Построители.** `with_cli(&CliProfile)` — голый `FA` (PE=1, PVI=0, VM=0); `with_cpuid(&CpuidProfile)`;
`with_rdtsc()` — голый `0F 31` с явным источником (без источника — `Unsupported { 0x31 }`, CR4.TSD
берётся из допущенного CR4, т.е. 0); `with_msr(&MsrProfile)` — ровно один профиль MSR;
`with_halt(&HaltProfile)` — голый `F4` без STI (HLT не может возобновиться сам);
`with_cpu_owned_cr3(MovCr3Long64V1)` — `state.cr3` смоделирован (<= 36 бит), `0F 22 D8` через общий
`commit_mov_cr3`, `LOCK`-формы и прочие недопустимые формы — `#UD`, значение выше 36 бит — `#GP(0)`
без изменения CR3; `with_pio_u8()` — `EC`/`EE`, исполняются только входом
`run_with_cpl0_profile_set_and_pio`, иначе остаются `Unsupported`, порт не вызывается. Без
построителя форма остаётся `Unsupported` (или своим прежним `#UD`).

**Интеграция с платой (S2-45f).** Адаптер плате — crate-internal
`od_machine::paged_memory_adapter::run_cpl0_set_paged_2m_ram` (ничего не экспортируется из
`lib.rs`): одна инструкция на вызов набора (бюджет 1) через `PagedMovMemoryAdapter` с
`large_ram_profile` (RAM only, 4 KiB/2 MiB листья, fetch в пределах 4 KiB страницы RIP, операнды
qword). Адаптер хранит RIP инструкции, поэтому он пересобирается на каждую инструкцию; снимок
`Long64ProbeConfig` пересобирается из `state.cr3` на каждом `TranslationContextChange`: старое
значение обязано совпасть с активным CR3, новое — с `state.cr3`, иначе
`Cr3EffectMismatch`; отказ снимка — `Cr3SnapshotRejected`; любое другое изменение контекста —
`UnexpectedContextChange`. Следующий fetch идёт уже по новому CR3. Удалившийся `MOV CR3`
записывается в отчёт адаптера до любой проверки: `cr3` отчёта становится новым значением, а событие
попадает в `translation_context_changes`, в том числе когда прогон закончился
`Cr3EffectMismatch` или `Cr3SnapshotRejected` (инструкция удалилась и учтена, устарел только
обходчик). Поэтому `cr3()` платы после прогона и `cr3` stop record — CR3 последнего удалившегося
`MOV CR3`, `cr3_changes` его считает, а окно `rip_bytes` читается по актуальному дереву (после
`Cr3SnapshotRejected` окно пусто, а `rip_bytes_error` содержит `InvalidCr3 ...`). Обе ошибки
защитные: из реального прогона набора с `with_cpu_owned_cr3` недостижимы (значение выше 36 бит —
`#GP(0)` до записи CR3, CR0/CR4/EFER не меняются), поэтому проверены на разборе выхода набора
(`paged_memory_adapter::tests::set_loop_*`). Плата с Linux-профилем вызывает адаптер через
`LoadedFirmwareBoard::run_linux_boot_cpl0_set` (`run_linux_direct_board_set`), с теми же квантами и
тиками, что `run_boot`; пути `run_boot` / `run_linux_boot` набор не используют и остаются на базовом
профиле пробы: на нём настоящее ядро по-прежнему останавливается `Unsupported { 0xFC }` на
`0x100_0200`. Состояние, которое отдаёт
загрузчик Linux, содержит загруженные кэши DS/ES, поэтому нулевой `MOV DS, AX` не является
допущенной legacy-загрузкой: до S2-46 `fc fa 31 c0 8e d8 ...` на нём останавливался на `8E` после 3
удалившихся инструкций (с legacy-состоянием без кэшей, инвариант S2-45a, — после 5); начиная с S2-46
нулевые загрузки DS/ES/SS над загруженным кэшем допущены и пролог проходит целиком (6 удалившихся:
cld, cli, xor, DS, ES, SS).

**Dword-чтение через адаптер платы (S4-38L3).** Адаптер набора (`run_cpl0_set_paged_2m_ram`,
поле `cpl0_set_dword_read`) принимает чтения шириной 4 и 8 байт; ширины 1 и 2 по-прежнему
отвергаются (`paged MOV profile does not support read width`); записи узкой ширины — в
следующем абзаце.
`MOV r32, m32` читает ровно 4 байта и обнуляет старшие 32 бита приёмника (zero-extend, без
знакового расширения). Dword целиком внутри 4 KiB страницы (включая последний, `0xFFC`) — один
доступ с теми же A/D-обновлениями и `#PF`, что у qword. Dword, пересекающий границу 4 KiB
(смещения `0xFFD`–`0xFFF`), — типизированный `TrackedAccessError::CrossesPage { width: 4 }` до
обхода таблиц: backend-ошибка адаптера, ничего не удалено, RAX и RIP не меняются (классификация
S4-11 `cross_page_unsupported`, раздвоенного доступа нет). Общие профили paged MOV остаются
qword-only. Настоящее ядро после этого удаляет 22 инструкции и останавливается на `LGDT [RAX]`
(`0F 01 10`, RIP `0x100_0257`).

**Узкие записи через адаптер платы (S4-38L3).** Тот же адаптер набора (поле
`cpl0_set_narrow_write`, `true` только в `run_cpl0_set_paged_2m_ram`) принимает любую запись шириной
1, 2, 4 и 8 байт от инструкций набора: `MOV m, r` (в том числе с REX для `SIL`/`DIL`, например
`40 88 30` — `MOV [RAX], SIL`), `MOV m, imm` (`C6`/`C7`), `SETcc m8`, `STOS` и dword-операции
чтения-изменения-записи (`ADD`/`OR`/`AND m32` и т. п.; байтовые и word-варианты чтения-изменения-
записи отвергаются на чтении, потому что адаптер не принимает чтения шириной 1 и 2). Walker от
ширины не зависит: запись пишет ровно свою ширину одним доступом, без чтения-изменения-записи
окружающего qword, соседние байты не меняются (у dword-RMW запись — ровно 4 байта).
A/D-биты листа (PTE или PDE 2 MiB) — как у qword-записи на той же странице (accessed при обходе,
dirty при записи), `#PF` — точная запись (вектор 14, код ошибки с W-битом, линейный адрес,
RIP на инструкции) до записи данных и без D-бита; A-биты пройденных уровней таблиц коммитятся, как
у qword-записи. Запись word/dword/qword, пересекающая границу 4 KiB,
— типизированный `TrackedAccessError::CrossesPage { width }` до обхода таблиц: backend-ошибка
адаптера, ни байта, ни A/D-бита, RIP не меняется (как для чтения); байтовая запись на `0xFFF`
остаётся внутри страницы. Другие длины источника (например 3) отвергаются
(`paged MOV profile does not support write width`). Общие профили paged MOV
(`step_paged_mov_2m_ram` и остальные) по-прежнему принимают только свою фиксированную ширину:
qword-профили — `paged MOV profile does not support non-qword writes`, dword-store профиль
(`step_paged_mov_dword_store`) — `... non-dword writes`; флаги узкой записи и dword-store профиля
взаимно исключают друг друга. Настоящее ядро после этого проходит
`MOV [RAX], SIL` (`40 88 30`) на `0x206_3a80`, удаляет 118 инструкций и останавливается на
`LIDT [RIP+0x17bbd]` (`0F 01 1D BD 7B 01 00`, RIP `0x206_647c`, `Unsupported { opcode: 0x01 }`).

**Член cpuid на плате и граница расхождения CPUID (S4-38L4).** Набор Linux-платы по умолчанию
(`LinuxCpl0SetMembers::linux_default()`, `--set-cpl0` раннера) — `cli`, `cpu_owned_cr3` и
`cpuid:DiagnosticV1` (`with_cpuid`); `rdtsc`, `msr`, `halt`, `pio_u8` по умолчанию не включены.
С S2-50 в набор по умолчанию входит и `popf_cpl0` (`with_popf_cpl0`, ниже).
`CPUID` с остальными листами (0, `0x8000_0000`, `0x21` и т. д.) обслуживает DiagnosticV1 как раньше
(лист 0: максимум 1 и вендор `OpenDesktop`; `0x8000_0000`: `0x8000_0008`; неизвестные листы — нули).
Оговорка: набор исполняет только голый `0F A2`; `CPUID` с префиксом (`66`/`48`/`F3` и т. д.) и не граничным
листом остаётся `Unsupported { opcode: 0xA2 }` (`66 0F A2` с листом 1 при этом попадает на границу, так как
